  • Each id finds its own stored row when it can. A row with the same text wins, so on a text key 1 finds '1', not '01'. A stored row is matched once, so on a number key toggle('songs', ['1', '01']) detaches song 1 once.
  • detach and updateExistingPivot send every given id. So on a text key, detach('songs', [1, '01']) deletes both rows.
  • sync deletes a stored row only when none of the given ids matches it. So on a text key, sync('songs', [1, '01']) keeps the rows '1' and '01'.
  • A new row is added once for ids that are the same by this rule, and the first id wins. So on a number key attach('songs', [1, '01']) adds one row. On a text key it adds only the row 1.
  • A whole double within ±2^53, like 2.0, is sent as the int 2. Any other double, like 1.5, NaN, infinity or 1e20, throws an ArgumentError.
  • Text ids are sent to the database as they are.

A null id or a model that is not saved is skipped by attach, detach, toggle, syncWithoutDetaching and updateExistingPivot. sync throws an ArgumentError for one, before it changes anything, because it would delete every other link. Each id is used once: [1, 1, '1'] adds one row.

A text key column can compare text without case. This is the default in MySQL and MariaDB, and in SQLite with COLLATE NOCASE. COLLATE NOCASE ignores case only. MariaDB can also ignore end spaces. Dart does not know that. So sync and toggle also ask the database about each text id that Dart did not match. Dox asks the database about all of these ids in one query (one query per 100 ids), with WHERE key = id for each id. When it finds a stored row, that row counts as a match. With a stored 'ABC':

  • sync('songs', ['abc']) keeps the row 'ABC'. It adds no row and deletes nothing.
  • toggle('songs', ['abc']) detaches the row 'ABC'. It adds no row.
  • The delete never removes a row that the database sees as a kept id.
  • detached has only the ids whose row is really gone.

docs.title: attach
docs.text:
Adds a pivot row for each id. The third argument has the pivot values for every new row.

await artist.attach('songs', 1);
await artist.attach('songs', <int>[2, 3], <String, dynamic>{'role': 'singer'});
await artist.attach('songs', <int, Map<String, dynamic>>{
  4: <String, dynamic>{'role': 'writer'},
});

attach does not check for a row that is already there. Use sync or syncWithoutDetaching when the row may be there.

docs.title: detach
docs.text:
Deletes the pivot rows of the ids. With no ids argument, it deletes every pivot row of the model. detach('songs', null) deletes nothing. It returns how many rows it deleted. The songs stay in the song table.

await artist.detach('songs', <int>[1, 2]);
await artist.detach('songs');

docs.title: sync
docs.text:
Makes the pivot rows match the ids.

  • It adds a row for each new id.
  • It deletes the rows of the ids that are not in the list.
  • It sets the pivot values of the rows that are already there, when a value changed. updated has those ids.

It returns a PivotSyncResult with the ids of each change. A number id is an int in the result, also when you gave '3'. A text that is not the plain text of an int, like '03' or '007', stays text.

PivotSyncResult result = await artist.sync('songs', <int>[1, 2, 3]);
print(result.attached); // ids that got a new row
print(result.detached); // ids whose row was deleted
print(result.updated);  // ids whose pivot values changed

syncWithoutDetaching does the same, but it does not delete rows.

await artist.syncWithoutDetaching('songs', <int>[4]);

docs.title: toggle
docs.text:
Adds a row for each id that has none. Deletes the row of each id that has one. It returns a PivotSyncResult with attached and detached.

await artist.toggle('songs', <int>[1, 2]);

docs.title: updateExistingPivot
docs.text:
Sets pivot values on the rows of one id or a list of ids. It returns how many rows changed.

await artist.updateExistingPivot('songs', 1, <String, dynamic>{'role': 'writer'});

docs.title: Filter by it
docs.text:
whereHas() keeps the artists that have a song. It checks the pivot table artist_song for you. It does not load the songs.

List<Artist> artists = await Artist().whereHas('songs', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('title', 'Yesterday');
}).get();

List<Artist> noSongs = await Artist().whereDoesntHave('songs').get();

See Query by relations.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
The examples are for @ManyToMany(Song) in the Artist model.

Option Default Example value What it is pivotTable the two model names in A-Z order, joined with _ artist_song The pivot table. pivotForeignKey {this model}_id artist_id The pivot column that points to this model. pivotRelatedForeignKey {related model}_id song_id The pivot column that points to the related model. localKey the primary key of this model id The column in artist that pivotForeignKey points to. relatedKey the primary key of the related model id The column in song that pivotRelatedForeignKey points to. withPivot none ['role'] Extra pivot columns to read. See Read pivot columns. withTimestamps false true Read and set created_at and updated_at in the pivot table. onQuery none A static function that changes the query. eager false Load the relation on every query.

The defaults use the class names in snake_case, not the table names. So @DoxModel(table: 'artists') does not change them.

  • Artist and Song give artist_song.
  • Blog and Category give blog_category.
  • BlogPost and Tag give blog_post_tag.

docs.title: Set all keys
docs.text:
@ManyToMany(
  Song,
  pivotTable: 'artist_song',
  pivotForeignKey: 'artist_id',
  pivotRelatedForeignKey: 'song_id',
  localKey: 'id',
  relatedKey: 'id',
)
List<Song> songs = <Song>[];

docs.title: onQuery
docs.text:
onQuery is a static function in the same model class. It gets the query of the related model and returns it.

@DoxModel()
class Artist extends ArtistGenerator {
  @ManyToMany(Song, onQuery: onlyPublished)
  List<Song> songs = <Song>[];

  static QueryBuilder<Song> onlyPublished(Song q) {
    return q.where('song.status', 'published');
  }
}

docs.title: In JSON
docs.text:
• A relation with eager: true is always in toJson().
  • A relation loaded with preload is in toJson() of that query.
  • The JSON key is the field name in snake_case: songs.

docs.title: Polymorphic
docs.text:
Use a polymorphic relation when one model can belong to more than one other model.

For example, a comment can belong to a photo or to a video. The comment table does not have a photo_id and a video_id. It has two columns:

  • commentable_id: the id of the photo or the video.
  • commentable_type: the type, like photo or video.

commentable is the morph name. You pick it.

docs.title: Tables
The morph map
docs.text:
The morph map gives each model a type name. The type name is the value in the commentable_type column.

Set it in the setup() of a provider. Dox runs providers in every isolate, before the first request. The map is kept per isolate, so setting it only in main() is not enough. Then the other isolates store the class name, and @MorphTo throws there.

class MorphMapProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Model.morphMap(<String, Model<dynamic> Function()>{
      'photo': Photo.new,
      'video': Video.new,
    });
  }
}

A queue worker or a CLI command that reads these relations must call it too.

  • @MorphTo needs it. It reads the type and makes the model from the map.
  • Without a map, @MorphMany and @MorphOne store the class name, like Photo.
  • Use a morph map in production. The class name changes when you rename the class, or when you build with --obfuscate. Then the old rows do not match.
  • Do not change a type name later. The rows in the table keep the old name.
  • Model.morphMap(map, merge: false) removes the names you set before.

Two helpers read the map:

String type = Model.morphTypeOf(Photo()); // 'photo'
Model<dynamic> model = Model.morphModel('video'); // a new Video()

docs.title: @MorphMany
docs.text:
A photo has many comments. The second argument is the morph name.

lib/app/models/photo/photo.model.dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

import '../comment/comment.model.dart';

part 'photo.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class Photo extends PhotoGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? title;

  @MorphMany(Comment, 'commentable')
  List<Comment> comments = <Comment>[];
}

docs.title: @MorphOne
docs.text:
A photo has one cover image. It works like @MorphMany, but the field is one model.

@MorphOne(Image, 'imageable')
Image? cover;

When there are many rows, it keeps the last row the query returns. Add an orderBy in onQuery to pick the row, like with HasOne.

docs.title: @MorphTo
docs.text:
A comment belongs to a photo or a video. The field type is Model<dynamic>?. The morph name is the field name in snake_case: commentable. The commentable_id and commentable_type columns must be @Column fields, or the relation is always null.

lib/app/models/comment/comment.model.dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'comment.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class Comment extends CommentGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? body;

  @Column()
  int? commentableId;

  @Column()
  String? commentableType;

  @MorphTo()
  Model<dynamic>? commentable;
}

Run dart run build_runner build after you add a relationship.

docs.title: Save a row
docs.text:
There is no associate(). Set the two columns yourself. Use Model.morphTypeOf() for the type, so it is the same as the morph map.

Comment comment = Comment()
  ..body = 'Nice'
  ..commentableId = photo.id
  ..commentableType = Model.morphTypeOf(photo);
await comment.save();

docs.title: Load it
docs.text:
Load it like the other relations: preload, $getRelation, related or eager.

Photo? photo = await Photo().preload('comments').find(1);
print(photo?.comments.length);

List<Comment> comments = await Comment().preload('commentable').get();
for (Comment c in comments) {
  if (c.commentable is Photo) {
    print((c.commentable as Photo).title);
  }
}
  • @MorphMany and @MorphOne run one query for all models. It has where commentable_type = 'photo'.
  • @MorphTo runs one query for each type in the list. A comment with a type that is not in the morph map throws a StateError. A comment with no type, or an empty type '', gets null.
  • related<Photo>('commentable') on one comment gives the query of its photo.

reload() and a preload set the relation fields again, also when there is no related row. See Relationships.

docs.title: Filter by it
docs.text:
whereHas(), whereDoesntHave() and withCount() work with @MorphMany and @MorphOne.

List<Photo> photos = await Photo().whereHas('comments').get();
List<Video> videos = await Video().withCount('comments').get();

They do not work with @MorphTo. It throws an UnsupportedError.

docs.title: @MorphMany and @MorphOne
docs.text:
The examples are for @MorphMany(Comment, 'commentable') in the Photo model.

Option Default Example value What it is name (2nd argument) commentable The morph name. typeColumn {name}_type commentable_type The type column in comment. idColumn {name}_id commentable_id The id column in comment. localKey the primary key of this model id The column in photo that idColumn points to. onQuery none A static function that changes the query. eager false Load the relation on every query.

docs.title: @MorphTo
docs.text: Option Default Example value What it is name the field name in snake_case commentable The morph name. typeColumn {name}_type commentable_type The type column in this table. idColumn {name}_id commentable_id The id column in this table. ownerKey the primary key of the related model id The column in the related table that idColumn points to. onQuery none A static function that changes the query of each type. It runs for every type, so it takes and returns Model<dynamic>. eager false Load the relation on every query.

docs.title: In JSON
docs.text:
• A relation with eager: true is always in toJson().
  • A relation loaded with preload is in toJson() of that query.
  • The JSON key is the field name in snake_case: comments, commentable.

docs.title: HasManyThrough
docs.text:
Use HasManyThrough to read rows that are two steps away. A model in the middle links the two ends. HasOneThrough is the same, but it gives one row.

For example, a country has many users, and a user has many posts. A country has many posts through its users.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text: Table Columns country id, name user id, country_id post id, user_id, title

docs.title: Define it
docs.text:
Add the field to the first model. The through option is the model in the middle.

lib/app/models/country/country.model.dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

import '../post/post.model.dart';
import '../user/user.model.dart';

part 'country.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel()
class Country extends CountryGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? name;

  @HasManyThrough(Post, through: User)
  List<Post> posts = <Post>[];

  @HasOneThrough(Post, through: User, onQuery: newest)
  Post? latestPost;

  static Model<Post> newest(Post q) {
    q.orderBy('post.id');
    return q;
  }
}

With HasOneThrough, when several rows match, the last row of the query wins. So newest orders by post.id from low to high, and the highest id is the last row.

Run dart run build_runner build after you add a relationship.

docs.title: Load it
docs.text:
It loads like the other relations.

Country? country = await Country().preload('posts').find(1);
print(country?.posts.length);

List<Country> countries = await Country().withCount('posts').get();
List<Country> active = await Country().whereHas('posts').get();

preload runs one query for all countries. withCount, whereHas, whereDoesntHave and has work too. See Counting relations and Query by relations.

Rows that are soft deleted are left out, in the middle table and in the far table.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Option Default What it is foreignKey {this model}_id, like country_id The column in the middle table that points to this model. localKey the primary key of this model The column in this table that foreignKey points to. throughForeignKey {middle model}_id, like user_id The column in the far table that points to the middle model. throughLocalKey the primary key of the middle model The column in the middle table that throughForeignKey points to. onQuery none A static function that changes the query. eager false Load the relation on every query. 
@HasManyThrough(
  Post,
  through: User,
  foreignKey: 'home_country_id', // on user, points to the country
  localKey: 'id', // on country
  throughForeignKey: 'author_id', // on post, points to the user
  throughLocalKey: 'id', // on user
)
List<Post> posts = <Post>[];

docs.title: Write the table in a column name
docs.text:
The query joins the two tables. So in onQuery and in a whereHas callback, write the table in front of the column.

List<Country> countries = await Country().whereHas('posts', (QueryBuilder<dynamic> q) {
  q.where('post.title', 'Hello');
}).get();

A column without the table, like title, can be in both tables.

docs.title: Broadcasting
docs.text:
Broadcasting sends server events to browsers and apps over Socket.IO, on public, private and presence channels.

A client subscribes to a channel. Your code sends an event to the channel. Every client in it gets the event. Use it for live pages, like order status, a chat or a list of who is online.

It is part of the dox_socketio package. It is off by default.

docs.title: Turn it on
docs.text:
Do the Socket.IO setup first. Then turn on broadcasting in the config:

lib/config/socketio.dart
SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  broadcasting: true,
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace()],
);

Channel rules are kept per isolate. So add them where every isolate runs them. A provider is a good place:

lib/providers/broadcast_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

class BroadcastProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Broadcast.channel('orders.{id}', (Object? user, String id) {
      return (user as User).id.toString() == id;
    });
  }
}

Run dart run build_runner build, so the generated container finds the provider. Without it, no rule is added, and every private subscribe gets Forbidden.

A client that is not logged in as a socket gets a token from the auth route. Add the route with your own auth middleware:

lib/routes/api.dart
@override
void register() {
  Broadcast.routes(middleware: <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()]); // POST /api/broadcasting/auth
}

The prefix of the router is added to the path. This router has the prefix api, so the path is /api/broadcasting/auth.

The route runs the channel rule with req.auth and answers {"auth": "<token>"}, or 403. Pass path: to use another path. The token is signed with a key made from APP_KEY. It works for one socket, one channel and one minute.

docs.title: Channels
Send an event
docs.text:
An event is a class with the ShouldBroadcast mixin:

class OrderShipped with ShouldBroadcast {
  OrderShipped(this.order);
  final Order order;

  @override
  List<Channel> broadcastOn() => <Channel>[PrivateChannel('orders.${order.id}')];

  @override
  String broadcastAs() => 'order.shipped'; // default: the class name

  @override
  Map<String, Object?> broadcastWith() => <String, Object?>{'id': order.id};
}
  • broadcastOn gives the channels. It is required.
  • broadcastAs gives the event name. The default is the class name.
  • broadcastWith gives the payload. It must be JSON. The default is an empty map.

Send it:

await broadcast(OrderShipped(order));
await Broadcast.event(OrderShipped(order)); // the same

toOthers skips one socket, for example the one that made the change. The client sends its socket id in the X-Socket-ID header. Broadcast.socketId(req) reads it:

await Broadcast.event(OrderShipped(order), toOthers: Broadcast.socketId(req));

Without a Socket.IO server in the process, and with no emitter, Broadcast.event throws a StateError.

docs.title: The client
docs.text:
Use socket.io-client. A public channel needs no token. A subscription belongs to one socket. After a reconnect, the client has a new socket and is in no channel. So subscribe inside the connect handler. It runs again after each reconnect.

import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('https://app.example.com', { transports: ['websocket'] });

socket.on('order.shipped', (channel, payload) => console.log(channel, payload));
socket.on('connect', () => {
  socket.emit('subscribe', { channel: 'news' }, (ack) => console.log(ack));
});

For a private or presence channel, get a token first, then send it in subscribe. A token works for one socket id only. So ask for a new token in the connect handler, after each reconnect too:

socket.on('connect', async () => {
  const res = await fetch('/api/broadcasting/auth', {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json', authorization: `Bearer ${apiToken}` },
    body: JSON.stringify({ socket_id: socket.id, channel_name: 'private-orders.5' }),
  });
  const { auth } = await res.json();
  socket.emit('subscribe', { channel: 'private-orders.5', auth }, (ack) => console.log(ack));
});

A socket that is already logged in with SocketAuth needs no token. The server runs the rule with socket.user.

  • The ack of subscribe and unsubscribe is {ok: true} or {ok: false, error}.
  • Events arrive as (channel, payload), under the name from broadcastAs.
  • socket.emit('unsubscribe', { channel }, ack) leaves the channel.
error Why channel is missing no channel name channel name is too long over Broadcast.maxChannelLength too many channels over Broadcast.maxChannelsPerSocket already subscribing the same channel is still being checked Forbidden the rule refused, or the token is missing, wrong or old unsubscribed an unsubscribe came while it was subscribing presence is not available another server did not answer in time

Send the token as a string in auth, like above. An object of headers is refused with Forbidden.

docs.title: Presence
docs.text:
A presence channel tells its members who else is in it. The client gets three events:

Event Arguments When presence:subscribed (channel, members) to the new socket, with all members presence:joining (channel, member) to the others, when a member joins presence:leaving (channel, member) to the others, when a member leaves

A member is {user_id, user_info}. user_info is the map from the rule.

socket.on('presence:subscribed', (channel, members) => console.log(members));
socket.on('presence:joining', (channel, member) => console.log(member.user_info.name));
socket.on('presence:leaving', (channel, member) => console.log(member.user_id));

A user with two sockets is one member. presence:joining is sent for the first socket, and presence:leaving for the last one. The member list covers all isolates and servers that share the adapter.

docs.title: Queued broadcasting
docs.text:
A queued broadcast goes through your queue. The request does not wait for it.

dox_socketio does not depend on dox_queue. You connect them with a hook and a small job. Follow these steps.

docs.title: 1. Mark the event
docs.text:
Use ShouldBroadcastQueued in place of ShouldBroadcast:

class OrderShipped with ShouldBroadcastQueued {
  OrderShipped(this.order);
  final Order order;

  @override
  List<Channel> broadcastOn() => <Channel>[PrivateChannel('orders.${order.id}')];

  @override
  Map<String, Object?> broadcastWith() => <String, Object?>{'id': order.id};
}

await broadcast(OrderShipped(order)); // goes to the queue

docs.title: 2. Write the job
docs.text:
The worker runs this job. It sends the saved broadcast to the clients:

lib/app/jobs/broadcast.job.dart
import 'package:dox_queue/dox_queue.dart';
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

/// Sends one queued broadcast to the clients.
@Job()
class BroadcastJob extends DoxJob {
  BroadcastJob({required this.payload});

  final Map<String, dynamic> payload;

  @override
  Future<void> handle() async {
    await Broadcast.deliver(BroadcastPayload.fromJson(payload));
  }
}

Run dart run build_runner build. It adds the job to lib/generated/jobs.g.dart. The queue needs this file to save and load the job. See how the queue works. Make sure jobs: jobRegistry is set in your queue config.

docs.title: 3. Set the hook
docs.text:
The hook gets the broadcast and puts it on the queue. Add it to the setup() of the BroadcastProvider from Turn it on, next to the channel rules. Keep the rules:

lib/providers/broadcast_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_queue/dox_queue.dart';
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/models/user/user.model.dart';

import '../app/jobs/broadcast.job.dart';

class BroadcastProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Broadcast.channel('orders.{id}', (Object? user, String id) {
      return (user as User).id.toString() == id;
    });

    // puts ShouldBroadcastQueued events on the queue
    Broadcast.useQueue(queueBroadcast);
  }

  static Future<void> queueBroadcast(BroadcastPayload payload) async {
    await Queue.dispatch(BroadcastJob(payload: payload.toJson()));
  }
}

The payload is JSON: {channels, event, data, except}. except is the toOthers socket id.

docs.title: 4. Use the Redis adapter
docs.text:
The worker is its own process. It starts your providers, so it gets its own Socket.IO server. That server has no clients. So the worker must reach the clients of the web server through Redis.

Set the Redis adapter in SocketIoConfig. The web server and the worker use the same config, so both use the same Redis. A Broadcast.emitter does not help here. The worker has its own Socket.IO server, and Broadcast.deliver sends through that server first.

docs.title: 5. Run the worker
docs.text:
dart run bin/queue.dart

Deploy the worker together with the web app. See run the worker.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• With no hook set (Broadcast.useQueue not called), a ShouldBroadcastQueued event is sent at once, like a normal one. So tests and small apps work without a queue.
  • Normal ShouldBroadcast events never use the hook.
  • Broadcast.deliver throws a StateError when the worker has no way to send. This is when broadcasting is off and there is no Broadcast.emitter.
  • deliver prints a warning once when it sends through an in-memory adapter with no clients. The clients of the web server do not get that broadcast.
  • In tests, Broadcast.fake() keeps queued events too. Check them with fake.assertQueued<OrderShipped>(). fake.delivered holds the payloads that deliver got.

docs.title: Send from a process with no Socket.IO server
docs.text:
A queue worker or a command has no Socket.IO server. Set an emitter, so Broadcast.event can send through Redis:

Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
Broadcast.emitter = SocketIoEmitter(redis);

await Broadcast.event(OrderShipped(order));

The servers must use the Redis adapter. When the emitter is for another namespace than /, use SocketIoEmitter(redis).of('/chat'). With no server and no emitter, Broadcast.event throws a StateError.

To send from a queue job, use queued broadcasting.

docs.title: Whisper
docs.text:
A whisper lets a client send an event to the other members of a private or presence channel. A typical use is "is typing". The server only passes it on.

It is off by default. A whisper lets clients message each other with no code of yours in between. So you choose to allow it:

SocketIoConfig(broadcasting: true, whisper: true);

The client sends client event with {channel, event, data}. The event name must start with client-. The other sockets in the channel get the event with (channel, data):

socket.emit('client event', {
  channel: 'presence-chat.lobby',
  event: 'client-typing',
  data: { name: 'Alice' },
}, (ack) => console.log(ack)); // the ack is optional

socket.on('client-typing', (channel, data) => console.log(channel, data));
  • Only a socket that subscribed to the channel can whisper.
  • Only private and presence channels allow it. A public channel does not.
  • The sender does not get its own whisper. Its other sockets do.
  • It works across isolates and servers with the Redis adapter.
  • A whisper is dropped when its data is bigger than Broadcast.maxWhisperSize. The default is 10 KB of JSON.
  • When a whisper is refused, the ack is {ok: false, error}. The error is, for example, not subscribed or data is too big.
  • With whisper off, a client event is ignored, with no ack.
  • The client- prefix keeps a whisper apart from server events. Do not give a server event (broadcastAs) a name that starts with client-.
  • The event names and the whisper format follow Laravel Echo. So channel.whisper('typing', data) and listenForWhisper('typing', ...) use the same names.
  • Laravel Echo sends auth as an object of headers. This server refuses that. So Echo can not join a private or presence channel on its own. Log the socket in with SocketAuth, or send your own subscribe with the token, as shown in The client. Then whispers work.

docs.title: Limits and settings
docs.text:
Setting Default What it does Broadcast.maxChannelLength 200 the longest channel name a client may subscribe to Broadcast.maxChannelsPerSocket 100 the most channels for one socket Broadcast.tokenLifetime 1 minute how long a token from the auth route works Broadcast.presenceTimeout 2 seconds how long a presence join or leave waits for other servers Broadcast.maxWhisperSize 10 KB the biggest data of a whisper, in bytes of JSON
  • It needs APP_KEY, to sign the tokens.
  • Turn broadcasting on for one namespace only. With two namespaces, both accept subscribe, but Broadcast.event sends only through the last one.
  • A presence subscribe is refused when a server does not answer in time. A leave still sends presence:leaving.
  • Presence joins and leaves of one channel run one after another in each isolate. During a Redis outage, each one waits up to presenceTimeout, so keep it short.
  • When two sockets of one user join or leave at the same moment on two isolates or servers, presence:joining or presence:leaving can be missed or sent twice.
  • A client cannot send events to the other clients of a channel, unless you turn on whispers.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Broadcast.fake() keeps the events and sends nothing:

test('shipping an order broadcasts', () async {
  BroadcastFake fake = Broadcast.fake();

  await shipOrder(order);

  fake.assertBroadcasted<OrderShipped>();
  fake.assertBroadcastedOn<OrderShipped>('private-orders.${order.id}');
  fake.assertBroadcastedTimes<OrderShipped>(1);
});
Method Passes when assertBroadcasted<T>([test]) an event of type T was sent. With test, one of them passes it assertBroadcastedOn<T>(name) T was sent on the channel name, with its private- or presence- prefix assertBroadcastedTimes<T>(n) T was sent exactly n times assertNotBroadcasted<T>() no T was sent assertNothingBroadcasted() no event was sent

A failed assert throws an AssertionError. fake.eventsOf<T>() gives the events, and fake.clear() forgets them. Broadcast.restore() turns the fake off. Broadcast.reset() forgets the rules, the emitter and the fake. Call it in tearDown.

docs.title: Cache
docs.text:
Cache() keeps data that is slow to make, so the next request can read it fast.

It runs on dox_cache, which is built into dox_core.

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text:
Driver Where the data is Shared between isolates Locks file files in a folder (default storage/cache) yes, on the same machine yes, on the same machine memory a map inside the isolate no yes redis a Redis server yes, also between machines yes null nowhere. It stores nothing - no database a table in your database, from dox_cache_database yes, also between machines yes

Many isolates

Dox runs one isolate per CPU core. Each isolate has its own memory store. So a value you put in one isolate is missing in the others. Use redis or database when all isolates and servers must see the same data.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dox add cache

Add --store=redis (or memory, database) to pick the default store. file is the default. It writes lib/config/cache.dart, adds it to lib/config/app.dart and adds the CACHE_STORE key. redis also adds the REDIS_* keys. database also adds dox_cache_database, its provider and the cache table migration. It needs dox add orm first. It never overwrites a file, so it is safe to run twice. A new app already has it. To set it up by hand, follow Config.

docs.title: Config
docs.text:
A new project already has lib/config/cache.dart, with a file store and a memory store. CACHE_STORE in .env picks the default store (file when it is not set). To add a store, edit the file. This example adds a redis store:

lib/config/cache.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: env.cacheStore,
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'redis',
      'host': env.redisHost,
      'port': env.redisPort,
      'prefix': 'app_cache:',
    },
  },
);

Redis needs two keys that a new project does not have yet. Add them to lib/config/env.dart and run dart run build_runner build:

lib/config/env.dart
  String get redisHost => '127.0.0.1';

  int get redisPort => 6379;

lib/config/app.dart already passes it to AppConfig(cache: cache). Each store is made once per isolate, the first time you use it.

docs.title: Store options
docs.text:
Driver Options file path (default storage/cache), prefix memory max_size: the most items. When it is full, the item that was used least recently is removed. No limit by default. Expired items are removed when read, and by a sweep after many writes (at least 1000). Also prefix. redis host (default 127.0.0.1), port (default 6379), username, password, db (default 0), tls (true/false), pool_size (default 10), max_value_bytes (no limit by default), prefix

A redis store with no prefix gets <app name>_cache: from APP_NAME, like my_shop_cache:. So two apps on one Redis do not share keys. The other drivers use dox_cache:. You rarely need pool_size: the cache sends no blocking commands, so each isolate uses about one Redis connection.

docs.title: Encrypt the cache
docs.text:
By default the cache keeps plain JSON. Anyone who can read the cache file or the Redis database can read the values. To hide them, add 'encrypt': true to a file or redis store:

'file': {'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache', 'encrypt': true},
  • It is off by default. A store without the option is not changed.
  • The normal Dox().cache has the encrypter set for you, and values are encrypted with your APP_KEY. A CacheManager you build yourself needs encrypter: (for example const CryptCacheEncrypter()). Old keys in previousKeys can still read old entries.
  • When the key changes, the old entries cannot be read. They count as a miss. The cache then fills again.
  • On a file store, the whole file is encrypted, also the expiry time. Lock files are not encrypted. They hold no values.
  • On a redis store, a plain int stays plain text, so increment and decrement still work. Every other value is encrypted. Tag counters are int values, so they stay plain too. To keep a secret number encrypted, store it as a String.
  • A memory or null store does not encrypt. Its values never leave the process. The option still needs an encrypter, or building the store throws.
  • The option must be true or false. Any other type, like 'true', throws an ArgumentError.
  • Old plain values read as a miss after you turn the option on. The one exception is an int on Redis, which is plain by design and still reads as a value.
  • On a file store, prune deletes files that cannot be decrypted. After a key change with no previous keys, or in a folder that apps with different keys share, prune removes those files.
  • Cache keys and tag names are not encrypted. A value is not tied to its key, so someone who can write to Redis or the cache folder can copy an encrypted value to another key. Encryption protects against reading only.
  • maxValueBytes is checked on the plain JSON size. The stored encrypted text is about a third bigger.

docs.title: Values are JSON
docs.text: A value must be a JSON type: Map, List, String, num, bool or null. A Map comes back as Map<String, dynamic>. A List comes back as List<dynamic>.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
// no duration: the value stays forever
await Cache().put('foo', 'bar');
await Cache().put('foo', 'bar', duration: Duration(minutes: 10));

await Cache().get('foo');             // 'bar', or null when missing
await Cache().get('foo', 'default');  // 'default' when missing
await Cache().has('foo');             // true
await Cache().forget('foo');          // remove one key
await Cache().forever('settings', <String, dynamic>{'theme': 'dark'});
await Cache().flush();                // remove all items of the store

await Cache().putMany(<String, Object?>{'a': 1, 'b': 2}); // many at once
await Cache().many(<String>['a', 'b', 'c']); // {a: 1, b: 2, c: null}

docs.title: remember
docs.text:
remember reads the value from the cache. When it is missing, the function runs and its result is stored. The value is stored as JSON. Return maps, lists, strings and numbers, not models.

List<dynamic> posts = await Cache().remember(
  'posts',
  Duration(minutes: 5),
  () async => (await Post().all()).map((Post p) => p.toJson()).toList(),
);

rememberForever(key, fn) does the same with no expiry.

  • decode: turns the stored JSON back into your type on a hit, like decode: (j) => (j as List).cast<String>(). Without it, use JSON types like List<dynamic>.
  • lock: true lets only one caller on all isolates and servers run the function. The others wait for its value.

flexible(key, fresh, stale, fn) serves the value as it is for fresh. Then, until stale more has passed, it still serves the old value at once and runs fn once in the background:

Map<String, dynamic> stats = await Cache().flexible(
  'stats', Duration(minutes: 1), Duration(minutes: 5), loadStats,
);

After fresh + stale, the value is gone and the next call waits for fn.

Pass null as stale to keep the value until a refresh replaces it. Use it when an old value is better than no value, like rates from a service that can be down. When fn fails, callers still get the last good value:

Map<String, dynamic> rates = await Cache().flexible(
  'rates', Duration(minutes: 10), null, fetchRates,
);

docs.title: getRaw
docs.text:
getRaw gives the stored JSON text as it is. Send it as a response with no decode and no encode:

String? json = await Cache().getRaw('posts');
if (json != null) {
  return response(json).contentType(ContentType.json);
}

A missing key gives null. A stored String comes back as JSON, with its quotes: "bar". The memory driver also keeps JSON text, so get decodes on every hit there too.

docs.title: Another store
docs.text:
store(name) uses a store from the config instead of the default store:

await Cache().store('redis').put('foo', 'bar');
await Cache().store('memory').get('foo');

store() changes the Cache it is called on. The flag cacheCopies makes store() and tags() give a new Cache. See Core flags.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Put items under a tag. Then you can remove only the items of that tag:

await Cache().tag('users').put('u1', 'Ann');
await Cache().tag('users').flush(); // removes only the items of this tag

tags(['a', 'b']) uses many tags.

docs.title: Locks
docs.text:
A lock makes sure only one request (or one server) runs some code at a time. The memory, file and redis stores support locks. The memory lock works inside one isolate only. The file lock works for all isolates on one machine. Use redis when many servers must share the lock.

CacheLock lock = Cache().store('redis').lock('report', Duration(seconds: 30));
if (await lock.get()) {
  try {
    await buildReport();
  } finally {
    await lock.release();
  }
}
  • get() tries once. It is true when you got the lock.
  • block(Duration(seconds: 5)) tries again and again until the time is over. It gives false when the time is over. With the flag CacheFlags(lockThrows: true) it throws LockTimeoutException. See CacheConfig.
  • The lock is freed after its ttl, even if you never call release().
  • block(timeout, callback) runs the callback while it holds the lock, then frees it.
  • forceRelease() frees the lock, whoever holds it.

docs.title: More methods
docs.text:
Method What it does add(key, value, duration:) store only when the key is missing. true when it was stored pull(key) get the value and remove it, in one step increment(key, [by]) / decrement(key, [by]) change an integer. A missing key starts at 0 touch(key, duration:) give a key a new expiry. false when it is missing repository the dox_cache CacheStore, for everything else

See dox_cache for custom drivers.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: To use a memory store in tests, see Testing.

docs.title: Deployment
docs.text:
This page shows how to build a Dox app for production and run it safely.

Never run production with dart run

dart run (and dox serve) uses the JIT compiler. It is made for development. It uses about 25x more memory at start (around 390 MB instead of 16 MB) and starts slower. Always build an AOT binary for production.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
dox build

This makes a build/bundle/ folder:

File What it is build/bundle/bin/server the native binary. No Dart SDK needed to run it build/bundle/bin/queue the queue worker, when bin/queue.dart exists build/bundle/bin/schedule the scheduler, when bin/schedule.dart exists build/bundle/lib/ native libraries from build hooks (eg. SQLite) build/bundle/db/ your db/ folder (migrations, seeders). SQLite database files are left out build/bundle/.env.example copy it to build/bundle/.env, or use env variables

dox build runs build_runner (when your app uses it), then dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build. It builds bin/queue.dart and bin/schedule.dart the same way, when they exist. It exits with code 1 when a step fails, so CI can stop.

Not dart compile exe

dox_orm depends on sqlite3 v3. It bundles SQLite with a build hook. dart compile exe does not run build hooks, so it stops with an error. dart build cli is the same AOT compiler and runs the hooks. Keep bin/ and lib/ together: the binary loads the libraries from ../lib.

Start it:

cd build/bundle
./bin/server

The binary reads .env and db/ from the folder you start it in. A real environment variable wins over the .env file.

A new Dox app runs the migrations in bin/server.dart, before the server starts. So the database is up to date when the first request comes in.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
A new Dox app has this multi-stage Dockerfile. The final image is FROM scratch: only the Dart AOT runtime, the bundle, db/, libgcc_s and an empty /tmp.

FROM dart:stable AS build

# Resolve dependencies first, so this layer is cached.
WORKDIR /app
COPY pubspec.* ./
RUN dart pub get

COPY . .
RUN dart pub get --offline

# The dox CLI. `dox build` runs build_runner, then AOT-compiles
# bin/server.dart, bin/queue.dart and bin/schedule.dart with
# `dart build cli`. It puts all of them in build/bundle/bin, the native
# libraries in build/bundle/lib and the migrations in build/bundle/db.
# The queue worker and the scheduler run as their own processes:
# `/app/bin/queue work` and `/app/bin/schedule work`.
ARG DOX_VERSION=^3.2.0
RUN dart pub global activate dox "$DOX_VERSION"
RUN /root/.pub-cache/bin/dox build

# Lay out the final file tree:
# /app/bin/server, /app/bin/queue, /app/bin/schedule, /app/lib (native
# libraries), /app/db/migration, /app/storage and a writable /tmp
# (uploads bigger than 1 MB are streamed to a temp file).
RUN mkdir -p /out/app/storage /out/tmp \
  && chmod 1777 /out/tmp \
  && cp -r build/bundle/. /out/app/ \
  # the native HTTP server (Rust) needs libgcc_s, which /runtime/ does not have
  && LIBGCC=$(find / -name libgcc_s.so.1 -path '*lib*' | head -n 1) \
  && mkdir -p /out$(dirname $LIBGCC) && cp $LIBGCC /out$LIBGCC

# Minimal serving image: the AOT runtime files from the dart image
# (`/runtime/`) plus our bundle. No Dart SDK, no source code.
FROM scratch
COPY --from=build /runtime/ /
COPY --from=build /out/ /
WORKDIR /app

# Config comes from env variables. The image has no .env file,
# so secrets stay out of it.
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["/app/bin/server"]

The image has no .env file, so secrets stay out of it. Pass config as environment variables:

docker build -t my-app .
docker run -p 3000:3000 --env-file .env -e DB_HOST=... my-app

A new app also has a docker-compose.yml. It runs the app, a queue worker and Postgres, and reads .env with env_file: .env:

docker compose up -d --build

A new .env uses SQLite. The compose services set DB_CONNECTION=postgres and DB_NAME=dox themselves. To use the compose Postgres with dox s, set the same two values in .env. The database port listens on 127.0.0.1 only.

A new app skips the Postgres driver in pubspec.yaml, because it uses SQLite. Remove the dox_postgres_native skip lines before you run the compose app. See Skip unused drivers.

See Docker for a health check in the image.

docs.title: Server, queue worker and scheduler
docs.text:
One image has three binaries. Run each one as its own process:

Process Command web server /app/bin/server (the default CMD) queue worker /app/bin/queue work scheduler /app/bin/schedule work

The image is FROM scratch, so it has no shell. Start the other binaries with --entrypoint:

docker run -d -p 3000:3000 --env-file .env my-app
docker run -d --env-file .env --entrypoint /app/bin/queue my-app work
docker run -d --env-file .env --entrypoint /app/bin/schedule my-app work

In compose, use command: ["/app/bin/queue", "work"]. The worker service of a new app does this.

  • Only the server runs the migrations, when it starts. The worker and the scheduler do not. Start the server first.
  • Without Docker, run ./bin/queue work and ./bin/schedule work in build/bundle, for example as two more systemd services.
  • For a small app, QueueConfig(inProcess: true) runs the jobs inside the server, and ScheduleConfig(inProcess: true) runs the schedule there. Then you need only the server. Heavy jobs slow down requests. See Small apps.

docs.title: HTTPS: put a proxy in front
docs.text:
Dox serves plain HTTP only. Its native server has no TLS.

Run Dox on plain HTTP on a private port. Put Caddy or nginx in front of it. The proxy does TLS, HTTP/2 and gzip.

By default Dox listens on all network interfaces. When the proxy runs on the same machine, set APP_HOST=127.0.0.1. Then the app port can not be reached from outside.

flowchart LR
    C["Client"] -->|HTTPS| X["Caddy or nginx<br>TLS, HTTP/2, gzip, body size limit"]
    X -->|"plain HTTP on 127.0.0.1:3000"| D["Dox binary<br>bin/server, one isolate per core"]
    D -->|"one shared pool"| DB[("Database")]
    M["Migrations<br>bin/server.dart runs them once, before the server starts"] --> DB

Then tell Dox to trust the proxy, so req.ip() and req.scheme() show the real client:

AppConfig(
  /// the proxy's IP, or a range like '10.0.0.0/8', or '172.16.0.0/12' for docker
  trustedProxies: <String>['127.0.0.1', '::1'],
);
  • req.ip() reads X-Forwarded-For. Dox walks the list from the right and skips your proxies, so a fake value from the client is ignored.
  • req.scheme() reads X-Forwarded-Proto (http or https). req.isSecure() is true for https.
  • trustedProxies is empty by default. Then Dox ignores those headers, because any client can send them.
  • ['*'] trusts any direct client. Only use it when the app port is not reachable from outside. With *, req.ip() is the right-most X-Forwarded-For hop, the one your proxy added. If you have two proxies in a row, list their IPs or ranges instead.

docs.title: Caddy
docs.text:
Caddy gets a certificate for you and sets X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto. Websockets work with no extra config.

example.com {
  encode gzip
  reverse_proxy 127.0.0.1:3000
}

docs.title: Nginx
docs.text:
upstream dox {
  server 127.0.0.1:3000;
  keepalive 64;
}

map $http_upgrade $connection_upgrade {
  default upgrade;
  ''      '';
}

server {
  listen 443 ssl http2;
  server_name example.com;

  ssl_certificate     /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/fullchain.pem;
  ssl_certificate_key /etc/letsencrypt/live/example.com/privkey.pem;

  # match maxMultipartSize in AppConfig
  client_max_body_size 100m;

  gzip on;
  gzip_types application/json text/plain text/css application/javascript;

  location / {
    proxy_pass http://dox;
    proxy_http_version 1.1;

    # websocket upgrade
    proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
    proxy_set_header Connection $connection_upgrade;

    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;

    # stream uploads to Dox, do not buffer them in nginx first
    proxy_request_buffering off;
  }
}

server {
  listen 80;
  server_name example.com;
  return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
}

docs.title: Pass the real Host header
docs.text:
Behind a proxy, the proxy must pass the real Host header to Dox, like proxy_set_header Host $host; above. Some checks compare the request with this header:

  • the WebSocket origin check (allowedOrigins on Route.websocket, or AppConfig.webSocketAllowedOrigins): a page of the same host can open a socket.
  • back(): it only goes back to a page of the same host.
  • allowedOrigins of socket.io.

If the proxy sends its own host (like localhost:3000) instead, pages of your site look like another site. Then sockets from your own pages get 403, and back() goes to the fallback.

docs.title: Behind a load balancer
docs.text:
A load balancer keeps idle connections to Dox open, and sends new requests on them. Dox closes a connection with no request for 30 seconds. If the balancer keeps it longer, it may send a request on a connection Dox just closed. Then the client gets 502.

To fix this, set idleTimeout longer than the balancer's idle timeout. AWS ALB keeps idle connections for 60 seconds, so use 65 seconds:

AppConfig(
  // ...
  idleTimeout: Duration(seconds: 65),
)

docs.title: Keep it running
docs.text:
When a worker isolate dies, Dox starts it again. When the main isolate dies, the process exits with a non-zero code (see Isolate). Let a supervisor restart it: restart: unless-stopped in Docker compose, or Restart=always in systemd.

# /etc/systemd/system/dox.service
[Service]
WorkingDirectory=/srv/app/build/bundle
ExecStart=/srv/app/build/bundle/bin/server
EnvironmentFile=/srv/app/build/bundle/.env
Restart=always

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

docs.title: Graceful shutdown
docs.text:
On SIGTERM (docker stop, Kubernetes, Cloud Run, Fly, systemd) or SIGINT (Ctrl+C), Dox stops gracefully, in every isolate:

  1. It stops taking new connections at once.
  2. Open requests can finish. Each keep-alive connection closes after its current answer.
  3. After shutdownTimeout (default 8 seconds), it closes the connections that are still open.
  4. It runs shutdown() of every provider (see Providers). The ORMProvider of a new project closes the database connections here.
  5. It closes the cache stores of Cache(), eg. the Redis connections.
  6. The process exits with code 0.

A second SIGINT or SIGTERM stops the process at once.

Set the timeout in lib/config/app.dart:

AppConfig(
  shutdownTimeout: Duration(seconds: 20),
  ...
)

Keep it shorter than the time your platform waits before it kills the process:

Platform Waits Change it with docker stop 10 seconds docker stop -t 30, or stop_grace_period in compose Kubernetes 30 seconds terminationGracePeriodSeconds Cloud Run 10 seconds can not be changed Fly.io 5 seconds kill_timeout in fly.toml systemd 90 seconds TimeoutStopSec

In code, await Dox().stop() does steps 1 to 5 and does not exit.

docs.title: Many processes or machines
docs.text:
One Dox process already uses every core. You only need more processes to run on more machines, or to restart one process without downtime. Run each one on its own port (or machine) and list them in the proxy:

upstream dox {
  server 10.0.0.11:3000;
  server 10.0.0.12:3000;
  keepalive 64;
}

Socket.IO rooms then need a shared adapter (like Redis), because each process has its own memory.

docs.title: Dox CLI
docs.text:
The dox CLI creates projects and files, runs the dev server, builds for production and runs migrations.

Many make:* commands also answer to a create:* name. Run dox help to see all commands. Run dox help <command> for one command.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
dart pub global activate dox

Add the pub bin folder to your PATH

If your shell can not find dox, add this line to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc, and open a new terminal:

export PATH="$PATH":"$HOME/.pub-cache/bin"

To remove the CLI:

dart pub global deactivate dox

docs.title: All commands
docs.text: Command What it does dox create <name> [--version <v>] create a new project dox serve (or dox s) start the dev server with build_runner watch dox build build the native (AOT) bundle into build/bundle dox build_runner:watch / dox build_runner:build run the code generator dox make:controller <name> [-r] [--api] [--model=<model>] create a controller dox make:middleware <name> create a middleware dox make:dto <name> create a DTO (typed, checked input) dox make:serializer <name> create a serializer dox make:provider <name> create a provider in lib/providers dox make:command <name> create a command in lib/app/commands and add it to the commands list dox make:mail <name> [--no-view] create a mailable in lib/app/mail, and its view unless you pass --no-view dox make:view <name> create a .dox.html view in resources/views dox make:test <name> [--unit] create a test in test/ that uses DoxTestClient, or a plain one with --unit dox route:list [--json] list every route of the app, without starting the server dox make:model <name> [-m] [-c] [-r] [--api] [-f] [-s] [-a] create a model, and with the options its migration, controller, factory and seeder dox make:migration <name> [--sql] create a Dart migration, or a .sql one with --sql dox migration:run (or dox migrate) run new migrations dox migration:rollback [--step=N] [--batch=N] undo the last batch, the last N migrations, or only batch N dox migration:reset undo all migrations dox migration:refresh undo all, then run all again dox migration:fresh (or migrate:fresh) drop all tables, then run all migrations dox migration:status show which migrations ran, and their batch dox make:factory <model> create a model factory in db/factories, see Factories dox make:seeder <name> create a seeder in db/seeders (and bin/seed.dart), see Seeders dox db:seed [--class=<name>] run DatabaseSeeder, or another seeder dox make:job <name> create a queue job in lib/app/jobs (and bin/queue.dart) dox queue:work [--queue=a,b] [--concurrency=N] [--once] [--tries=N] [--timeout=S] [--sleep=S] [--stop-when-empty] [--timeout-grace=S] run the queue worker dox queue:failed list the failed jobs dox queue:retry <id\|all> put a failed job (or all) back on the queue dox queue:forget <id> delete one failed job dox queue:flush delete all failed jobs dox queue:clear [queue] delete the jobs of a queue dox queue:restart stop the running workers after their current jobs dox queue:prune-failed [--hours=N] delete failed jobs older than N hours (default 24) dox queue:table create a migration for the jobs, failed_jobs and job_batches tables (from the dox_queue_database package) dox auth:tokens-table create a migration for the auth_access_tokens table (from the dox_auth package) dox schedule:work run the scheduler and keep it running dox schedule:run run the tasks that are due now, once dox schedule:list list the scheduled tasks dox schedule:test <name> run one scheduled task now dox schedule:clear-cache remove the withoutOverlapping() locks left by a crash dox key:generate [--show] [--force] make a new APP_KEY. --show prints a key and writes nothing. In production it asks first, --force skips dox env:generate make lib/config/env.dart (the typed env class) from .env.example, see Environment Variables dox env:check check the env against lib/config/env.dart. Prints every missing or bad key (exit code 1) dox openapi:generate [dir] run bin/openapi.dart to write openapi.json and openapi.yaml (default storage/openapi). A new project has no bin/openapi.dart yet, see OpenAPI dox update update the CLI dox version (or dox -v) show the CLI version dox help [command] show help

docs.title: Create a project
docs.text:
dox create new_blog
dox create new_blog --version <release tag>

dox create copies the dox-sample template from GitHub. Without --version, it uses the newest template release with the same major version as the CLI.

  • The folder name is the project name in snake case: NewBlog makes new_blog.
  • It makes .env from .env.example, with a new APP_KEY.
  • Then run cd new_blog, dart pub get and dox serve.

docs.title: Run the dev server
docs.text:
dox serve                         # or: dox s
dox s --ignore-build-runner       # do not run build_runner watch

dox serve runs dart run bin/server.dart and restarts it when a .dart file changes. It also runs build_runner watch, so generated files stay up to date.

docs.title: Build for production
docs.text:
dox build
cd build/bundle
./bin/server

See Deployment.

docs.title: Create files
docs.text:
dox make:controller Blog        # lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart
dox make:controller Blog -r     # resource controller
dox make:controller Blog --api  # resource controller without create and edit
dox make:controller Blog --model=Post  # resource controller that uses the Post model
dox make:middleware Auth        # lib/app/http/middleware/auth.middleware.dart
dox make:dto CreateBlog         # lib/app/dtos/create_blog/create_blog.dto.dart
dox make:serializer Blog        # lib/app/serializers/blog.serializer.dart
dox make:provider Cache         # lib/providers/cache_provider.dart
dox make:command send_report    # lib/app/commands/send_report_command.dart, run it with dox app:send-report
dox make:mail Welcome           # lib/app/mail/welcome_mail.dart and resources/views/emails/welcome.dox.html
dox make:mail Invoice --no-view # the mail only, with a plain text body
dox make:view pages/about       # resources/views/pages/about.dox.html
dox make:test Ping              # test/ping_test.dart, starts the app with DoxTestClient
dox make:test Math --unit       # test/math_test.dart, a plain test
dox make:model Blog -m          # lib/app/models/blog/blog.model.dart and a create_blogs_table migration
dox make:model Blog -mcr        # model, migration and a resource controller
dox make:model Blog -a          # model, migration, factory, seeder and a resource controller
dox make:migration create_blogs_table          # .dart file (default)
dox make:migration create_blogs_table --sql    # .sql file
  • -r (or --resource) adds the methods index, create, store, show, edit, update and destroy. --api adds the same methods without create and edit.
  • make:model options: -m migration, -c controller, -r resource controller, --api resource controller without create and edit, -f factory, -s seeder, -a migration, factory, seeder and resource controller. Join them, like -mfs. See CLI reference.
  • dox route:list prints the routes of the app. See dox route:list.
  • Word breaks are kept. BlogPost makes blog_post.controller.dart with the class BlogPostController.
  • After make:controller or make:dto, run dox build_runner:build (or keep dox serve running). See Validation.
  • The table of a model is its name in plural snake case: BlogPost makes blog_posts. The model gets @DoxModel(table: 'blog_posts').

docs.title: Database settings
docs.text:
The migration commands read the database settings from the .env file and the real environment. A real environment variable wins.

.env
# postgres, mysql or sqlite
DB_CONNECTION=postgres
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
# for sqlite: the file path
DB_NAME=postgres
DB_USERNAME=admin
DB_PASSWORD=password
  • DB_CONNECTION defaults to postgres. The default port is 5432 for postgres and 3306 for mysql.
  • DB_DATABASE works too, in place of DB_NAME.
  • DATABASE_URL wins over all the DB_* keys when it is set.
  • Put comments on their own line. A # after a value becomes part of the value.

All keys are in the Env reference.

docs.title: Run and undo migrations
docs.text:
dox migration:run                # or: dox migrate
dox migration:status
dox migration:rollback           # undo the last batch
dox migration:rollback --step=2  # undo the last 2 migrations
dox migration:rollback --batch=3 # undo only batch 3
dox migration:reset              # undo all migrations
dox migration:refresh            # undo all migrations, then run them again
dox migration:fresh              # drop all tables, then run all migrations

migrate:rollback, migrate:reset, migrate:refresh, migrate:fresh and migrate:status also work. Add --seed to migration:run, migration:refresh or migration:fresh to run the seeders after it.

  • A failed migration stops the run, and the CLI exits with code 1.
  • On MySQL, statements like CREATE, ALTER and DROP save right away. So when a migration fails half way, these changes are not undone.

docs.title: Update the CLI
docs.text: dox update installs the newest version with the same major version as your CLI. To pick the version yourself, run the install command again.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text:
Declare your env keys once, in a typed class.

Then env.appPort is an int, your IDE suggests every key, and a missing key stops the app at startup.

docs.title: The typed env class
docs.text:
A new project already has lib/config/env.dart. Its keys are listed in the Env reference. This example shows the kinds of getters you can write:

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'env.g.dart';

enum LogLevel { debug, info, error }

@DoxEnv()
abstract class AppEnv {
  static AppEnv load([EnvReader? reader]) {
    return _$AppEnv.load(reader);
  }

  String get appName;                       // APP_NAME, required
  String get appKey;                        // APP_KEY, required
  int get dbPort => 5432;                   // DB_PORT, default 5432
  bool get appDebug => false;               // APP_DEBUG, default false
  LogLevel get logLevel => LogLevel.info;   // LOG_LEVEL=debug
  Duration get cacheTtl => const Duration(minutes: 5); // CACHE_TTL=5m
  List<String> get corsOrigins => <String>[];          // CORS_ORIGINS=a.com,b.com

  @EnvKey('AWS_BUCKET')
  String? get s3Bucket;                     // optional, null when not set
}

/// The env of the app. Read and checked once, on first use.
final AppEnv env = AppEnv.load();

Run dart run build_runner build after each change to the class. It writes env.g.dart. Then use env anywhere:

import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

DatabaseConfig databaseConfig = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: 'postgres',
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(port: env.dbPort /* int */, ...),
  },
);

docs.title: The rules
docs.text:
• Key: the getter name in UPPER_SNAKE case. appName reads APP_NAME, s3Bucket reads S3_BUCKET. Use @EnvKey('X') for another name.
  • Default: the getter body. It can be any expression, like Platform.numberOfProcessors. It runs only when the key is missing. A default can not read another env getter.
  • Optional: a nullable getter with no body (String? get s3Bucket;). It is null when the key is missing.
  • Required: any other getter with no body. A missing key stops the app.
  • Empty: an empty value (or the text null) counts as missing.

docs.title: Types
docs.text:
Type Value in .env String any text int, double, num 3000, 0.5 bool true/false, 1/0, yes/no, on/off (any case) Uri https://dox.dev Duration a number and a unit: 500ms, 30s, 5m, 2h, 1d. A plain number is seconds: 300 is 5 minutes. an enum the name of a value, any case: debug List<String> comma separated: a, b, c. Empty items are dropped.

Any other type is a build error.

docs.title: Fail fast
docs.text:
AppEnv.load() reads every key one time. Then it checks them all, and throws one EnvException that lists every missing or bad key:

EnvException: the env is not valid
  - APP_KEY is missing
  - DB_PORT must be an int, not "abc"

This happens once, when the app starts. After that, env.dbPort is a plain field read.

docs.title: Where values come from
docs.text:
Dox reads values from these places:

  1. Real environment variables (set in the shell, Docker or systemd).
  2. In tests only: the .env.testing file. See Testing: a test database.
  3. The .env file in the folder where you start the app. It is optional.

The environment wins

A real environment variable wins over the .env file. So you can keep .env for development and use real variables in production.

docs.title: The .env file
docs.text:
.env
APP_NAME=dox
APP_KEY=3f9a1c7e5b2d4f6a8c0e1b3d5f7a9c2e
DB_PORT=5432
  • One KEY=value per line.
  • Quotes around a value are removed. So APP_NAME="My app" gives My app. Use ", ' or `.
  • A = inside the value is kept: TOKEN=a=b gives a=b.
  • A line that starts with # is a comment.
  • A # after a space starts a comment: APP_PORT=3000 # dev gives 3000.
  • A # with no space before it is kept: DB_PASSWORD=abc#123 gives abc#123.
  • A # inside quotes is kept: DB_PASSWORD="abc # 123" gives abc # 123.
  • export KEY=value is read like KEY=value.
  • KEY= (empty) gives the default value, like a key that is not there.

docs.title: Use one value in another
docs.text:
CoreFlags.envExpand is off by default. Turn it on to use ${OTHER} in a value:

.env
HOST=localhost
PORT=3000
APP_URL=http://${HOST}:${PORT}
GREETING="Hello\nWorld"
  • ${OTHER} works in an unquoted value and in a "..." value. It does not work in '...'.
  • Dox looks for a real environment variable first, then for a key above this line. In tests, .env.testing also sees the keys of .env.
  • A name that Dox does not find stays as it is: ${OTHER}.
  • In a "..." value, \n, \t, \", \\ and \$ become a new line, a tab, ", \ and $. Use \$ to write a $ that is not a variable.

The .env file is read before AppConfig exists. So you must set the flag in two places:

  1. Env.flags = flags; at the top of main(), before any env value is read.
  2. The same flags in AppConfig(flags: flags).
lib/config/app.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

const CoreFlags flags = CoreFlags(envExpand: true);

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  appKey: Env.get('APP_KEY', ''),
  flags: flags,
  // ...
);
bin/server.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';

void main() async {
  Env.flags = flags;
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);
  await Dox().startServer();
}

my_app is the name in your pubspec.yaml.

A test does not run bin/server.dart. So set Env.flags = flags; at the top of the main() of each test file too, before the app or the client starts:

test/http_test.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/testing.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';
import 'package:test/test.dart';

void main() {
  Env.flags = flags;
  late DoxTestClient client;

  setUpAll(() async {
    client = await DoxTestClient.start(appConfig);
  });
  // ...
}

Without it, ${OTHER} stays as written in the test, and Dox prints the warning.

The server isolates follow the main isolate. You set nothing for them. When the flag is on in AppConfig but .env was read without it, Dox prints a warning at start, once in each isolate.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
dox env:generate   # make lib/config/env.dart from .env.example
dox env:check      # load the env and print every missing or bad key

dox env:generate reads .env.example:

  • digits become an int with that default: APP_PORT=3000 gives int get appPort => 3000;
  • true/false become a bool with that default
  • an empty value becomes an optional String?
  • any other value becomes a required String. The example value is never a default, so a secret in the example can not leak into the code.
  • # comment lines above a key become its doc comment

It does not overwrite an existing lib/config/env.dart. Run dox build_runner:build after it.

dox env:check exits with code 1 when a key is missing or bad. Use it in CI or before a deploy.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text: To pass your own values in a test, see Testing.

docs.title: Env.get: the low-level way
docs.text:
Env.get() reads one key by name. Use it for a key you only know at run time. For normal config, use the typed class.

Env.get<String>('APP_KEY');             // '' when missing
Env.get('APP_KEY', 'default_value');
Env.get<int>('APP_PORT', 3000);
Env.get<bool>('SOCKETIO_ENABLED', false); // true, 1, yes, on
Env.get<String?>('AWS_BUCKET');          // null when it is not set

A missing or empty key gives the default. With no default:

  • String gives an empty string ''. It is never the text "null".
  • String? and dynamic give null. With no type, like Env.get('KEY'), the type is dynamic, so you get null.
  • int, num, double and bool throw an ArgumentError with the key name. A value that is not a number throws too.

Env.get() looks up and converts the value on every call. Do not call it on a hot path.

APP_KEY

When APP_KEY is missing, not 32 characters, or a public sample key, Dox().startServer() stops with an error. When APP_ENV is development, local, test or testing, it only logs a warning. Make a key with dox key:generate.

docs.title: File Storage
docs.text:
Storage() saves and reads files on a disk: the local folder, AWS S3 (and R2, MinIO, Spaces), or memory.

It is in the dox_storage package. A new project already has it.

import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';

Route.post('/avatar', (DoxRequest req) async {
  RequestFile file = req.input('avatar');
  String path = await Storage().putFile('avatars', file);
  return <String, String>{'path': path}; // /avatars/<uuid>.png
});

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dox add storage

It writes lib/config/storage.dart, the provider, the storage folder and the STORAGE_DISK=local key. It never overwrites a file, so it is safe to run twice. Add --disk=s3 to also add an s3 disk and the AWS_* keys. STORAGE_DISK stays local, so the app starts before you fill in the keys. Fill them in, then set STORAGE_DISK=s3. To set it up by hand, follow Config.

docs.title: Config
docs.text:
A new project already has lib/config/storage.dart, with one local disk in the storage folder. STORAGE_DISK in .env picks the default disk. To add disks, edit the file. This example adds a url to the local disk, an s3 disk and a memory disk:

lib/config/storage.dart
import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

StorageConfig storageConfig = StorageConfig(
  defaultDisk: env.storageDisk,
  disks: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'local': <String, dynamic>{
      'driver': 'local',
      'root': 'storage',
      'url': 'https://app.test/files', // for signedUrl(); url() gives /storage/<path> without it
    },

    /// only when AWS_BUCKET is set
    if (env.awsBucket != null)
      's3': <String, dynamic>{
        'driver': 's3',
        'bucket': env.awsBucket,
        'region': env.awsDefaultRegion,
        'key': env.awsAccessKeyId,
        'secret': env.awsSecretAccessKey,
        'endpoint': env.awsEndpoint, // R2, MinIO, Spaces
      },
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory'},
  },
);

A local disk writes a file in place by default. To write to a temp file and rename it when the write is done, add 'atomic_writes': true to the disk. A failed or stopped upload then never leaves a partial file, and the old file stays. It is off by default. The rename makes a new file. So the folder must be writable, the file gets the default mode and the owner of the app, a hard link keeps the old content, and a symlink is replaced.

'local': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage', 'atomic_writes': true},

A local disk has no per-file access rules by default. setVisibility() does nothing there, and getVisibility() gives the disk visibility. To make visibility the file mode, add 'permissions': true. It is off by default. Then setVisibility() runs chmod and getVisibility() reads the mode of the file. The modes are: public file 0644, private file 0600, public folder 0755, private folder 0700. To change them, give a map with a file and a dir key. Each has a public and a private mode. A mode that is not there keeps its default. A key that is not one of these is ignored. Each mode must be an int from 0 to 0x1ff (0777). A string like '0644', a negative number or a bigger number throws ArgumentError when the disk is made. Dart has no octal numbers, so write the modes in hex. 0x1a0 is 0640, 0x1e8 is 0750:

'local': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage', 'permissions': true},
'private': <String, dynamic>{
  'driver': 'local',
  'root': 'storage-private',
  'visibility': 'private',
  'permissions': <String, dynamic>{
    'file': <String, int>{'public': 0x1a4, 'private': 0x1a0},
    'dir': <String, int>{'public': 0x1ed, 'private': 0x1e8},
  },
},

How it works:

  • The mode is set before the content is written. A private file is never readable by others, not even for a moment.
  • A new file gets the visibility of the write, or the disk visibility.
  • An overwrite, append() and prepend() keep the mode the file has, unless the call gives a visibility.
  • A copy() gets the visibility of the call, or else the mode of the source. It is written to a temp file first and then renamed. Listings hide that temp file. A copy onto a symlink replaces the link.
  • A move() keeps the mode, unless the call gives a visibility.
  • Folders that a write creates get the folder mode. Folders that were there before, and the disk root, keep their mode.
  • getVisibility() reads the real mode. The private mode is private. Any other mode is public.
  • getVisibility() and setVisibility() of a symlink throw UnsupportedOperationException.
  • When the chmod fails, a file that the write created is removed.
  • Windows has no chmod. There permissions does nothing.

The s3 disk reads five keys that a new project does not have yet. Add them to lib/config/env.dart and run dart run build_runner build. They are nullable, and the s3 disk is only added when AWS_BUCKET is set. So the app starts without them:

lib/config/env.dart
  String? get awsBucket;

  String get awsDefaultRegion => 'us-east-1';

  String? get awsAccessKeyId;

  String? get awsSecretAccessKey;

  /// R2, MinIO or Spaces. Null for AWS.
  String? get awsEndpoint;

The provider of a new project sets these disks in every isolate. It is in lib/providers/, so the generated container finds it:

lib/providers/storage_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/storage.dart';

class AppStorageProvider extends StorageProvider {
  AppStorageProvider() : super(storageConfig);
}
Driver Options local root (default storage), url, app_key (default: your APP_KEY), visibility, atomic_writes, permissions s3 bucket, region, key, secret, token, endpoint, path_style (MinIO), url (CDN), visibility, acl, batch_delete memory none. For tests

The s3 disk needs bucket, key and secret. When one is missing, the app stops at start with an ArgumentError that names the setting.

docs.title: Functions
docs.text:
// save with a new uuid file name, returns '/images/<uuid>.png'
String path = await Storage().putFile('images', file);  // a RequestFile
Uint8List bytes = Uint8List.fromList(<int>[1, 2, 3]);
String path2 = await Storage().putFile('images', bytes, extension: 'png');
String path3 = await Storage().put('images', bytes, extension: 'png'); // like putFile
String path4 = await Storage().putFileAs('avatars', file, 'user-1.png'); // your own name

// save to this exact path. String, List<int> or Stream<List<int>>
await Storage().put('notes/a.txt', 'hello', exact: true);

Uint8List? found = await Storage().get(path);  // null when missing
bool exists = await Storage().exists(path);           // files only
bool gone = await Storage().missing(path);            // not exists()
bool folder = await Storage().directoryExists('images');
await Storage().delete(path);

await Storage().copy('notes/a.txt', 'backup/a.txt');
await Storage().move('backup/a.txt', 'old/a.txt');

List<String> files = await Storage().files('images');         // direct files only
List<String> all = await Storage().allFiles('images');        // in sub-folders too
List<String> folders = await Storage().directories('images'); // direct sub-folders
await Storage().deleteDirectory('old');                       // the folder and its files

await Storage().setVisibility(path, Visibility.private);
Visibility visibility = await Storage().getVisibility(path);

int size = await Storage().size(path);                 // throws when missing
DateTime changed = await Storage().lastModified(path); // throws when missing

await Storage().append('logs/app.log', 'new line');    // a missing file is made
await Storage().prepend('logs/app.log', 'first line');
await Storage().makeDirectory('reports');              // local disk only

String url = await Storage().url(path);         // /storage/<path> when the disk has no `url`
String signed = await Storage().signedUrl(path, expiresIn: Duration(minutes: 10));
String same = await Storage().temporaryUrl(path); // the same as signedUrl()

// another disk
await Storage().disk('s3').put('reports/2026.pdf', bytes, exact: true);

put() and putFile() make a new uuid name in the folder and return the path. For bytes, they find the extension from the bytes, or you pass extension:. put() with exact: true writes to the exact path, and replaces an old file there. It takes a String, a List<int> or a Stream<List<int>>, and returns the path. putFileAs() uses your name, and replaces an old file with the same name.

files(), allFiles() and directories() give paths that start with /, like putFile(). On S3 and memory disks, a folder is there when a file is under it.

deleteDirectory() deletes a folder and every file in it. A missing folder is not an error. It refuses the root ('' or /) with InvalidKeyException, so a wrong path can not empty the disk. To empty a whole disk on purpose, use Storage().use().deleteAll().

copy() and move() replace an old file at the new path. On S3 the copy runs inside S3, so the bytes do not pass through your app. copy(), move(), getVisibility() and setVisibility() of a missing file answer 404. On a local disk, a copy() or move() of a missing file makes no folders.

On S3, setVisibility() sets the ACL when acl is on (the default). With 'acl': false (R2 and similar), setVisibility() does nothing, and getVisibility() gives the disk visibility, also for a missing file. On a local disk, setVisibility() needs the permissions option, see Config.

On a local disk with no url option, url() gives /storage/<path> (no host). Dox serves it only when you add Storage.route('storage', signed: false). signedUrl() still needs url.

get() gives null for a missing file, but size() and lastModified() throw FileNotFoundException.

append() and prepend() add a new line between the old and the new text, but only when the file is not empty. Change it with separator. They keep the visibility and content type of the file. They read the file and write it back, so two writers at the same time can lose a write.

makeDirectory() makes a folder only on a local disk. On any other disk it does nothing.

exists() finds files only. directoryExists() finds folders. On a local disk it checks the real folder. On S3 and memory disks, a folder exists when a file is under it.

directoryExists('') is always true on every disk: the empty path is the root.

putFile with a RequestFile, on the local disk, moves the upload temp file (with permissions on, it streams it). It does not read it into memory.

An uploaded file can store itself. store gives it a new uuid name, like putFile. storeAs uses your name, like putFileAs, and replaces an old file with the same name. Both take disk::

RequestFile file = req.input('image');
String path = await file.store('images');
String onS3 = await file.store('images', disk: 's3');
String avatar = await file.storeAs('avatars', 'user-1.png');

storeAs and putFileAs use the name as it is. Do not use the file name from the client. Make your own name, like user-1.png.

putFile and file.store() take the extension of an upload from the file name. When the bytes are a known format (png, jpg, pdf, zip, ...) that does not match the name, the extension of the bytes is used. So a png sent as a.html is saved as .png and is never served as a web page.

docs.title: stream and download
docs.text:
Route.get('/photo', (DoxRequest req) {
  return Storage().stream(req.input('path'));    // shown in the browser
});

Route.get('/report', (DoxRequest req) {
  return Storage().disk('s3').download('reports/2024.pdf'); // saved as a file
});

Both read the file as a stream, from any disk, with Content-Length. A big file is never loaded into memory. A missing file answers 404.

download() saves the file with the last part of the path as its name. Pass name: to pick the name:

Route.get('/invoice', (DoxRequest req) {
  return Storage().download('invoices/42.pdf', name: 'Invoice 42.pdf');
});
