dox_core uses dox_cache and exports it. There is nothing to install. To set up the cache config in an app, run dox add cache. A new app already has it. See Cache. With no config, Dox has a file store (the default) and a memory store. Use it with Cache():

await Cache().put('foo', 'bar', duration: Duration(minutes: 10));
String? foo = await Cache().get('foo');

// store JSON values, so a model becomes a map with toJson()
List<dynamic> posts = await Cache().remember(
  'posts',
  Duration(minutes: 5),
  () async => (await Post().all()).map((Post p) => p.toJson()).toList(),
);

The app template has the stores in lib/config/cache.dart. lib/config/app.dart passes them to AppConfig(cache: cache). Change this file to add a store, like Redis:

lib/config/cache.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: env.cacheStore, // CACHE_STORE in .env, default 'file'
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'redis', 'host': '127.0.0.1', 'prefix': 'app_cache:'},
  },
);

Then set CACHE_STORE=redis in .env.

  • Cache().store('memory') uses another store.
  • Dox().cache is the CacheManager of this page. Cache().repository is the CacheStore.
  • The full guide is at Cache.

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text:
Driver What it is Shared between isolates memory a map in this isolate. Fast. Optional LRU size limit No file one JSON file per key in a folder Yes (same machine) redis Redis, with the ioredis package Yes null stores nothing. Use it to turn caching off - database a table in your database, from the dox_cache_database package. See Database store Yes

Warning

Dox runs many isolates. Each isolate has its own memory cache. Use redis when isolates or servers must see the same data.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_cache

import 'package:dox_cache/dox_cache.dart';

Note

dox_core exports CacheConfig, CacheManager, CacheStore and CacheLock from this package. They are the same classes, so importing both packages is fine.

Make a CacheManager with your stores:

CacheManager cache = CacheManager(CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: 'redis',
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 1000},
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},
    'redis': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'redis', 'host': '127.0.0.1', 'prefix': 'app:'},
  },
));

CacheStore store = cache.store();     // the default store
await cache.store('file').get('a');   // a named store
Driver Options every driver driver, prefix (default dox_cache:) memory max_size: the most items. When full, the least recently used item is removed. No limit when not set file path (default storage/cache). Each prefix gets its own sub folder redis host (default 127.0.0.1), port (default 6379), username, password, db, tls, pool_size, max_value_bytes (values bigger than this throw. No limit by default)

pool_size is the most Redis connections one store opens in one isolate (default 10). A store uses about one, so you rarely change it.

docs.title: Basic use
docs.text:
await store.put('a', 1, Duration(minutes: 5));
await store.get('a');               // 1
await store.get('missing', 'none'); // 'none'
await store.has('a');               // true
await store.forget('a');

No ttl means forever

put without a ttl keeps the value forever. A zero or negative ttl removes the key. Cache() in dox_core takes the ttl as a named argument: Cache().put('a', 1, duration: Duration(minutes: 5)).

docs.title: Remember
docs.text:
Get the cached value, or run the function and cache the result.

List<dynamic> posts = await store.remember('posts', Duration(minutes: 10), () async {
  return await loadPostsAsJson();
});

A cached value comes back as JSON. A List is List<dynamic> and a Map is Map<String, dynamic>. So without decode, the type must be a raw JSON type. For other types, pass decode. It turns the cached JSON into your type:

List<String> names = await store.remember<List<String>>(
  'names',
  Duration(minutes: 10),
  loadNames,
  decode: (Object? json) => List<String>.from(json as List<dynamic>),
);
  • Many calls for the same key at the same time run the function once in one isolate. The others wait for the first.
  • With lock: true, callers in other isolates and servers wait too. It uses a cache lock, so the driver must support locks.

docs.title: Flexible
docs.text:
Stale while revalidate. The value is fresh for the first time. After that it is stale for the second time. A stale value is still returned right away, and one caller refreshes it in the background. After both times, the value is gone and the next call waits for the function.

int count = await store.flexible<int>(
  'users',
  Duration(minutes: 5),  // fresh
  Duration(minutes: 10), // stale
  countUsers,
);

It takes decode like remember. The driver must support locks.

docs.title: All methods
docs.text: Method What it does get(key, [default]) the value, or the default when missing or expired. The default can be a function. It runs only on a miss getRaw(key) the stored JSON text, with no decode. Null when missing put(key, value, [ttl]) store it add(key, value, [ttl]) store only when missing. Returns true when stored has(key) true when the value is not null forget(key) remove it. Returns true when it was there flush() remove all items of this store many(keys) / putMany(map, [ttl]) many keys at once increment(key, [by]) / decrement(key, [by]) change a number. A missing key starts at 0. The ttl stays forever(key, value) store without expiry remember(key, ttl, compute, {decode, lock}) see above flexible(key, fresh, stale, compute, {decode}) see above touch(key, ttl) set a new ttl and keep the value. Returns true when the key was there rememberForever(key, compute, {decode, lock}) the same, without expiry pull(key, [default]) get it and remove it, in one atomic step tags([...]) a tagged view lock(name, [ttl, owner]) an atomic lock

docs.title: Values are JSON
docs.text:
Values must be JSON types: Map, List, String, num, bool, null. Other types throw.

  • A Map comes back as Map<String, dynamic>. A List comes back as List<dynamic>.
  • A stored null reads as a miss. has returns false for it.
  • For a model, store model.toJson(), not the model.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
await store.tags(<String>['users']).put('u1', 'Ann');
await store.tags(<String>['users']).flush(); // removes only the 'users' items

Tags work with every driver. Old items are not deleted right away. They are just not found any more, and they go away when their ttl ends.

docs.title: Locks
docs.text:
Only one worker runs the code at a time.

CacheLock lock = store.lock('report', Duration(seconds: 10));
if (await lock.get()) {
  try {
    // only one worker runs this
  } finally {
    await lock.release();
  }
}

bool got = await lock.block(Duration(seconds: 5)); // wait up to 5 seconds
  • get() takes the lock and returns true, or returns false when someone else has it.
  • block(timeout) tries again every 50 ms until it gets the lock or the time is over.
  • The ttl frees the lock by itself if the worker crashes. Without a ttl, the lock stays until release().
  • release() frees the lock only for the owner that took it.
  • block(timeout, callback) runs the callback while it holds the lock, frees the lock and returns the result. It throws LockTimeoutException when the time is over.
  • block(timeout) with no callback gives false when the time is over. With lock.throwOnTimeout = true or the flag CacheFlags(lockThrows: true) it throws LockTimeoutException. See CacheConfig.
  • forceRelease() frees the lock, whoever holds it.
  • memory, file and redis support locks. The memory lock works inside one isolate only. The file lock is a file made with create(exclusive: true). It works for all isolates on one machine. null throws UnsupportedError.

docs.title: Prefix
docs.text:
Every store has a prefix (default dox_cache:). It is added to every key. Use different prefixes when two apps share one Redis database. On Redis, a prefix with no : at the end gets one, so app does not match the keys of app2.

Redis flush

flush deletes only the keys with the prefix. It never runs FLUSHDB. An empty prefix makes flush throw.

docs.title: Encrypt the cache
docs.text:
By default the cache keeps plain JSON. Anyone who can read the cache file or the Redis database can read the values. To hide them, add 'encrypt': true to a file or redis store, and give the config an encrypter. In a Dox app, the normal Dox().cache has the encrypter set for you. A CacheManager you build yourself needs encrypter: (for example const CryptCacheEncrypter()). Without Dox, write your own class:

class MyEncrypter implements CacheEncrypter {
  @override
  String encrypt(String text) => myEncrypt(text);

  @override
  String decrypt(String text) => myDecrypt(text); // throw on bad input
}

CacheConfig(defaultStore: 'file', stores: stores, encrypter: MyEncrypter());

Then turn it on per store:

'file': {'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache', 'encrypt': true},
  • It is off by default. A store without the option is not changed.
  • In a Dox app the values are encrypted with your APP_KEY. Old keys in previousKeys can still read old entries.
  • When the key changes, the old entries cannot be read. They count as a miss. The cache then fills again.
  • A store with 'encrypt': true and no encrypter throws a StateError when it is built, for every store type.
  • On a file store, the whole file is encrypted, also the expiry time. Lock files are not encrypted. They hold no values.
  • On a redis store, a plain int stays plain text, so increment and decrement still work. Every other value is encrypted. Tag counters are int values, so they stay plain too. To keep a secret number encrypted, store it as a String.
  • A memory or null store does not encrypt. Its values never leave the process. The option still needs an encrypter, or building the store throws.
  • The option must be true or false. Any other type, like 'true', throws an ArgumentError.
  • Old plain values read as a miss after you turn the option on. The one exception is an int on Redis, which is plain by design and still reads as a value.
  • On a file store, prune deletes files that cannot be decrypted. After a key change with no previous keys, or in a folder that apps with different keys share, prune removes those files.
  • Cache keys and tag names are not encrypted. A value is not tied to its key, so someone who can write to Redis or the cache folder can copy an encrypted value to another key. Encryption protects against reading only.
  • maxValueBytes is checked on the plain JSON size. The stored encrypted text is about a third bigger.

docs.title: File driver
docs.text:
• Each prefix has its own sub folder inside path. flush deletes only the files of that prefix.
  • add, increment and touch take a file lock on the key, so they are safe across isolates.
  • A read never deletes a file. An expired file stays until it is written again.
  • prune() deletes the expired files. Call it from time to time, eg. in a schedule:
int deleted = await (store.driver as FileDriver).prune();
  • Or set prune_every on the store to run prune() in the background once every that many writes. It is off by default. Each run reads every file of the store, so pick a big number, eg. 1000:
'file': {'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache', 'prune_every': 1000},
  • prune() takes the key lock that add, increment and touch use, so it never deletes their new value. A plain put takes no lock. If a put writes a key at the same moment prune() deletes it, the new value is lost. It is only a cache miss.

docs.title: Database store
docs.text:
The dox_cache_database package keeps the cache in a table of your database. All servers that use the same database share the cache, the locks and the sessions, with no Redis. It works on SQLite, Postgres, MySQL and MariaDB.

Install it and make the table:

dart pub add dox_cache_database
dox cache:table
dox migrate

dox cache:table writes a migration that calls CacheTables.up(schema). Give --table=<name> for another table name.

Register the driver when the app starts, before the first use of the store:

import 'package:dox_cache_database/dox_cache_database.dart';

Dox().cache.extend(
  'database',
  DatabaseCacheDriverFactory(Dox().cache.config.encrypter),
);

Then add a store to lib/config/cache.dart:

'database': <String, dynamic>{
  'driver': 'database',
  'table': 'cache', // optional, default `cache`
  'connection': 'cache', // optional, default the default connection
  'prefix': 'app:', // optional
  'encrypt': true, // optional
},
  • A full key (the prefix and the key) may have at most 255 characters. A longer key throws an ArgumentError.
  • Cache calls inside an app transaction on the same connection join that transaction. Their writes roll back with it, and other servers do not see a lock until the commit. Give the store its own connection (a second connection with the same database settings) to keep the cache out of app transactions.
  • An expired row reads as a miss, but it stays in the table. Call prune() from time to time, eg. in a schedule:
int deleted = await (store.driver as DatabaseCacheDriver).prune();
  • Expiry times come from the clock of each server. Keep the clocks of your servers in sync.

docs.title: Your own driver
docs.text:
class MyDriverFactory implements CacheDriverFactory {
  @override
  CacheDriver create(Map<String, dynamic> options) {
    return MyDriver(options);
  }
}

cache.extend('mine', MyDriverFactory()); // config: {'driver': 'mine'}
cache.addStore('ready', MemoryDriver()); // or add a ready driver

MyDriver extends CacheDriver. It must implement prefix, get, put, add, increment, forget and flush. Override lock to support locks, and close to close its connections. Override pull to make it atomic, and has and touch to make them faster. The defaults work, but pull is a get and then a forget.

docs.title: Close
docs.text:
cache.close() closes the connections of every store that was built, eg. the Redis connections. Memory, file and null stores have nothing to close. It is safe to call twice. A store used after it is built again.

In a Dox app you do not call it. Dox closes Cache() stores on shutdown, in every isolate, after the open requests are done.

docs.title: MCP server
docs.text:
A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for the Dox framework.

It serves tools to MCP clients (Claude, ChatGPT, IDE agents) over the Streamable HTTP transport, from a normal Dox route.

  • Tool arguments are dox_validation schemas: clients see them as JSON Schema, and every call is checked before your code runs.
  • Session ids are signed with APP_KEY, so a session made on one isolate works on every isolate, and after a restart. No store is needed.
  • Replies are plain JSON. No SSE stream is needed for tools.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dox add mcp

It adds the package, lib/config/mcp.dart with an McpServer, and a sample tool in lib/app/mcp/echo.tool.dart. You add the route and the auth. It never overwrites a file, so it is safe to run twice.

docs.title: Set it up by hand
docs.text: dart pub add dox_mcp

docs.title: Use
docs.text:
Write a tool:

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_mcp/dox_mcp.dart';

class AddExpense extends McpTool {
  @override
  String get name => 'add_expense';

  @override
  String get description => 'Record an expense. Amount is in dollars.';

  @override
  ObjectSchema get input => v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
    'amount': v.num().positive().describe('Amount, like 12.50.'),
    'note': v.string().max(500).optional(),
  });

  @override
  Future<McpToolResult> call(Map<String, dynamic> args, McpContext context) async {
    User user = context.authAs<User>();
    // ... save it
    return McpToolResult.text('Recorded ${args['amount']} for ${user.email}.');
  }
}

Serve it on a route. Find the user first (from a token, a header or the URL), and pass it as auth. scope ties each session to that user:

final McpServer mcp = McpServer(
  name: 'my-app',
  version: '1.0.0',
  tools: <McpTool>[AddExpense()],
);

Route.match(<String>['GET', 'POST', 'DELETE'], '/mcp/{token}', (DoxRequest req) async {
  User? user = await User().where('mcp_token', req.param['token']).getFirst();
  if (user == null) return response('Invalid token').statusCode(401);
  return mcp.handle(req, auth: user, scope: 'user:${user.id}');
});

A small tool can be a function:

McpTool.of(
  name: 'echo',
  description: 'Say the text back.',
  input: v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{'text': v.string()}),
  handler: (Map<String, dynamic> args, McpContext context) {
    return McpToolResult.text(args['text'] as String);
  },
);

docs.title: Tools that take a DTO
docs.text:
A tool can take a @Dto class as its input. Extend McpDtoTool<T>. The rules of the DTO (like @Length and @HexColor) are written once, and handle gets the typed object, not a map.

Use @Describe on a field to explain it to the model. It goes into the JSON Schema as description. It does not change the checks.

@Dto()
class NewCategory {
  @Describe('The category name, like Food.')
  @Length(min: 1, max: 50)
  final String name;

  @Describe('A color, like #1a2b3c.')
  @HexColor()
  final String color;

  const NewCategory({required this.name, required this.color});

  static const DtoSchema<NewCategory> schema = $NewCategoryDto;
}

class CreateCategory extends McpDtoTool<NewCategory> {
  @override
  String get name => 'create_category';

  @override
  String get description => 'Add a category.';

  @override
  DtoSchema<NewCategory> get dto => NewCategory.schema;

  @override
  Future<McpToolResult> handle(NewCategory input, McpContext context) async {
    // ... save it
    return McpToolResult.text('Added ${input.name}.');
  }
}
  • tools/list sends the JSON Schema of the DTO (toJsonSchema()) as inputSchema.
  • The arguments are checked like a DTO in a controller, with async rules like @Unique and @Exists too.
  • Bad arguments are a tool result with isError: true, not a JSON-RPC error. The text lists each problem, so the model can fix the call:
Input validation error: Invalid arguments for tool create_category: name: The name is required; color: The color must be a hex color like #1a2b3c

docs.title: What the server answers
docs.text:
Request Answer POST initialize 200 with the server info and an Mcp-Session-Id header POST a request with a valid Mcp-Session-Id 200 with the JSON-RPC response (a list for a batch) POST only notifications or responses 202, no body POST with no session id 400 POST with an unknown session id, or one of another scope 404, so the client starts a new session POST with an ended session id 404, only when SignedMcpSessions has an ended store. Without it, the id still works POST with a body that is not valid JSON 400 with the JSON-RPC error -32700 POST with an empty batch, or a message that is not JSON-RPC 2.0 400 with the JSON-RPC error -32600 POST with initialize in a batch with other messages 400 with the JSON-RPC error -32600. Send initialize alone POST with an unsupported MCP-Protocol-Version header 400 POST with another Content-Type than JSON 415 Any request with an Origin header that is not in allowedOrigins 403 GET 405: there is no server-to-client stream DELETE with a valid session id 200. The session ends only if SignedMcpSessions has an ended store (see Sessions) DELETE with no session id 400 DELETE with an unknown session id, or one of another scope 404. An ended id also gets 404 when there is an ended store

Methods: initialize, ping, tools/list, tools/call. Others get -32601 Method not found.

  • An unknown tool is a JSON-RPC error (-32602).
  • Bad arguments are a tool result with isError: true and the problems, so the model can fix them.
  • A tool that throws gives a tool result with isError: true and the error text. onToolError gets the error, for logs.

Protocol versions: 2025-11-25, 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05. A client that asks for another one gets the newest.

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text:
SignedMcpSessions (the default) makes ids like <random>.<signature>. The signature is HMAC-SHA256 of the random part and the scope, with a key made from APP_KEY (label dox:mcp).

  • Every isolate, and every server with the same APP_KEY, can check an id. Nothing is stored.
  • A new APP_KEY ends every session. Clients start a new one by themselves.
  • A signed id cannot be ended by itself. To refuse ended ids, give a cache store: SignedMcpSessions(ended: Cache().store('redis')). Use a store that all isolates share (file or Redis, not memory).

For another kind of session, implement McpSessions.

docs.title: OAuth sign-in
docs.text:
McpOAuth lets a client sign in by itself. You give the client only the address, like https://my.app/mcp. The client finds the rest. This is the sign-in the MCP spec asks for: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE.

dox_mcp does the OAuth part. Your app does three things:

  1. Tokens. Implement McpOAuthTokens. issue makes a token for a grant. verify gives what a token stands for (like a user), or null. You choose the table and how a token is revoked. Keep only a hash of the token.
  2. The consent page. Serve it at <issuer>/oauth/authorize, or set authorizePage. It reads client_id, redirect_uri, state, code_challenge, code_challenge_method and resource from the query. The person signs in there the way your app always does.
  3. The answer. Your page calls a route of your own, behind your own login. On yes, the route calls oauth.approve(subject: ...) and gives the page the address to send the browser to. On no, it calls oauth.deny(...). oauth.checkClient(...) gives the client for the page and throws when the client or the redirect address is wrong. Then never send the browser anywhere. Put this route behind CSRF protection. Without it, another site can make a signed-in person say yes to a client without knowing it.
final McpOAuth oauth = McpOAuth(
  issuer: 'https://my.app',
  tokens: MyTokens(),
  codes: Cache().store('file'), // all isolates must share it
);

class McpRouter extends Router {
  @override
  void register() {
    oauth.routes(); // discovery, register and token
    Route.match(<String>['GET', 'POST', 'DELETE'], '/mcp', handleMcp);
  }
}

Future<DoxResponse> handleMcp(DoxRequest req) async {
  Object? user = await oauth.authenticate(req); // reads Authorization: Bearer
  if (user == null) return oauth.unauthorized(); // 401 with WWW-Authenticate
  return mcp.handle(req, auth: user, scope: '$user');
}

On the consent page, show the redirect host, so the person sees where the browser goes. HTML-escape the client name before you print it. The client chose the name, so do not trust it.

Call oauth.routes() in a router with no prefix. The routes must sit at the root of the host. Clients look for /.well-known/... at the root, as the OAuth specs say. The discovery file also gives <issuer>/oauth/register and <issuer>/oauth/token as full addresses. Under a prefix, the routes move, but these addresses do not, so clients cannot find them.

oauth.routes() adds these routes:

Route What it does GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource (also with /mcp after it) Names the MCP address and the issuer. GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server Lists the endpoints. PKCE S256 only, authorization_code only, no client secret. POST /oauth/register Dynamic client registration. Nothing is stored. The client_id is the name and the redirect addresses, signed with APP_KEY. POST /oauth/token Swaps a code for a token. The body is a form or JSON. The code works once, for codeTtl (1 minute). The client, the redirect address and the PKCE verifier must all match. An unknown client_id gets 401 with invalid_client.

Rules:

  • A redirect address must be https, or http on localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1]. It has no #fragment. It has at most 2048 characters (McpOAuth.maxRedirectUriLength).
  • A code_verifier must be 43 to 128 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~ (RFC 7636). Other verifiers get invalid_request. A code_challenge must be 43 base64url characters.
  • The codes live in codes, a Dox cache. Use a store that all isolates share (file on one host, Redis on many). Each code is taken under a lock, so two isolates cannot both swap it.
  • These routes answer any origin (CORS *) and read no cookie. They skip the CORS list of the app.
  • issue may throw McpOAuthException, like access_denied when a person has too many clients. The client gets it from the token endpoint.
  • There is no refresh token. To revoke a client, delete its token.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Check who calls before handle: the MCP route has no auth of its own. McpOAuth is one way to do it.
  • allowedOrigins stops browser pages on other sites (DNS rebinding). Set it when the server runs on a local or private network.
  • Keep tokens out of logs. A token in the URL ends up in proxy logs, so prefer a header when your clients can send one.

docs.title: OpenAPI
docs.text:
This page shows how Dox makes OpenAPI 3.1 docs for your API, and how to change them.

You write no docs code. You get a Scalar docs page at /docs, plus /openapi.json and /openapi.yaml.

The docs come from three places:

  • the routes: method, path, path params, middleware (login),
  • the request classes: a @Dto class,
  • the controllers: the /// comment, the arguments and the return type of each method.

docs.title: 1. Run the builder
docs.text:
dart run build_runner build      # or: dox build_runner:build

dox_builder reads your code and writes lib/generated/openapi.g.dart. Run it again after you change routes, controllers, request classes or models. dox build_runner:watch does it for you while you work.

docs.title: 2. Pass the result to the config
3. Open /docs
docs.text: Start the app and open http://localhost:3000/docs. In production the docs are off, unless you set enabled: true. The document is built on the first /docs request, then kept.

docs.title: The docs page
docs.text:
The page loads Scalar from the jsDelivr CDN, at a fixed version, and reads /openapi.json. Change the look with scalar::

OpenApiConfig(
  registry: openApiRegistry,
  pageTitle: 'Blog API docs',
  scalar: ScalarOptions(theme: ScalarTheme.purple, darkMode: true),
);
Option Default What it does theme ScalarTheme.default_ Color theme. Same names as Scalar: moon, purple, deepSpace, saturn, kepler, mars and more. darkMode false Start in dark mode. The user can still switch. showDownloadButton true Show the button that downloads the document. proxyUrl null Send "Try it" requests through this proxy. Off by default, so requests go from the browser straight to your API.

pageTitle and all options are escaped, so a value can not break the page.

To use Swagger UI instead, set ui::

OpenApiConfig(registry: openApiRegistry, ui: DocsUi.swagger);

docs.title: What you write, what you get
docs.text:
A normal controller. There are no docs annotations here:

class BlogController {
  /// Get one blog
  ///
  /// Deleted blogs are not found.
  Future<Blog?> show(DoxRequest req, String id) async {
    return Blog().find(id);
  }

  /// Create a blog
  Future<Blog> store(CreateBlog body) async { ... }
}

// routes
Route.get('/blogs/{id}', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), (BlogController c) => c.show]);

The generated docs for GET /blogs/{id}:

get:
  tags: [Blog]
  summary: Get one blog
  description: Deleted blogs are not found.
  operationId: BlogController.show
  parameters:
    - {name: id, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string}}
  responses:
    "200":
      content:
        application/json:
          schema: {$ref: "#/components/schemas/Blog"}
    "401": {description: Not logged in}
    "404": {description: Not found}
    "500": {description: Server error}
  security:
    - bearerAuth: []

Blog is in components/schemas, made from the model:

Blog:
  type: object
  properties:
    id: {type: integer}
    title: {type: [string, "null"]}
    user: {anyOf: [{$ref: "#/components/schemas/User"}, {type: "null"}]}
    created_at: {type: [string, "null"], format: date-time}

docs.title: How each part is found
docs.text:
Part of the docs Where it comes from path, method the live route table path param types the controller arguments after the first one, in order. int id gives integer tags the controller class name without Controller (BlogController gives Blog) operationId Class.method, for example BlogController.show summary the first line of the /// comment description the rest of the /// comment request see Request below 200 answer the return type, see Response below 401 and a login scheme @Security on a middleware class, or a middleware whose class name ends with AuthMiddleware. See Login schemes 401 and 403 the Can middleware on the route, or a req.authorize(...) call in the controller method 403 the GuestMiddleware or ValidateSignature middleware on the route, or a Gate.authorize(...) call in the controller method 404 the path has a {param}. The short path of an optional param, like /blog, has no 404 422 the route has a request class, or the controller method calls req.validate<T>() or req.validateSchema(...). The body is {field: message} 500 every route

Can, GuestMiddleware and ValidateSignature are found by their class name. req.authorize(...) is found when it is called on the request (DoxRequest or IDoxRequest) in the controller method. Gate.authorize(...) is found when Gate is the class of dox_auth. A @Response with the same status wins over an automatic answer.

GuestMiddleware(redirectTo: ...) also shows a 403, but the app sends a redirect. Put @Response(403, ...) on the method to replace it.

Routes that the builder does not know (for example inline closures) still get a basic entry.

An optional param shows as two paths. The route /blog/{id?} gives /blog/{id} and /blog. OpenAPI path params must always be required. An optional param in the middle, like /a/{x?}/b, also gives the path without it: /a/{x}/b and /a/b. Optional params next to each other are dropped from the right, the same way the Dox router matches them. When the summary and operation id are made from the path, the short path gets its own, like GET /blog and getBlog.

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
The builder looks in this order. The first one wins.

  1. @Body(T), @Query(T) or @Request(T) on the method.
  2. An argument whose type is a @Dto class: store(CreateBlog body).
  3. A req.validate<T>() call in the method, where T is a @Dto class.

For POST, PUT and PATCH the request is the JSON body. For other methods each field is one query parameter. @Dto(source: Source.query) or Source.body chooses the place by hand. The route body: option still works, and it wins over all of these.

A @Dto class:

@Dto()
class CreateBlog {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 200)
  final String title;

  /// Text of the blog.
  final String? description;   // nullable: optional

  final int views;             // default: optional, `default: 0`

  final Status status;         // enum: only `draft` or `published`

  final List<Tag> tags;        // a list of another @Dto class

  const CreateBlog({required this.title, this.description, this.views = 0,
      required this.status, required this.tags});
}

The keys are the same as the keys the DTO reads: snake_case by default (postCode is post_code), or @Name('key'), or @Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field). Each rule annotation adds its JSON Schema keys. See the rules reference.

docs.title: Response
docs.text:
The return type of the method gives the 200 answer. Future<T> counts as T.

Return type Schema a model (@DoxModel) $ref to the model. Keys in hidden are left out List<Model> an array of the model a @Dto class $ref to the class a Serializer<Model> the map that convert() returns, else the model Pagination total, per_page, last_page, current_page, data String, int, bool, Map, List the basic JSON type dynamic the types of the return values. A map literal gives its keys. Exceptions are left out DoxResponse, void no schema

A model schema has the primary key, the @Column fields, created_at, updated_at, the relations (only there when loaded) and the @Computed getters.

docs.title: Change the docs (optional)
docs.text:
Add these to a controller method when the automatic result is not what you want. They are all in dox_core.

@Summary('Log in')
@Description('Gives a bearer token for the Authorization header.')
@Tags(<String>['Auth'])
@Request(LoginUser)
@Response(200, LoginResult)
@Response(401, null, description: 'Wrong email or password')
Future<dynamic> login(DoxRequest req) async { ... }
Annotation What it does @Summary('text') short title. Default: the first line of the /// comment @Description('text') longer text. Default: the rest of the /// comment @Tags(['Users']) groups. On a method or on the class @Request(T) the request class. Body or query by the HTTP method @Body(T) the request class, always the body @Query(T) the request class, always the query @Response(status, Type, description: '') one answer. Add more than one for more codes. With a 2xx one, the return type is not used @ApiDeprecated() marks the route as deprecated. Dart @Deprecated works too @ApiIgnore() leaves the method (or the whole class) out of the docs. To leave out routes by path, use include and exclude in OpenApiConfig @DoxController(tag: 'Users') for a class that the builder can not see in a Route.get(...) call

The Type of @Response can be a model, List<User>, a @Dto, a Serializer or a basic type like String.

Each annotation also has a lower case name, like @summary('Log in'). Only @Response has none, because response() is already a dox_core helper.

docs.title: Login schemes
docs.text:
Put @Security above a middleware class. Every route with this middleware gets the scheme in the docs. Run dart run build_runner build after you add it.

/// `Authorization: Bearer <api key>`. Not a JWT.
@Security.bearer(format: 'API key')
class ApiKeyAuthMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware { ... }

/// `X-API-Key: <key>`
@Security.apiKey(header: 'X-API-Key')
class HeaderKeyMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware { ... }
Annotation Scheme in the docs @Security.bearer() type: http, scheme: bearer, no format @Security.bearer(format: 'JWT') the same, with bearerFormat: JWT @Security.apiKey(header: 'X-API-Key') type: apiKey, in: header, name: X-API-Key. The default header is X-API-Key

The scheme name is the class name without Middleware, with a small first letter: ApiKeyAuthMiddleware gives apiKeyAuth. Use scheme: 'myName' to pick another name.

A middleware without @Security whose class name ends with AuthMiddleware gets bearerAuth: a bearer token with no format, because Dox can not know if it is a JWT.

For a key in the query or a cookie, or to change a scheme without the builder, set it in the config. The config wins over @Security:

OpenApiConfig(
  registry: openApiRegistry,
  securitySchemes: <String, SecurityScheme>{
    'apiKey': SecurityScheme.apiKey(name: 'X-API-Key'),
  },
  securityByMiddleware: <String, List<Map<String, List<String>>>>{
    'ApiKeyMiddleware': <Map<String, List<String>>>[
      <String, List<String>>{'apiKey': <String>[]},
    ],
  },
);

docs.title: How a route finds its docs
docs.text:
The builder saves the docs of each controller method, and each Route.get(...) / Route.resource(...) call it finds. At runtime, Dox matches each route handler by its method name, HTTP method and the end of its path. If there is no match, it picks the only method with that name and the same argument types. Group prefixes (like api/) do not matter.

Tip

Two controllers can have a method with the same name, like index. When the route names the class, like (LinkController c) => c.index or Route.get<LinkController>(...), only methods of that class match. With a plain links.index, the path of the route call decides.

docs.title: Write the files: dox openapi:generate
docs.text:
dox openapi:generate              # storage/openapi/openapi.json and openapi.yaml
dox openapi:generate docs/api     # another folder

It runs bin/openapi.dart of your app. A new app does not have this file. Make it with this code:

bin/openapi.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/app.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);
  await Dox().writeOpenApi(args.isEmpty ? 'storage/openapi' : args.first);
  exit(0);
}

writeOpenApi runs your providers and registers the routes. It does not start the server.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
dox_openapi also works on its own. Describe routes by hand with ApiDoc:

import 'package:dox_openapi/dox_openapi.dart';

ApiDoc docs = ApiDoc();
Map<String, dynamic> user = docs.schema('User', userSchema); // returns a $ref

docs.route('GET', '/users/{id}',
    summary: 'Get one user',
    tags: <String>['users'],
    params: <String, Object>{'id': <String, dynamic>{'type': 'integer'}},
    responses: <int, ResponseDoc>{
      200: ResponseDoc(schema: user, description: 'The user'),
      404: const ResponseDoc(description: 'Not found'),
    });

OpenApi api = OpenApi(info: const Info(title: 'My API', version: '1.0.0'), docs: docs);

api.toJson();                              // Map
api.toJsonString();                        // pretty JSON
api.toYaml();                              // YAML
await api.writeFiles('storage/openapi');   // openapi.json + openapi.yaml

// Serve the docs from your own server
OpenApiServer server = OpenApiServer(api); // Swagger UI: OpenApiServer(api, ui: DocsUi.swagger)
OpenApiResponse? page = server.handle('/docs'); // also '/openapi.json' and '/openapi.yaml'
if (page != null) {
  // send page.body with the header Content-Type: page.contentType
}

A schema can be a JSON Schema Map, a dox_validation schema, or any object with toJsonSchema(). Paths can use {id} or :id. Both become {id}. responses takes status codes as int keys. To use a text key like default or 2XX, pass namedResponses:

docs.route('GET', '/users/{id}',
    responses: <int, ResponseDoc>{
      200: ResponseDoc(schema: user, description: 'The user'),
    },
    namedResponses: <String, ResponseDoc>{
      'default': const ResponseDoc(description: 'Any other error'),
    });

namedResponses come after responses. When the same key is in both, the one in namedResponses wins. DoxRouteAdapter().addTo(docs, routes) adds a basic entry for each route you did not describe.

docs.title: Socket.IO
docs.text:
This page shows how to set up Socket.IO in a Dox app with dox_socketio.

It can also run on its own, see Without Dox.

dox_socketio is a Socket.IO v4 server for Dart. The official clients connect to it with no changes: socket.io-client (JavaScript v4) and the Dart socket_io_client package. It has acks, rooms, namespaces, binary data and long-polling. Socket.IO is the way to do realtime in Dox.

docs.title: In a Dox app
docs.text: Socket.IO runs on the same port as your HTTP routes, at /socket.io/. You add a provider, a config, a namespace and one env key.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dox add socketio

Add --broadcasting to turn on broadcasting. It adds the package, the provider, the config and the env key (steps 1 to 3 and 5 below). It never overwrites a file, so it is safe to run twice. Then do steps 4 and 6 yourself.

docs.title: Set it up by hand
docs.text: Do all the steps below when you do not use dox add socketio.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text: dart pub add dox_socketio

docs.title: 2. The provider
docs.text:
The provider starts Socket.IO in every isolate. Put it in lib/providers/, so the generated container finds it:

lib/providers/socketio_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/socketio.dart';

class AppSocketIoProvider extends SocketIoProvider {
  AppSocketIoProvider() : super(socketIoConfig);
}

docs.title: 3. The config
docs.text:
The config says which namespaces to serve:

lib/config/socketio.dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  enabled: env.socketioEnabled,
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace()],
);
SocketIoConfig option Default What it does enabled true serve Socket.IO at options.path options ServerOptions() see Options namespaces [] NamespaceHandler classes to register adapter null (in memory with one isolate, IsolateAdapter with many) makes one adapter in each isolate, see Many isolates

docs.title: 4. A namespace
docs.text:
A namespace handles the events of one path, like /chat:

lib/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.emit('welcome', <String, dynamic>{'id': socket.id});
    socket.join('lobby');
    socket.on('message', onMessage);
  }

  void onMessage(SocketEvent event) {
    event.socket.to('lobby').emit('message', event.data); // everyone in lobby but me
    event.ack('sent'); // answer the client callback
  }
}

See Namespaces for middleware and dependencies.

docs.title: 5. Turn it on
docs.text:
Add a getter for the SOCKETIO_ENABLED key to lib/config/env.dart:

lib/config/env.dart
  /// serve Socket.IO on the app port
  bool get socketioEnabled => false;
.env
SOCKETIO_ENABLED=true

Then run dart run build_runner build and dox serve.

docs.title: 6. Connect a client
docs.text:
import { io } from 'socket.io-client';

const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/chat', { transports: ['websocket'] });
socket.on('welcome', (data) => console.log(data.id));
socket.emit('message', 'hi', (answer) => console.log(answer)); // 'sent'

Use transports: ['websocket']. See Many isolates for why.

docs.title: Send from a controller or a service
docs.text:
SocketIoProvider.server is the Socket.IO server of this isolate:

await SocketIoProvider.server?.of('/chat').to('lobby').emit('news', data);

From a queue job or another program, use the emitter.

  • Requests to /socket.io/ go to Socket.IO before the router. Middleware and body reading are skipped. To log users in, see Log in a socket.
  • With no provider, or with enabled: false, there is no extra work per request.
  • Need a plain WebSocket with no Socket.IO protocol? Route.websocket(path, handler) in dox_core gives you the raw socket.

docs.title: Many isolates
docs.text:
Dox runs one isolate per CPU core, and each isolate has its own Socket.IO server. A client is connected to one of them.

With many isolates and no adapter, the provider uses the IsolateAdapter. It sends each broadcast to the other isolates of the process (through IsolateBus of dox_core), so it reaches the clients of every isolate. socketsJoin, fetchSockets, serverSideEmit and broadcast acks work across isolates too. You need no Redis.

Adapter Reaches InMemoryAdapter (one isolate) the clients of this isolate IsolateAdapter (many isolates, the default) the clients of every isolate of this process RedisAdapter the clients of every isolate of every server

Add each namespace in every isolate

The IsolateAdapter counts the isolates on the bus, not the isolates that have a namespace. fetchSockets and serverSideEmitWithAck wait for an answer from each of them. A NamespaceHandler in the config is added in every isolate, so it is fine. A namespace that only one isolate adds with io.of('/x') gets no answer from the others. Then these calls wait 5 seconds and throw.

Clients should connect with websocket only

One websocket stays on one isolate. HTTP long-polling sends many requests, and they can reach different isolates. Long-polling only works with totalIsolate: 1, or with sticky sessions in front of many single-isolate servers. Dox logs this hint at startup when it runs many isolates and polling is allowed.

With more than one server process, or next to Node.js servers, use the Redis adapter.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
dox_socketio also runs on its own, with no Dox app:

import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer();
  io.register(ChatNamespace());
  await io.listen(3001);
}
  • io.listen(port) starts a native server (dox_http_native) on its own port. Run it in its own small program, for example bin/socket.dart, and put it behind the same proxy as the HTTP server.
  • io.attach(httpServer) uses a server you already have: a NativeHttpServer or a dart:io one.
  • In your own server, call io.handle(request) when io.matches(request) is true.
  • io.on('connection', (Socket socket) {...}) handles the default namespace / with no class.

docs.title: Namespaces
docs.text:
A namespace is a class. Its dependencies come in through the constructor.

class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  ChatNamespace(this.messages);

  final MessageService messages;

  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  List<Middleware> get middleware => <Middleware>[checkToken];

  void checkToken(Socket socket) {
    if (socket.handshake.auth['token'] != 'secret') {
      throw SocketIoException('unauthorized', data: <String, dynamic>{'reason': 'bad token'});
    }
  }

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.on('message', onMessage);
  }

  void onMessage(SocketEvent event) {
    event.ack(messages.save(event.data));
  }
}

// in lib/config/socketio.dart
namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace(MessageService())],

When a middleware throws a SocketIoException, the client gets connect_error with the message and the data. Any other error is written to stderr. The client only gets {"message": "Internal error"}, so it can not see private text like SQL.

A client that is refused is still closed after connectTimeout, unless it joins another namespace.

docs.title: Log in a socket
docs.text:
Socket.IO gets its requests before the router, so route middleware (session, auth) does not run for it. Use SocketAuth as a namespace middleware. Your function gets the handshake and gives the user, or null.

lib/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart
class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  List<Middleware> get middleware => <Middleware>[SocketAuth(findUser).handle];

  static Future<User?> findUser(Handshake handshake) async {
    String? token = handshake.token;
    if (token == null) return null;
    return User().where('api_token', token).getFirst();
  }

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    User user = socket.user! as User;
    socket.join('user:${user.id}');
  }
}

The client sends the token in auth:

const socket = io('http://localhost:3000/chat', {
  transports: ['websocket'],
  auth: { token: 'the-user-token' },
});
socket.on('connect_error', (err) => console.log(err.message)); // 'Unauthorized'
  • With a user, it is kept in socket.user. It stays on this server. fetchSockets() on other servers does not get it.
  • With null, the client gets a connect_error with the message Unauthorized, and onConnection does not run. Change the message with SocketAuth(findUser, message: '...').
  • handshake.token is auth.token from the client, else the Authorization: Bearer header. Browsers can not set headers on a websocket, so use auth.
  • handshake.cookie('name') reads a cookie and decrypts it with the APP_KEY, like req.cookie('name'). Use decrypt: false for a plain cookie.
  • await handshake.session() gives the Dox session of the client, from its session cookie. See below.
  • io.use(SocketAuth(findUser).handle) does the same for the default namespace.

docs.title: With dox_auth
docs.text:
dox_auth can check a JWT or the web login session for you:

static Future<User?> findUser(Handshake handshake) async {
  // an API client or a mobile app sends a JWT
  String? token = handshake.token;
  if (token != null) return Auth(guard: 'api').userFromToken(token);

  // a browser that logged in on a web page sends the session cookie
  Session session = await handshake.session();
  return Auth(guard: 'web').userFromSession(session);
}
  • userFromToken runs the same checks as AuthMiddleware: signature, guard, exp and revocation. A bad, expired, revoked or changed token gives null, so the client is refused. With userCacheTtl on, a deleted or banned user can still connect until the cache time ends, unless forgetUser runs.
  • handshake.session() runs the same cookie checks as SessionMiddleware. A changed cookie, a cookie made with another APP_KEY or an expired session gives an empty session, so userFromSession gives null.
  • handshake.session() uses AppConfig.session. Pass another SessionConfig like handshake.session(config).
  • The session is read once, when the socket connects. A logout later does not close the socket. Call socket.disconnect() yourself if you need that.
  • The session is read only. Changes to it are not saved.
  • With no allowedOrigins, or with '*' in it, handshake.session() prints a warning once.
  • With the cookie session driver, an old copy of the session cookie still works after logout, until the session lifetime ends. If a logout must stop old cookies, use the cache session driver, like SessionConfig(driver: 'cache', store: 'redis').

Cookie login needs allowedOrigins

A browser sends its cookies on a websocket from any website. So if you log users in with a cookie, set allowedOrigins to your own sites. Without it, another website can open a socket as your user. See Allowed origins.

docs.title: Node.js to Dart
docs.text:
Node.js Dart socket.on('e', (a, cb) => ...) socket.on('e', (SocketEvent e) => ...), then e.data, e.args, e.ack(x) socket.emit('e', a, b) socket.emit('e', a) or socket.emitArgs('e', [a, b]) await socket.timeout(5000).emitWithAck('e', a) await socket.emitWithAck('e', a, timeout: Duration(seconds: 5)) socket.join(r) / socket.leave(r) the same socket.to(r).emit(...) the same socket.broadcast.emit(...) the same io.to(r).except(x).emit(...) the same io.of('/chat'), io.use(fn) the same socket.handshake .headers, .query, .auth, .address, .token, .cookie(name), .session() socket.data socket.data (a Map) await io.in(r).fetchSockets() await io.to(r).fetchSockets() (all servers) await io.timeout(5000).emitWithAck('e', a) await io.timeout(Duration(seconds: 5)).emitWithAck('e', a) io.serverSideEmit('e', a) await io.serverSideEmit('e', [a]) io.on('e', (a, cb) => ...) (from other servers) io.onServerSideEmit('e', (ServerSideEvent e) => ...), then e.data, e.ack(x)
  • disconnecting and disconnect give the reason in event.data, like transport close or ping timeout.
  • Binary data: send a Uint8List. It can be anywhere in lists and maps.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
SocketIoServer(
  options: ServerOptions(
    path: '/socket.io/',
    pingInterval: Duration(seconds: 25),
    pingTimeout: Duration(seconds: 20),
    maxHttpBufferSize: 1000000,
    transports: <String>['polling', 'websocket'],
    cors: CorsOptions(origins: <String>['https://my.app'], credentials: true),
  ),
);
Option Default What it does path /socket.io/ the URL path pingInterval 25 s how often the server sends a ping pingTimeout 20 s how long to wait for the pong before the client is gone upgradeTimeout 10 s how long an upgrade from polling to websocket may take connectTimeout 45 s how long the client has to join a namespace maxHttpBufferSize 1,000,000 bytes the biggest message. A bigger websocket message closes the connection maxAttachments 10 the most binary parts in one packet. A packet with more closes that client transports ['polling', 'websocket'] allowed transports allowUpgrades true let polling clients move to websocket cors null CORS headers for polling requests. It also checks the origin of websockets allowedOrigins null the sites that may connect, see Allowed origins allowRequest null a function that accepts or refuses each request, see Allow requests and limit sessions maxSessions null the most open sessions, see Allow requests and limit sessions
  • cors with a list of origins: a websocket from another origin gets 403. A request with no Origin header (not a browser) is allowed.
  • cors: null, or * in origins: websockets from any origin are allowed. If you log users in with cookies, list your origins.
  • * together with credentials: true throws an ArgumentError. List your origins instead.
  • Websocket compression is off. A message bigger than maxHttpBufferSize closes with code 1009.
  • On a plain dart:io server (io.attach), the whole message is read before the size check. Also set a size limit in your proxy.

docs.title: Allowed origins
docs.text:
allowedOrigins says which websites may open a socket. Set it when you log users in with cookies.

ServerOptions(allowedOrigins: <String>['https://app.example.com']);
  • null (the default): no extra check. Websockets are checked against cors when it is set. Dox logs a warning at start.
  • []: only pages of the same host can connect.
  • A list of sites: the same host and those sites can connect.
  • ['*']: every site can connect.
  • Other sites get 403. A client with no Origin header (not a browser) is always allowed.

docs.title: Allow requests and limit sessions
docs.text:
allowRequest is a function that runs for every handshake and every websocket upgrade. It does not run again for the polling requests of an open session. It gets an EngineRequest (headers, query and address). It gives true or false, sync or async. maxSessions is the most open sessions. Set both in the options of SocketIoConfig:

lib/config/socketio.dart
SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  options: ServerOptions(
    allowRequest: (EngineRequest req) => req.query['key'] == 'secret',
    maxSessions: 10000,
  ),
);
  • When the function gives false or throws, the client gets 403 with {"code":4,"message":"Forbidden"}.
  • At the limit, a new handshake gets 503 with {"code":3,"message":"Too many sessions"}. Open sessions keep working.
  • The count is per isolate. With 4 isolates, the app allows 4 times maxSessions.
  • Keep the function fast. When the client leaves while the function runs, the session is still made. It holds a maxSessions slot until the ping timeout.
  • A browser client only sees a connect error. It does not see the 403 or 503 body.

Both are null by default: all requests are allowed and there is no limit.

docs.title: Many servers: Redis adapter
docs.text:
With more than one server process, or next to Node.js servers, use the Redis adapter. Then a broadcast on one server reaches the clients of all servers, and of all their isolates.

Add the ioredis package:

dart pub add ioredis

In a Dox app, make the adapter in each isolate with a factory:

lib/config/socketio.dart
import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:ioredis/ioredis.dart';
import 'package:my_app/app/socket/chat.namespace.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

SocketIoConfig socketIoConfig = SocketIoConfig(
  enabled: env.socketioEnabled,
  namespaces: <NamespaceHandler>[ChatNamespace()],
  adapter: const RedisSocketAdapterFactory(),
);

/// makes the Redis adapter inside each isolate.
/// A Redis connection can not be sent to another isolate.
class RedisSocketAdapterFactory extends SocketAdapterFactory {
  const RedisSocketAdapterFactory();

  @override
  Adapter create() {
    Redis redis = Redis(); // 127.0.0.1:6379. Or Redis(RedisOptions(host: ..., port: ...))
    return RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis);
  }
}

Without Dox, pass the adapter to the server:

Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
SocketIoServer io = SocketIoServer(
  adapter: RedisAdapter(subscriber: redis.duplicate(), publisher: redis),
);
  • The subscriber needs its own connection. A Redis connection in subscribe mode can not run other commands.
  • It uses the format of @socket.io/redis-adapter. Node.js servers with that adapter can share one Redis with Dox servers.
  • It reads messages in msgpack and in JSON. It writes msgpack, like the Node.js adapter. If your Node.js servers use a JSON parser, set format: RedisFormat.json.
  • fetchSockets, socketsJoin, socketsLeave and disconnectSockets act on the sockets of all servers.
  • Broadcasts with an ack get the acks of clients on all servers.
  • Servers can send events to each other with serverSideEmit. Clients do not get them.
  • A request waits at most requestsTimeout for the other servers (5 seconds by default, like Node.js).
  • Long-polling needs sticky sessions, the same as with many isolates. Or use transports: ['websocket'] on the client.

docs.title: Act on all servers
docs.text:
// sockets of every server. Sockets of this server are `Socket`s.
List<RemoteSocket> sockets = await io.to('room1').fetchSockets();
for (RemoteSocket socket in sockets) {
  socket.emit('hello', socket.data['name']);
}

await io.to('room1').socketsJoin('room2');
await io.to('banned').disconnectSockets();

// one ack per client, from all servers. A timeout is needed.
List<Object?> answers = await io
    .timeout(const Duration(seconds: 5))
    .emitWithAck('ping', 'are you there?');

fetchSockets throws a TimeoutException when a server does not answer in time.

docs.title: Events between servers
docs.text:
serverSideEmit sends an event to the other servers. Clients do not get it.

// on every server
io.onServerSideEmit('reload-config', (ServerSideEvent event) {
  reloadConfig(event.data);
  event.ack('done'); // only when the sender waits for an answer
});

// on one server
await io.serverSideEmit('reload-config', <Object?>['v2']);

// wait for one answer from each other server
List<Object?> answers = await io.serverSideEmitWithAck('reload-config', <Object?>['v2']);

When a server does not answer in time, serverSideEmitWithAck throws an AckTimeoutException. Its responses holds the answers that came back. onServerSideEmit is also on namespaces: io.of('/chat').onServerSideEmit(...).

docs.title: Broadcasting
docs.text: To send events to public, private and presence channels, see Broadcasting.

docs.title: Emit from other programs
docs.text:
An emitter sends events to your clients without a Socket.IO server. Use it in a queue worker, a cron job or a service in another language. It writes to Redis, and every server with the Redis adapter sends the event to its clients.

Dart (for example in a Dox queue job or a CLI command):

import 'package:dox_socketio/dox_socketio.dart';
import 'package:ioredis/ioredis.dart';

Future<void> main() async {
  Redis redis = Redis(RedisOptions(host: '127.0.0.1', port: 6379));
  SocketIoEmitter emitter = SocketIoEmitter(redis);

  await emitter.emit('news', <String, dynamic>{'title': 'hello'}); // all clients of `/`
  await emitter.to('room1').except('room2').emit('news', 'hi room1');
  await emitter.of('/chat').to('vip').emit('notice', 'for vip');

  await emitter.to('room1').socketsJoin('room3'); // sockets in room1 join room3
  await emitter.to('room3').socketsLeave('room1');
  await emitter.to('banned').disconnectSockets();

  await redis.disconnect();
}

Node.js, with @socket.io/redis-emitter:

import { Emitter } from '@socket.io/redis-emitter';
import { createClient } from 'redis';

const redis = createClient({ url: 'redis://127.0.0.1:6379' });
await redis.connect();

const emitter = new Emitter(redis);
emitter.to('room1').emit('news', { title: 'hello' });
emitter.of('/chat').emit('notice', 'for everyone in /chat');
  • The emitters of other languages (PHP, Python, Go) use the same format, so they work too.
  • Binary data (Uint8List in Dart, Buffer in Node.js) arrives as binary.
  • The emitter does not wait for an answer. It can not know if a client got the event.
  • key must be the same as the key of the adapter. Both default to socket.io.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
This page shows how to save and read files with dox_storage.

dox_storage gives one API for files in many places: local disk, AWS S3 and S3-compatible services.

docs.title: In a Dox app
docs.text: A new app from dox create already has steps 1 to 3. Go to step 4.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text: dart pub add dox_storage

docs.title: 2. The config
3. The provider
docs.text:
The provider sets up the disks in every isolate. Put it in lib/providers/, so the generated container finds it:

lib/providers/storage_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/storage.dart';

class AppStorageProvider extends StorageProvider {
  AppStorageProvider() : super(storageConfig);
}

Run dart run build_runner build.

docs.title: 4. Use it
docs.text:
import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';

Route.post('/avatar', (DoxRequest req) async {
  RequestFile file = req.input('avatar');
  String path = await Storage().putFile('avatars', file);
  return <String, String>{'path': path}; // /avatars/<uuid>.png
});
  • Storage().use('s3') gives the full Disk of this page.
  • Storage.route('files') serves local signed URLs.
  • S3 disks, env keys and all Storage() functions are in File Storage.

docs.title: Drivers
docs.text: Driver Use for Signed download URL Signed upload URL LocalDriver a folder on the server Yes (HMAC with your app key) No S3Driver AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, GCS (HMAC keys) Yes (SigV4) Yes (SigV4) MemoryDriver tests fake URLs fake URLs

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
dox_storage also works on its own:

dart pub add dox_storage

Make a DriveManager with your disks:

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';

Map<String, String> env = Platform.environment;

DriveManager drive = DriveManager(
  defaultDisk: 'local',
  disks: <String, DriverContract>{
    'local': LocalDriver(LocalDriverConfig(
      root: 'storage',
      urlBase: 'https://app.test/uploads',
      atomicWrites: true, // off by default
      appKey: env['APP_KEY'], // signs local URLs
    )),
    's3': S3Driver(S3DriverConfig(
      bucket: 'my-bucket',
      region: 'us-east-1',
      accessKeyId: env['AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID']!,
      secretAccessKey: env['AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY']!,
    )),
  },
);

Disk disk = drive.use('s3'); // or drive.use() for the default disk

use() throws UnsupportedOperationException when no disk has that name.

LocalDriverConfig(atomicWrites: true) makes a local disk write to a temp file and rename it when the write is done. In a Dox app, use 'atomic_writes': true in the disk map. A failed or stopped upload then never leaves a partial file, and the old file stays. Temp file names end with .dox-upload.tmp, and listAll() hides them. It is off by default.

LocalDriverConfig(permissions: LocalPermissions()) makes visibility the file mode. In a Dox app, use 'permissions': true in the disk map. setVisibility then runs chmod and getVisibility reads the mode of the file. The modes are public file 0644, private file 0600, public folder 0755 and private folder 0700. Without permissions, setVisibility does nothing, and getVisibility gives the disk visibility. LocalPermissions takes other modes. In a Dox app, the map has a file and a dir key, each with public and private. A mode that is not in the map keeps its default. A key that is not one of these is ignored. Each mode must be an int from 0 to 0x1ff (0777). A string like '0644', a negative number or a bigger number throws ArgumentError when the disk is made. It is off by default. On Windows it does nothing.

  • The mode is set before the content is written. A private file is never readable by others, not even for a moment.
  • A new file gets the visibility of the write, or the disk visibility.
  • An overwrite, append and prepend keep the mode the file has, unless the call gives a visibility.
  • A copy gets the visibility of the call, or else the mode of the source. It is written to a temp file first and then renamed. Listings hide that temp file. A copy onto a symlink replaces the link.
  • A move keeps the mode, unless the call gives a visibility.
  • Folders that a write creates get the folder mode. Folders that were there before, and the disk root, keep their mode.
  • getVisibility reads the real mode. The private mode is private. Any other mode is public.
  • getVisibility and setVisibility of a symlink throw UnsupportedOperationException.
  • When the chmod fails, a file that the write created is removed.

On every local disk, with permissions on or off, copy or move of a missing file throws FileNotFoundException and makes no folders.

docs.title: Use a disk
docs.text:
In a Dox app, get a disk with Storage().use('s3'). Without Dox, use drive.use('s3').

await disk.put('avatars/1.png', bytes); // String, List<int> or Stream<List<int>>
await disk.put('a.json', '{}', options: WriteOptions(contentType: 'application/json', visibility: Visibility.public));
await disk.putStream('videos/big.mp4', File('big.mp4').openRead());

Uint8List data = await disk.get('avatars/1.png');
String text = await disk.getString('notes/a.txt');
Stream<List<int>> stream = await disk.getStream('videos/big.mp4');
ObjectMetaData meta = await disk.getMetaData('avatars/1.png'); // size, contentType, lastModified, etag
bool found = await disk.exists('avatars/1.png');
int size = await disk.size('avatars/1.png');
DateTime changed = await disk.lastModified('avatars/1.png');

await disk.append('logs/app.log', 'new line');  // a missing file is made
await disk.prepend('logs/app.log', 'first line');
await disk.makeDirectory('reports/2026');        // local disk only
bool folder = await disk.directoryExists('reports');

await disk.copy('a.png', 'b.png');
await disk.move('b.png', 'c.png');
await disk.delete('c.png');
bool gone = await disk.missing('c.png');
await disk.deleteAll('avatars'); // every file under this prefix, '' for all
await disk.deleteDirectory('reports'); // never the root

List<String> files = await disk.files('avatars');         // direct files
List<String> all = await disk.allFiles('avatars');        // in sub-folders too
List<String> folders = await disk.directories('avatars'); // direct sub-folders

ListResult page = await disk.listAll('avatars', ListOptions(recursive: true, limit: 100));
// next page: ListOptions(paginationToken: page.paginationToken)

await disk.setVisibility('avatars/1.png', Visibility.public);
Visibility v = await disk.getVisibility('avatars/1.png');
  • size and lastModified throw FileNotFoundException when the file is missing.
  • append and prepend put a \n between the old and the new text, but only when the file is not empty. Change it with separator, like separator: ', '.
  • append and prepend keep the visibility and content type of the file.
  • append and prepend read the file and write it back. They are not atomic, so two writers at the same time can lose a write.
  • makeDirectory makes the folder and its parent folders on a local disk. On any other disk it does nothing, because those disks have no real folders.
  • files, allFiles and directories give keys, like avatars/1.png. They read every page of listAll.
  • deleteDirectory deletes a folder and its files. The root ('' or /) throws InvalidKeyException. deleteAll() empties the whole disk.
  • directoryExists is true when a folder exists. On a local disk it checks the real folder. On S3 and memory disks, a folder exists when a file is under it. exists is true for files only.

docs.title: Save an upload
docs.text:
Stream the upload to the disk. The file is not loaded into memory.

Route.post('/avatar', (DoxRequest req) async {
  RequestFile file = req.input('avatar');
  String key = 'avatars/${DateTime.now().microsecondsSinceEpoch}.${file.extension}';
  await disk.putStream(key, file.stream());
  return <String, String>{'url': await disk.getUrl(key)};
});

Warning

Do not use file.filename from the client as the key. A client can send any name. Make your own name, like above or with a uuid.

docs.title: URLs and signed URLs
docs.text:
String url = await disk.getUrl('avatars/1.png');

// a download link that works for 10 minutes
String signed = await disk.getSignedUrl('avatars/1.png',
    options: SignedUrlOptions(expiresIn: Duration(minutes: 10)));

// the browser can upload straight to S3 with this URL
String upload = await disk.getSignedUploadUrl('avatars/2.png',
    options: SignedUrlOptions(contentType: 'image/png'));
  • expiresIn is 30 minutes when you do not set it.
  • S3 signed URLs can live at most 7 days. This is an S3 rule.
  • contentDisposition asks the server to send this header on download, like attachment; filename="report.pdf".
  • Set urlBase to serve public files from a CDN.

docs.title: Check a local signed URL
docs.text:
In a Dox app, Storage.route('files') does this for you.

LocalDriver.getSignedUrl returns <urlBase>/<key>?expires=...&signature=.... Check it in the route that serves the file:

LocalDriver local = LocalDriver(localConfig);
bool ok = local.verifySignedUrl(keyFromPath, req.uri.queryParameters);
if (!ok) {
  return response('Forbidden').statusCode(403);
}

docs.title: Cloudflare R2
docs.text:
Set supportsAcl: false. R2 does not take ACL headers.

S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  region: 'auto',
  endpoint: 'https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com',
  accessKeyId: '...',
  secretAccessKey: '...',
  supportsAcl: false,
);

docs.title: MinIO
docs.text:
MinIO needs path style URLs, so set forcePathStyle: true.

S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  region: 'us-east-1',
  endpoint: 'http://localhost:9000',
  forcePathStyle: true,
  accessKeyId: 'minioadmin',
  secretAccessKey: 'minioadmin',
);

docs.title: DigitalOcean Spaces
docs.text:
Spaces works like S3. Put the region of your space in region and in the endpoint.

S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-space',
  region: 'nyc3',
  endpoint: 'https://nyc3.digitaloceanspaces.com',
  accessKeyId: '...',
  secretAccessKey: '...',
);

docs.title: Google Cloud Storage
docs.text:
Set supportsAcl: false and supportsBatchDelete: false. GCS does not take ACL headers or the S3 batch delete call.

S3DriverConfig(
  bucket: 'my-bucket',
  region: 'auto',
  endpoint: 'https://storage.googleapis.com',
  accessKeyId: 'GOOG...',
  secretAccessKey: '...',
  supportsAcl: false,
  supportsBatchDelete: false,
);

Big files

  • put sends one request. S3 allows at most 5 GiB in one request.
  • putStream uses a multipart upload when the stream is bigger than multipartPartSize (8 MiB). Only one part is in memory at a time. The limit is about 78 GiB. Raise multipartPartSize for bigger files.
  • copy and move copy on the server. S3 allows at most 5 GiB here.

docs.title: Keys are checked
docs.text:
• a//b/./c.txt becomes a/b/c.txt. \ becomes /.
  • .., absolute paths (/etc/passwd) and null bytes throw InvalidKeyException.
  • LocalDriver also checks that the path stays inside its root folder.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
All errors extend StorageException and have the key.

Error When FileNotFoundException the file does not exist PermissionDeniedException file system permission error, or S3 403 InvalidKeyException unsafe key UnsupportedOperationException the driver can not do this DriverException anything else. The first error is in cause

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
fake() swaps a disk for a memory disk.

Disk fake = drive.fake('s3'); // drive.use('s3') now writes to memory
await uploadAvatar();         // your code
expect(await fake.exists('avatars/1.png'), isTrue);
drive.restore('s3');

A disk also has assertExists and assertMissing. They throw a StateError when the check fails:

Disk fake = drive.fake('s3');
await uploadAvatar();
await fake.assertExists('avatars/1.png');
await fake.assertMissing('avatars/old.png');

docs.title: Your own driver
docs.text:
Implement DriverContract and register it.

class DropboxDriver implements DriverContract { ... }

drive.register('dropbox', DropboxDriver(...));
await drive.use('dropbox').put('a.txt', 'hello');

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
dox_validation checks input and gives you typed Dart objects.

It has two parts:

  1. DTOs: a class with @Dto() and rule annotations. A generator writes the checks. Use this for almost everything.
  2. Fluent schemas: v.object(...), like Zod. Use it only when the shape is known at runtime.

Both give all errors at once, and a JSON Schema for OpenAPI.

docs.title: In a Dox app
docs.text:
dox_core uses dox_validation and exports it. There is nothing to install: import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart' is all you need.

  1. Make a DTO with dox make:dto CreateUser. It writes lib/app/dtos/create_user/create_user.dto.dart.
  2. Run the generator: dox build_runner:build.
  3. Give the list of DTOs to the app, once:
lib/config/app.dart
import 'package:my_app/generated/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  // ...
  dtos: dtos, // from lib/generated/dtos.g.dart
);

Then ask for the DTO in a controller. Dox checks the body before the method runs. Bad input gets 422 with the errors:

lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart
class UserController {
  Future<Map<String, dynamic>> store(CreateUser body) async {
    // body is already checked and typed
    return <String, dynamic>{'name': body.name};
  }
}

The full guide is at Validation. Every rule is in the rules reference. The rest of this page is about the package itself.

docs.title: Without Dox
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_validation
dart pub add dev:dox_builder dev:build_runner

import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

The DTO generator is in dox_builder. Run it with dart run build_runner build. @Unique and @Exists are in dox_orm, not here.

docs.title: DTOs
docs.text:
import 'package:dox_validation/dox_validation.dart';

part 'create_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  @Trim()
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  const CreateUser({required this.name, required this.email});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}

The generator makes, for each @Dto class:

Name What it is $CreateUserDto a const DtoSchema<CreateUser>: the checks, the converter and the JSON Schema lib/generated/dtos.g.dart const List<DtoSchema<Object>> dtos: every DTO in lib/. Dox uses it to find DTOs by type. An app with no DTO gets an empty final list.

The static const ... schema = $CreateUserDto; line is how you reach the schema: CreateUser.schema.

docs.title: DtoSchema<T>
docs.text:
DtoSchema<T> is also a Schema<T>. So it works everywhere a schema works: inside v.object(...), v.list(...), with OpenAPI, and as a StandardSchema.

Member Does Future<T> validateMap(Map<String, dynamic> input, {Source source = Source.body, Map<String, String> params = const {}, MessageResolver? messages, String? locale}) all checks, then the object. Throws ValidationException with the errors. Future<ParseResult<T>> safeValidateMap(input, {source, params, messages, locale}) the same, but never throws for bad input. result.success, result.value, result.errors. T fromMap(Map<String, dynamic> input) builds the object with no checks. Reads keys, converts JSON types, uses defaults. A wrong type throws a TypeError. Only for data you trust. Map<String, dynamic> toMap(T value) the object as a map with the input keys (snake_case). DateTime becomes an ISO 8601 string, an enum its name. Map<String, dynamic> toJsonSchema() JSON Schema (draft 2020-12). parse, safeParse, parseAsync, safeParseAsync the normal Schema methods, with Source.body. parse throws a StateError when the DTO has async rules. Type get type, String get name CreateUser and 'CreateUser'.

source: Source.query reads the map like a query string: text is converted to the field type. params are path params, used by @Unique(ignoreParam: ...). messages and locale change the error text for this call. See Messages.

ParseResult<CreateUser> result = await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(input);
if (!result.success) {
  print(result.errors); // {'email': 'The email is not a valid email'}
}
ParseResult member What it is success true when there are no errors value the result. null when success is false errors the first message for each field, like {'user.email': '...'} fieldErrors all messages for each field issues the full list of ValidationIssue objects, with code and path

Note

dox_core has its own ValidationException (the HTTP 422 one), so it does not export the one from dox_validation. In a Dox app, both answer 422 when thrown in a controller. In tests, prefer safeValidateMap.

docs.title: JSON Schema of a DTO
docs.text:
For the CreateUser from the Validation guide (with age and role):

CreateUser.schema.toJsonSchema();

{
  "type": "object",
  "title": "CreateUser",
  "properties": {
    "name": { "type": "string", "minLength": 3, "maxLength": 50 },
    "email": { "type": "string", "format": "email" },
    "age": { "type": ["integer", "null"], "minimum": 18 },
    "role": { "type": "string", "enum": ["admin", "user"], "default": "user" }
  },
  "required": ["name", "email"]
}
  • required lists the required fields only.
  • A nullable field has "type": [..., "null"]. A default becomes default.
  • A nested DTO goes in $defs under its class name, with a $ref. OpenAPI moves it to components/schemas.
  • @Dto(strict: true) adds "additionalProperties": false.
  • A /// doc comment on a field becomes description. @Describe('...') on a field sets it too, and wins over the comment. It does not change the checks.
  • Each rule adds its keys. See the rules reference.

docs.title: Fluent schemas (for dynamic input)
docs.text:
Use these when you only know the fields at runtime. The output is a Map, not a class.

final ObjectSchema createUser = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'name': v.string().trim().min(3).max(50),
  'email': v.string().email(),
  'age': v.coerce.int().min(18).optional(),
  'role': v.enumOf<String>(<String>['admin', 'user']).defaultTo('user'),
  'tags': v.list(v.string()).max(5),
  'address': Address.schema, // a DTO inside a fluent schema
});

// throws ValidationException when the input is not valid
Map<String, dynamic> data = createUser.parse(input);

// never throws for bad input
ParseResult<Map<String, dynamic>> result = createUser.safeParse(input);

In a controller: Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(createUser);

Different defaults

Fluent schemas do not follow the DTO rules. A key is required unless you add optional(). "" is a value, not "missing". Text is not converted, unless you use v.coerce.

docs.title: Schemas
docs.text:
Schema Checks v.string() min, max, length, nonEmpty, email, url, uuid, ip, datetime, regex, startsWith, endsWith, includes, alpha, alphaDash, alphaNumeric, json, digits, digitsBetween, dateFormat, password, exists, unique, trim, toLowerCase, toUpperCase v.int(), v.num() min, max, between, gt, lt, positive, nonNegative, multipleOf, exists, unique v.bool() v.date() DateTime only. min, max v.enumOf([...]), v.literal(x) v.list(item) min, max, nonEmpty v.object({...}) strict, passthrough, strip, pick, omit, extend, partial v.map(values, keys: ...) any keys v.union([...]) the first match wins v.any(), v.file() file() has maxSize, minSize, mimes, mimeTypes, dimensions, image and extensions

On every schema:

  • optional(): the key may be missing. null is still an error. After it: requiredIf(other, value) and requiredWith([others]).
  • nullable(): the value may be null. The key must be there.
  • nullish(): both.
  • defaultTo(x): the value when the key is missing. (default is a reserved word in Dart.)
  • transform(fn), refine(fn), refineAsync(fn), superRefine(fn), superRefineAsync(fn), use(rule).
  • same(other), confirmed(): compare with another key of the same object.
