  • bail(): stop at the first failed rule. See Stop at the first error.
  • excludeIf(other, value), excludeUnless(other, value): leave a key out. See Skip a field.
  • describe(text), example(x): only used in the JSON Schema.

docs.title: Coercion
docs.text:
Query strings and form data are text. v.coerce turns text into the right type first.

v.coerce.int().parse('42');       // 42
v.coerce.num().parse('4.5');      // 4.5
v.coerce.bool().parse('on');      // true (true/1/yes/on, false/0/no/off)
v.coerce.date().parse('2024-01-31');
v.coerce.string().parse(5);       // '5'

docs.title: Checks across fields
docs.text:
final ObjectSchema signUp = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'password': v.string().min(8),
  'confirm': v.string(),
}).refine((Map<String, dynamic> data) {
  return data['password'] == data['confirm'];
}, message: 'Passwords do not match', path: <Object>['confirm']);

docs.title: More rules
docs.text:
final ObjectSchema signUp = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  // needs password_confirmation with the same value
  'password': v.string().password(min: 8, mixedCase: true, numbers: true).confirmed(),
  'email': v.string().email().unique('users', column: 'email'),
  'team_id': v.int().exists('teams'),
  'type': v.enumOf<String>(<String>['person', 'company']),
  'company': v.string().optional().requiredIf('type', 'company'),
  'phone': v.string().digitsBetween(8, 12).optional(),
  'country_code': v.string().optional().requiredWith(<String>['phone']),
  'birthday': v.string().dateFormat('Y-m-d').optional(),
  'settings': v.string().json().optional(),
  'age': v.int().between(18, 120).optional(),
});

Map<String, dynamic> data = await signUp.parseAsync(input);

They use the same codes and messages as the DTO annotations. See the rules reference.

  • requiredIf and requiredWith come after optional() or nullish(). Then a missing, null or blank value is an error when the condition is true.

More rules:

final ObjectSchema order = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'type': v.string(),
  'email': v.string().optional().requiredWithout(<String>['phone']),
  'phone': v.string().optional(),
  'fax': v.string().optional().requiredWithoutAll(<String>['email', 'phone']),
  'company': v.string().optional().requiredUnless('type', 'person'),
  'nick': v.string().optional().filled(),
  'note': v.string().optional().present().nullable(),
  'coupon': v.string().optional().prohibitedIf('type', 'guest'),
  'debug': v.any().optional().prohibited(),
  'terms': v.coerce.bool().accepted(),
  'new_password': v.string().different('old_password'),
  'id': v.string().ulid(),
  'min_price': v.int(),
  'max_price': v.int().gtField('min_price'),
});
  • requiredUnless, requiredWithout, requiredWithoutAll, filled and present come after optional(), like requiredIf.
  • present() needs the key. Add .nullable() to allow null.
  • prohibited() and prohibitedIf() come after optional(). They treat empty values in different ways:
    • prohibited(): a missing key or blank text passes. Any other sent value fails, also null, [], 0 and false.
    • prohibitedIf(): when the condition matches, a missing key, null, blank text and an empty list or map pass. 0, false and any other value fail.
  • accepted() and declined() check the value after the type check. v.bool() takes only true and false, so "yes" is a boolean error there. Use v.coerce.bool().accepted() for form words like yes and on (any case), or v.string() or v.any() to check the exact words: true, 1, "1", "true", "yes" and "on" for accepted(), and false, 0, "0", "false", "no" and "off" for declined(). The text is case sensitive.
  • gtField, gteField, ltField and lteField compare with another key. A missing other key fails.
  • The rules are explained in the rules reference.
  • exists and unique are async. Use parseAsync() or safeParseAsync().
  • For one value, the database decides what matches. On MySQL TAKEN@dox.dev is taken when taken@dox.dev is there.
  • exists(table, column: 'id'): the column default is id. For a number id column, use v.int().exists('teams'), not v.string(). Then text like abc is a type error, before any query.
  • unique(table, column: 'email', ignore: id): column is required. It is never taken from the input key, because a key in v.map() comes from the user. ignore skips the row where ignoreColumn (default id) has this value. Use it for updates.

docs.title: Stop at the first error
docs.text:
A fluent schema runs all rules of a value, and gives one error for each failed rule. Add .bail() to stop at the first failed rule. A DTO always does this.

v.string().min(8).email().bail().safeParse('ab');
// one error: min_length. Without bail(): min_length and email.
  • It counts for all rules of that schema, wherever you put .bail() in the chain.
  • Async rules after a failed rule do not run. So no database query is made for a value that is already wrong.
  • Put it before .optional(), .nullable() or .transform(). A rule after one of them belongs to the wrapper, so it does not count. .bail() after a wrapper, like .optional().bail(), does nothing for the rules inside it.
  • On v.object() or v.list(), it counts for the rules of the object or list only. Each field and each item keeps its own setting.
  • A type error already stops the rules of a value, with or without .bail().

docs.title: Skip a field
docs.text:
excludeIf(other, value) and excludeUnless(other, value) skip a field of v.object(). When they match, the field is not checked, and its key is not in the output.

final ObjectSchema account = v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'type': v.string(),
  'vat_number': v.string().min(5).excludeIf('type', 'person'),
  'company': v.string().excludeUnless('type', 'company'),
});

account.parse(<String, dynamic>{'type': 'person', 'vat_number': 'x'});
// {type: person}
  • They work like the DTO @ExcludeIf and @ExcludeUnless. They read the raw input of the other key, and match like requiredIf (also with a list of values).
  • other is a key of the same object. A dotted path like user.type does not work.
  • excludeIf: a missing other key does not skip. excludeUnless: a missing other key counts as null, so the field is skipped.
  • The key is left out also with .optional(), .nullable() or .defaultTo(), in any order. A skipped field never gets its default.
  • In a v.list() of objects, each item is checked on its own.
  • A skipped key is not an unknown key for strict(), and passthrough() does not add it back.
  • In the JSON Schema, the field is not in required.
  • The rules of other fields that read this key (like same, requiredIf or gtField) still see its raw input, also when it is skipped.
  • They work only on a field of v.object(). On a top-level value, a list item or a value of v.map(), they do nothing.

docs.title: The presence verifier
docs.text:
exists and unique ask a PresenceVerifier. dox_orm sets one when the database starts, so in a Dox app they just work. Outside Dox, or with another database layer, set your own. Each isolate has its own value, so set it in a provider's setup(), which runs in every isolate:

class MyVerifier extends PresenceVerifier {
  @override
  Future<Set<String>> found(
    String table,
    String column,
    List<Object?> values, {
    String? exceptColumn,
    Object? exceptValue,
    String? connection,
  }) async {
    // Return the values that are in the column, as text.
    // Bind the values as query parameters, never put them into the SQL.
    return <String>{};
  }
}

class VerifierProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    PresenceVerifier.instance = MyVerifier();
  }
}

Table and column names are checked when the schema is built. They take the same names as the dox_orm query builder: letters, digits, _ and $, with . between parts, like 2fa_codes or public.users. Other names throw an ArgumentError.

docs.title: Async checks
docs.text: refineAsync runs a check that needs the database. Then use parseAsync() or safeParseAsync(). parse() throws a StateError when a schema has async checks.

docs.title: Custom rules in a fluent schema
docs.text:
A Rule<T> class works in both worlds: as an annotation on a DTO, and with use() here.

v.string().min(3).use(const Slug());

See Custom rules for how to write one.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
Each error has a code, like required or min_length. Placeholders: {field}, {value}, and rule values like {min} and {max}.

// for the whole app (outside Dox; in Dox use AppConfig(validationMessages: ...))
MessageResolver.global = MessageResolver(messages: <String, String>{
  'required': 'Please fill in {field}',
});

// for one call
createUser.safeParse(input, messages: MessageResolver(messages: <String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
}));

A resolver for one call is used in place of the global one. Codes that it does not have get the built-in text, not the global text.

With the flag laravelMessageKeys, a key can use the Laravel rule name too, like name.min for the min_length error. See the list of names.

To show a name for {field} in place of the key, give attributes:

MessageResolver.global = MessageResolver(
  attributes: <String, String>{'first_name': 'first name'},
);
// The first name is required

A DTO can give its own names with @Dto(attributes:). See Names for {field}.

For other languages, extend MessageResolver and override resolve(). See Messages.

docs.title: Opt-in flags
docs.text:
ValidationFlags turns on behaviors that are off by default. Set it in Validator.flags.

// turn on one flag
Validator.flags = const ValidationFlags(unicodeAlpha: true);

// turn on every flag
Validator.flags = const ValidationFlags.all();
Flag What it does when on emptyStringsToNull Fluent schemas turn each "" in the input into null before they check it. This also happens in nested maps and lists. So "" fails a required field, and .nullable() gives null. unicodeAlpha alpha, alphaNumeric and alphaDash accept Unicode letters and marks, like José. alphaNumeric and alphaDash also accept Unicode digits. This works for fluent schemas and DTOs. shortInMessage The default in message is The selected {field} is invalid. It does not list the allowed values. dtoAllErrors A DTO runs the rules of each field that has the right type, also when another field is missing or has the wrong type. So one request gets all its errors at once. The type and required errors come first (a nested DTO's errors at its field), then the rule errors. A list or map with a bad item skips its rules. dtoRejectEmptyList A required List field of a DTO fails required on [], and its other rules do not run. It does not apply to a nullable list, a list with a default, or a Maybe<List>. dtoMaybeRejectsEmpty A Maybe<T> field of a DTO (with T not nullable) fails required when the key is sent with an empty value, like "". A missing key still gives Maybe.missing(). It does not apply to Maybe<T?>. A text of only spaces is a value and passes. With @Trim it becomes "" and fails. laravelMessageKeys A custom message key can use the Laravel rule name of a code, like name.min for the min_length error. It works in @Dto(messages:) and in a MessageResolver. At each step of the lookup the Dox code wins. The error code does not change. See the list of names.

With a flag off, the check works as described in the rest of this page: "" is text, the alpha rules take only a-z, A-Z and 0-9, the in message lists the allowed values, and a message key matches only the Dox code. For DTOs: a missing field or a type error stops the rules of the other fields, [] passes a required list, and "" in a Maybe field counts as not sent.

The three DTO flags are read when the check runs. They need the DTO code from a dox_builder that knows them. Run dart run build_runner build once to make it.

emptyStringsToNull is for fluent schemas. A DTO checked on its own keeps ""; use @Dto(emptyStringsToNull: true) there. A DTO inside a fluent schema gets the changed input.

Each isolate has its own Validator.flags. In a Dox app, set it in a provider's setup(), so every isolate runs it:

class ValidationProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Validator.flags = const ValidationFlags.all();
  }
}

docs.title: Standard Schema
docs.text: Every schema, and every DtoSchema, implements the Standard Schema interface (StandardSchema). Code that only needs to validate can accept any StandardSchema, from Dox or from another library.

Short lookup pages, with values taken from the Dox source code.

Page What is on it App config every field of AppConfig and the config classes it holds, with type, default and meaning CLI every dox command, its options and the files it writes Environment variables every env var the framework and its packages read HTTP exceptions the exception classes, their status codes and the body a client gets Request and response the members of DoxRequest, DoxResponse and response() Troubleshooting known problems, the exact error text, the cause and the fix Cheat sheet one page of the code you use every day, with links to the full pages Production checklist what to check before you deploy, and what Dox does not do for you Error index every message Dox prints or throws, when it happens and what to do Changelog what changed in each package, newest first

docs.title: App config
docs.text:
Every field of AppConfig, with its type, its default and what it does.

AppConfig is the one object you give to Dox().initialize(). It lives in lib/config/app.dart.

Source: packages/dox-core/lib/interfaces/app_config.dart.

docs.title: Server
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning appKey String required Encrypts cookies (req.cookie(), DoxCookie) and signs local storage URLs. It must be exactly 32 characters. The app stops at start when it is empty, has another length, or is a public sample key. When APP_ENV is development, local, test or testing, this is only a warning. Make one with dox key:generate. serverPort int 3000 The port the HTTP server listens on. When the env has no APP_PORT but has PORT, Dox listens on PORT instead (Cloud Run, Fly, Render and Heroku set it). host String? null: APP_HOST, else all interfaces The network interface to listen on, like 127.0.0.1. null reads the env var APP_HOST. With neither, Dox listens on all interfaces, IPv6 and IPv4 (::). totalIsolate int? Platform.numberOfProcessors Isolates (threads) that serve HTTP, all on the same port. On Windows the native server runs on one isolate. compress bool false gzip responses (HttpServer.autoCompress). Rust gzips on its own thread, not on the isolate. It still costs CPU on every response. Let a proxy do it when you have one. maxBodySize int 10 * 1024 * 1024 (10 MB) Biggest JSON or urlencoded body in bytes. Bigger gets 413. maxMultipartSize int 100 * 1024 * 1024 (100 MB) Biggest multipart/form-data body (file uploads) in bytes. Bigger gets 413. bodyTimeout Duration Duration(seconds: 120) A client that sends no body bytes for this long gets 408. A slow but steady upload is fine. Native server only. idleTimeout Duration Duration(seconds: 30) A keep-alive connection with no new request for this long is closed. A request head must also arrive in this time. Behind a load balancer, set it longer than the balancer's idle timeout. See Behind a load balancer. maxConnections int? null (no limit) The most connections one isolate holds open at once. Must be 1 or more. 0 or less throws an ArgumentError when the server starts. When it is full, new clients wait in the OS listen queue until a connection closes. WebSocket connections and connections that are still closing count too. The queue holds up to 1024 clients, and the OS can make it smaller (somaxconn; 128 by default on macOS). When the queue is full, new clients wait and then time out. On Linux each new client goes to one isolate (SO_REUSEPORT), so it can wait for a full isolate even when others have room. The whole app holds up to maxConnections * totalIsolate, so keep that below ulimit -n. Native server only. shutdownTimeout Duration Duration(seconds: 8) On SIGTERM or SIGINT, how long open requests may run before Dox closes them. Keep it below the kill timeout of your platform. See Graceful shutdown. trustedProxies List<String> [] IPs or CIDR ranges of reverse proxies. Only when the direct client is in this list does Dox read X-Forwarded-For for req.ip() and X-Forwarded-Proto for req.scheme(). ['*'] trusts any direct client, and takes the right-most X-Forwarded-For hop (the one the proxy added) as the client.

docs.title: Routing and request handling
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning container void Function(IocContainer)? null Fills the container: registerContainer from lib/generated/container.g.dart. Every isolate runs it. It also gives the routers, providers and model binders. See Dependency injection. routers List<Router> [] Routers to register first, in this order. Every other Router class comes from container. globalMiddleware List<dynamic> [] Middleware that runs on every route. A function or an IDoxMiddleware. dtos List<DtoSchema<Object>> [] Every DTO of the app: dtos from lib/generated/dtos.g.dart. Dox finds the DTO of a controller parameter and of req.validate<T>() with it. validationMessages MessageResolver? null (English messages) Messages for validation errors, for example in other languages. responseHandler ResponseHandlerInterface? null A class with DoxResponse handle(DoxResponse res). It sees every response before it is sent. exceptionHandler ExceptionHandler ExceptionHandler() Reports every unhandled error and turns it into a response. The default logs the error with Logger.warn and the stack with Logger.danger. See Error handling. htmlErrors bool false Sends an HTML error page to a request that does not want JSON (see DoxRequest.expectsJson()). In development or local the page also shows the error text and the stack. JSON clients, validation errors and ExceptionHandler.render answers do not change. See An HTML error page. errorPage String Function(int status, Object error, StackTrace stack, bool debug) defaultErrorPage Makes the HTML of the page. debug is true in development or local. Escape every value you put in the page. Used only with htmlErrors. providers List<DoxProvider> [] Providers to run first, in this order. Every other DoxProvider class comes from container. Dox runs them in every isolate at start. webSocketAllowedOrigins List<String>? null (no check) Turns on the Origin check for every Route.websocket route. Only pages of the same host and the listed sites, like https://app.example.com, can open a socket. Other origins get 403. [] means the same host only. allowedOrigins on a route wins over this. With null, any website can open a socket with the cookies of the user, and Dox prints one warning to stderr at start.

docs.title: Sub configs
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning cors CORSConfig CORSConfig() CORS headers. See CORSConfig. logger LoggerConfig LoggerConfig() The Logger output. See LoggerConfig. cache CacheConfig file store in storage/cache, plus a memory store Cache stores for Cache(). See CacheConfig. session SessionConfig cookie driver, cookie dox_session, 2 hours Settings for SessionMiddleware. See Session. openApi OpenApiConfig OpenApiConfig() /docs, /openapi.json and /openapi.yaml. See OpenApiConfig. flags CoreFlags CoreFlags() (all off) Opt-in core behaviors. See Core flags.

docs.title: Core flags
docs.text:
CoreFlags turns on opt-in behaviors. Every flag is off by default. Turn on the ones you want:

AppConfig(
  appKey: env.appKey,
  flags: const CoreFlags(onlyPresent: true, cookieDefaults: true),
);

CoreFlags.all() turns on every flag:

AppConfig(appKey: env.appKey, flags: const CoreFlags.all());
Flag When it is on laravelErrors A 422 body is {"message": "...", "errors": {"field": ["..."]}}, with all messages of each field. The message is the first error, plus (and N more errors). The OpenAPI ValidationError schema has this shape too. Off: {"field": "first message"}. onlyPresent req.only([...]) leaves out keys that are not in the input. So model.update(req.only([...])) does not write null for a field the client did not send. Off: a missing key is in the map with null. cookieDefaults A DoxCookie with no path gets Path=/, and one with no sameSite gets SameSite=Lax. A value you set wins. SameSite.none needs secure: true, or browsers drop the cookie. A cookie set before with no Path on a sub-path (like /auth) is not removed by an expire() that sends Path=/. Expire it with its old path. Off: no Path and no SameSite. hasKeyOnly req.has('x') is true when the key is there, with any value (also '' or null), like req.exists('x'). Dot keys work. Off: '' and null give false. htmlStrings A string from a controller is sent as text/html. A content type you set wins, also one a middleware set on the response. Only the preset text/plain; charset=utf-8 is changed, so a string with that type set by hand is sent as HTML too. To keep plain text, return response(text).contentType(ContentType.text). Escape user input in the string. Off: text/plain. replaceHeaders res.header(k, v) replaces a value of the header that a middleware put on the response before. Vary and Set-Cookie are lists, so they still get one more value. Off: it adds a second value. res.header(k, v, replace: true) or replace: false picks for one call. decryptServerError A DecryptException gives 500 with {"code": "server_error", "message": "Server Error"}, and the ExceptionHandler reports it. Off: 400 decrypt_failed, not reported. req.cookie() still gives null for a bad cookie. envExpand .env values can use ${OTHER}, and a "..." value reads \n, \t, \", \\ and \$. Also set Env.flags = flags; at the top of main() in bin/server.dart and in your tests, because .env is read before AppConfig exists. See Use one value in another. Off: values are read as written. cacheCopies Cache().store('x'), .tag() and .tags() give a new Cache, and the first one does not change. Off: they change the same object and give it back.

Each isolate builds its own AppConfig, so every isolate has the same flags. Dox reads a flag when the code runs, with Dox().flags.

The lock flag of the cache is in CacheConfig: CacheFlags.

docs.title: CORSConfig
docs.text:
Source: packages/dox-core/lib/interfaces/app_config.dart. Headers are set in packages/dox-core/lib/http/http_cors_handler.dart.

A value can be a String ('*' or a comma list) or a List<String>. A null value sends no header.

Field Type Default Header enabled bool true Send CORS headers. A route can override it with its own cors setting. origin dynamic null Access-Control-Allow-Origin. One origin, '*', or a list. With a list, Dox sends back only the request origin if it is in the list. methods dynamic null Access-Control-Allow-Methods headers dynamic null Access-Control-Allow-Headers exposeHeaders dynamic null Access-Control-Expose-Headers credentials bool? null Access-Control-Allow-Credentials maxAge num? null Access-Control-Max-Age in seconds

Note

With the default CORSConfig() every value is null. So enabled: true alone sends no header. Set origin at least.

docs.title: LoggerConfig
docs.text: Field Type Default Meaning name String '' Written as logger.name in each JSON log line. Left out when empty. enabled bool false Turn the Logger on. When it is false, LogMiddleware(enabled: true) does not turn request logs on. prettyPrint bool false true prints colored text. false prints one JSON object per line (for log services). The line has timestamp, status, message and logger.name. Keys of a Map you log are added at the top level. Other data goes under payload. LogMiddleware follows this setting too. level String 'info' The lowest level to print: debug, info, warn or error. Logger.success counts as info. Logger.danger counts as error. An unknown value prints every line.

docs.title: CacheConfig
docs.text:
Source: packages/dox-cache/lib/src/cache_config.dart. Option keys: packages/dox-cache/lib/src/constants/cache_constants.dart.

Field Type Default Meaning defaultStore String required The store Cache() uses when no store is named. stores Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>> required Store name to options. Each store needs a driver option. flags CacheFlags CacheFlags() (all off) Opt-in cache behaviors. See below.

CacheFlags has one flag. CacheFlags.all() turns it on.

Flag When it is on lockThrows lock.block(timeout) with no callback throws LockTimeoutException when the lock was not taken in time. Off: it gives false. Set lock.throwOnTimeout to pick for one lock. 
CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: 'redis',
  stores: stores,
  flags: const CacheFlags(lockThrows: true),
);

Options of each driver:

Driver Option Type Default Meaning all driver String required file, memory, redis or null all prefix String dox_cache: Text in front of every key. file path String storage/cache Folder of the cache files. memory max_size int no limit Most items in the map. redis host String 127.0.0.1 Redis host. redis port int 6379 Redis port. redis username String none Redis user. redis password String none Redis password. redis db int 0 Redis database number. redis tls bool false Use TLS. redis pool_size int 10 Most connections per store.

docs.title: StorageConfig
docs.text:
StorageProvider of the dox_storage package takes it. See File storage. Source: lib/src/dox/storage_config.dart in dartondox/dox-storage.

Field Type Default Meaning defaultDisk String 'local' The disk Storage() uses when no disk is named. disks Map<String, Map<String, dynamic>> {'local': {'driver': 'local', 'root': 'storage'}} Disk name to options. Each disk needs a driver option.

Options of each driver:

Driver Option Type Default Meaning all driver String required local, s3 or memory local root String storage Folder of the files. local url String none Base of the public URLs, like http://localhost:3000/files. local app_key String AppConfig.appKey Key that signs the URLs. local visibility String public public or private. local atomic_writes bool false Write to a temp file, then rename it. local permissions bool or Map off Visibility is the file mode. See File storage. s3 bucket String required Bucket name. s3 region String us-east-1 Region. s3 key String required Access key id. s3 secret String required Secret access key. s3 token String none Session token. s3 endpoint String none Custom endpoint (R2, MinIO, Spaces). s3 path_style bool false Use path style URLs. s3 url String none Base of the public URLs. s3 visibility String private public or private. s3 acl bool true The service supports ACLs. s3 batch_delete bool true The service supports batch delete.

An unknown driver throws ArgumentError('Storage disk "<name>" has unknown driver "<type>"').

docs.title: OpenApiConfig
docs.text:
Source: packages/dox-core/lib/openapi/openapi_config.dart.

Field Type Default Meaning enabled bool? null Serve the docs routes. null means: on only when APP_ENV is development or local. An empty APP_ENV counts as production. info Info Info(title: 'Dox API', version: '1.0.0') Title and version of the API. servers List<Server> [] Base URLs of the API. securitySchemes Map<String, SecurityScheme> {} Ways to log in, like {'bearerAuth': SecurityScheme.bearer()}. securityByMiddleware Map<String, List<Map<String, List<String>>>> {} Security for routes that use a middleware class with this name. It wins over @Security on the class. A class name that ends with AuthMiddleware gets bearerAuth when it has neither. registry OpenApiRegistry OpenApiRegistry() (empty) What dox_builder found in the code. Pass openApiRegistry from lib/generated/openapi.g.dart. ui DocsUi DocsUi.scalar scalar or swagger. scalar ScalarOptions ScalarOptions() Options of the Scalar page. See below. pageTitle String? null (uses info.title) Title of the /docs page. include List<String> [] (all routes) Only routes with these paths are in the docs, like ['/api/*']. A * at the end matches the rest of the path. exclude List<String> [] Routes with these paths are left out. Checked after include.

ScalarOptions (lib/src/docs_ui.dart in dartondox/dox-openapi):

Field Type Default Meaning theme ScalarTheme ScalarTheme.default_ One of default_, alternate, moon, purple, solarized, bluePlanet, deepSpace, saturn, kepler, elysiajs, fastify, mars, laserwave, none. darkMode bool false Start in dark mode. showDownloadButton bool true Show the download button for the OpenAPI document. proxyUrl String? null Send "Try it" requests through this proxy.

docs.title: SocketIoConfig
docs.text:
SocketIoProvider of the dox_socketio package takes it. See Socket.IO. Source: lib/src/dox/socket_io_config.dart in dartondox/dox-socketio.

Field Type Default Meaning enabled bool true Mount Socket.IO on the HTTP port at /socket.io/. options ServerOptions ServerOptions() Engine options. See below. namespaces List<NamespaceHandler> [] Namespaces to register, like ChatNamespace(). adapter SocketAdapterFactory? null (in memory with one isolate, IsolateAdapter with many) Makes the adapter in each isolate. Use a Redis adapter with many servers.

ServerOptions (lib/src/engine/server_options.dart in dox-socketio). The defaults match the Node.js server.

Field Type Default Meaning path String /socket.io/ URL path. Must end with /. pingInterval Duration 25 s Time between two server pings. pingTimeout Duration 20 s Time to wait for a pong before the session is closed. upgradeTimeout Duration 10 s Time a websocket upgrade may take. connectTimeout Duration 45 s Time a client has to join a namespace after the handshake. maxHttpBufferSize int 1000000 Biggest message in bytes a client may send. maxAttachments int 10 Most binary attachments in one packet. A packet with more closes that client. transports List<String> ['polling', 'websocket'] Allowed transports. allowUpgrades bool true Allow upgrades from polling to websocket. cors CorsOptions? null (no CORS headers) CORS for the long-polling requests.

CorsOptions:

Field Type Default Meaning origins List<String> ['*'] Allowed origins. credentials bool false Send Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. methods List<String> ['GET', 'POST'] Allowed methods for preflight. allowedHeaders List<String>? null (the requested headers) Allowed request headers. maxAge Duration? null How long a browser may cache the preflight answer.

docs.title: DatabaseConfig
docs.text:
The database is not a field of AppConfig. A provider calls SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig) in its setup(). Source: packages/dox-orm/lib/src/types/database_config.dart and connection_config.dart in dartondox/dox-orm.

Field Type Default Meaning connection String required Name of the connection to use. A missing name throws Exception('<name> not found'). connections Map<String, ConnectionConfig> required Connection name to config.

ConnectionConfig:

Field Type Default Meaning driver Driver required Driver.postgres, Driver.mysql (also MariaDB) or Driver.sqlite. host String 'localhost' Database host. Not used by sqlite. port int 0 Database port. Not used by sqlite. user String '' Database user. Not used by sqlite. password String '' Database password. Not used by sqlite. database String required Database name. For sqlite: the file path, or :memory:. useSSL bool false Use TLS. Postgres: mode require (no certificate check), set extra['sslMode'] to change it. MySQL: the certificate is checked. debug bool required Print every query with printer. printer QueryPrinter? null ConsoleQueryPrinter(), PrettyQueryPrinter(), FileQueryPrinter(file: File('queries.log')) or your own. FileQueryPrinter(file: ..., buffered: true) writes in the background, so a query does not wait for the disk. Then call await printer.flush() before exit(), or the last lines are lost. logRedact List<String> [] Names of values to hide in the query log. A value shows as *** when its key ends with one of these names, in any case. ['password', 'token'] hides password, users.password and remember_token. Only the log changes. The query gets the real values. The list of the default connection counts for every query. The list of a named connection counts too, for the queries on that connection. slowQueryMs int? null Log each query that takes longer than this many milliseconds, with printer. 0 logs every query. null turns it off. It works with debug off. Values named in logRedact show as ***. A failed query is not logged. read List<Map<String, dynamic>>? null Read replica hosts. Each map can change host, port, user, password, database and extra. See Read replicas. write Map<String, dynamic>? null Settings of the write host, in the same form as one read map. Only used with read. sticky bool false With read: after a write, the reads of the same request go to the write host. extra Map<String, dynamic> {} Driver options. See below. driverFactory DBDriver Function(ConnectionConfig)? null Your own driver class. It wins over every other setting.

Keys of extra:

Driver Key Type Default Meaning postgres, mysql maxConnectionCount int 10 Most open connections, for the whole process. postgres, mysql threads int 1 Rust threads of the native driver. Only the first pool sets it. postgres, mysql requestTimeout Duration 300 s The longest wait for one request (a free connection, the connect and the query). Over it, the request fails. postgres, mysql maxConnectionAge Duration none on Postgres, 12 hours on MySQL Close a connection older than this, once it has no query. postgres, mysql idleTimeout Duration no limit on Postgres, 12 hours on MySQL Close a free connection that is not used for this long. mysql serverKill bool true Stop a cancelled or timed out query on the server with KILL. Set false behind a proxy like ProxySQL. mysql, sqlite preparedStatementCacheSize int 100 Prepared statements kept per connection. postgres sslMode String require with useSSL, else disable TLS mode: disable, prefer, require or verify-full. postgres sslRootCert String none Path of a PEM file with the CA certificates to trust for verify-full. sslrootcert in DATABASE_URL. postgres sslWarning bool true false hides the warning that Dox prints (once per isolate) when TLS mode is require. sslWarning=false in DATABASE_URL works too. postgres timeZone String UTC Session time zone. postgres applicationName String none Name of the app in pg_stat_activity. mysql verifyCertificate bool true false skips the TLS certificate check. Only for a self-signed certificate in development. sqlite busyTimeout int 5000 PRAGMA busy_timeout in milliseconds. sqlite background bool false true (or 1, 'true', '1', so ?background=true in DATABASE_URL works) runs the queries in a helper isolate, so a slow query does not block the request isolate. Each query costs one message hop. See SQLite.

A time key takes a Duration, or a number of seconds. See Pool settings.

docs.title: AuthConfig
docs.text:
Auth is not a field of AppConfig. A provider calls Auth.initialize(AuthConfig(...)) in its setup(). Source: lib/src/interfaces.dart in dartondox/dox-auth.

Class Field Type Default Meaning AuthConfig defaultGuard String required The guard Auth() uses when no guard is named. AuthConfig guards Map<String, AuthGuard> {} Guard name to guard. AuthGuard driver AuthDriver required How a token is made and checked, like JwtAuthDriver(secret: SecretKey(...)). AuthGuard provider AuthProvider required Where users come from. AuthProvider model dynamic Function() required Makes the user model, like () => User(). AuthProvider identifierFields List<String> ['email'] Columns attempt() matches the login with. AuthProvider passwordField String 'password' Column with the bcrypt hash.

docs.title: Full example
docs.text:
The config files of a new project. They read their values from env, the typed env class in lib/config/env.dart (see Env reference).

lib/config/app.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/cache.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/cors.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/logger.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';
import 'package:my_app/generated/container.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  /// Changing the key makes old cookies and encrypted data unreadable.
  appKey: env.appKey,
  serverPort: env.appPort,
  totalIsolate: env.appTotalIsolate ?? Platform.numberOfProcessors,
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    LogMiddleware(enabled: env.appEnv != 'production'),
  ],
  container: registerContainer,
  cache: cache,
  cors: cors,
  logger: logger,
);
lib/config/cache.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

CacheConfig cache = CacheConfig(
  defaultStore: env.cacheStore,
  stores: <String, Map<String, dynamic>>{
    'file': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'file', 'path': 'storage/cache'},

    /// one map per isolate, fast, not shared
    'memory': <String, dynamic>{'driver': 'memory', 'max_size': 10000},
  },
);
lib/config/logger.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

LoggerConfig logger = LoggerConfig(
  name: env.appName,
  enabled: true,
  level: env.logLevel,
  /// colored text is slow. JSON lines in production.
  prettyPrint: env.isDevelopment,
);
lib/config/database.dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/env.dart';

/// Print every SQL query only in development.
bool _debug = env.isDevelopment;

DatabaseConfig databaseConfig = DatabaseConfig(
  connection: env.dbConnection,
  connections: <String, ConnectionConfig>{
    'postgres': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.postgres,
      host: env.dbHost,
      port: env.dbPort ?? 5432,
      user: env.dbUsername,
      password: env.dbPassword,
      database: env.dbName,
      extra: <String, dynamic>{
        /// One pool for all isolates.
        'maxConnectionCount': 10,
        'maxConnectionAge': Duration(hours: 1),
      },
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),

    /// MySQL and MariaDB
    'mysql': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.mysql,
      host: env.dbHost,
      port: env.dbPort ?? 3306,
      user: env.dbUsername,
      password: env.dbPassword,
      database: env.dbName,
      extra: <String, dynamic>{'collation': 'utf8mb4_general_ci'},
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),

    /// `DB_NAME` is a file path, or `:memory:`.
    'sqlite': ConnectionConfig(
      driver: Driver.sqlite,
      database: env.dbName,
      debug: _debug,
      printer: PrettyQueryPrinter(),
    ),
  },
);
lib/config/cors.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

CORSConfig cors = CORSConfig(
  enabled: false,
  // a list: Dox sends back the request origin only when it is in the list
  origin: <String>['http://localhost:3000'],
  methods: <String>['GET', 'HEAD', 'POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE'],
  headers: <String>[
    'accept',
    'authorization',
    'content-type',
    'x-csrf-token',
    'x-xsrf-token',
    'x-requested-with',
  ],
  exposeHeaders: <String>[
    'cache-control',
    'content-language',
    'content-type',
    'expires',
    'last-modified',
    'pragma',
  ],
  credentials: true,
  maxAge: 90,
);

Do not use origin: '*' together with credentials: true. With credentials the browser sends cookies, so it does not accept *, and the call fails. Dox does not send back any origin in place of *, because that would let every site call the app with the user's cookies. '*' is fine for a public API with credentials: false (or not set).

lib/providers/orm_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';
import 'package:my_app/config/database.dart';

/// Dox finds it by itself and runs it in every isolate.
/// No database? Delete this file.
class ORMProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  Future<void> setup() async {
    SqlQueryBuilder.initializeWithDatabaseConfig(databaseConfig);
  }

  @override
  Future<void> shutdown() async {
    await SqlQueryBuilder.close();
  }
}

A new project also has lib/config/storage.dart, queue.dart and schedule.dart, with a provider for each in lib/providers/. See File storage, Queue and Scheduler.

A new project has no openapi.dart, socketio.dart or auth provider. You add them when you need them. See OpenAPI, Socket.IO and Authentication.

Path What is in it bin/server.dart starts the app: Dox().initialize(), migrations, Dox().startServer() bin/migrate.dart runs migrations for dox migration:* bin/seed.dart runs seeders for dox db:seed bin/queue.dart the queue worker for dox queue:* bin/schedule.dart the scheduler for dox schedule:* bin/openapi.dart you add it: writes the OpenAPI files for dox openapi:generate lib/config/ app.dart (AppConfig), env.dart, database.dart, cors.dart, cache.dart, storage.dart, logger.dart, queue.dart, schedule.dart. docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong');
  }
}
Code Does Route.get('/blogs', (C c) => c.index) controller C from the container. Also post, put, patch, delete, options Route.get('/blogs', listBlogs) a plain function Route.post('/blogs', c.store, body: schema) body: is for the docs only. It checks nothing. Route.get('/blogs/{id}', c.show) path param. show(int id) Route.get('/posts/{page?}', c.list) optional param. list(int? page) Route.get('/docs/{path*}', c.page) rest of the path, with / Route.get('/me', <dynamic>[AuthMiddleware(), c.me]) middleware first, controller last Route.match(<String>['GET', 'POST'], '/contact', handler) one handler for a list of methods Route.any('/webhook', handler) one handler for GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE Route.redirect('/home', '/') / Route.permanentRedirect('/old', '/new') send a path to another URL. 302 by default, 301 for permanentRedirect. Route.get('/users/{id}', c.show).where('id', '[0-9]+') the route matches only when the param fits the regex Route.fallback((DoxRequest req) { ... }) answers a GET or HEAD request that matches no route and no static file. Use it for a 404 page or an SPA. globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[const MethodOverride()] lets an HTML form reach PUT, PATCH and DELETE routes Route.group('/blogs', () { ... }) prefix. Dox adds the / between parts. Route.middleware(<dynamic>[M()], () { ... }) middleware for a group Route.domain('api.app.com', () { ... }) match by Host Route.resource('blogs', BlogController) index, create, store, show, edit, update, destroy Route.health('/health') 200 {"status": "ok"}, or 503 when a check fails. See Health check. Route.staticFiles('/', 'public') serve a folder (CSS, JS, images) when no route matches. maxAge: sets Cache-Control Storage.route('files') serve a storage disk. Only signed URLs work, unless signed: false (dox_storage) Route.enabledCors(() { ... }) / Route.disabledCors(...) CORS for some routes Route.websocket('echo', (WebSocket s, DoxRequest req) { ... }) a raw WebSocket. For rooms and acks, use Socket.IO.

Controller parameters, by type: DoxRequest, one @Dto class, String/int/double/num/bool for path params (by position), a @DoxModel (loaded by its key), an @Inject() class. Only positional parameters.

In the examples, c.index and the like are methods of a controller C from the container.

docs.text:
@Inject()                       // one instance per isolate
class PostService {
  PostService(this.posts);      // from the container, by type
  final PostRepository posts;
}

@Inject(singleton: false)       // a new instance each time
class Clock {}

AppConfig(container: registerContainer); // from lib/generated/container.g.dart

Dox().ioc.get<PostService>();
Dox().ioc.override<PostRepository>(FakePostRepository()); // tests

Routers and DoxProvider classes are found without @Inject(). Run dart run build_runner build after a change. See Dependency injection.

Middleware order: globalMiddleware, router middleware, group, route.

See Routing, Controller, Middleware.

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text:
class ApiKeyMiddleware implements IDoxMiddleware {
  @override
  dynamic handle(IDoxRequest req) {
    String apiKey = Env.get<String>('API_KEY');
    // Hash.equals: constant time, so the time does not leak the key
    if (apiKey.isEmpty || !Hash.equals(req.header('X-Api-Key') ?? '', apiKey)) {
      return response('no').statusCode(401); // stop here
    }
    return req; // go on
  }
}
Middleware Does const RequestId() X-Request-Id header, req.requestId const ETag() ETag header, 304 when If-None-Match matches RequestTimeout(Duration(seconds: 30)) or Route.get(...).timeout(...) 503 when the route is too slow const ServerTiming() Server-Timing header; ServerTiming.add('db', d) adds a time. Development or trusted clients only const ValidateSignature() 403 unless the url is from Route.signedUrl(...) implements IDoxTerminableMiddleware terminate(req, res) runs after the answer is sent

See Middleware and Signed URLs.

docs.text:

Needs trustedProxies behind a proxy. req.userAgent() / req.host() / req.origin() / req.locale more headers req.isJson() / req.isFormData() content type req.auth?.user<User>() logged in user (after AuthMiddleware) req.auth?.id() / req.auth == null user id, or true for a guest req.method / req.uri method and URI

@Dto()
class CreateBlog {
  @Length(min: 3, max: 200)
  @Trim()
  final String title;

  final String? body;            // nullable = optional
  final Status status;           // enum = only its names

  const CreateBlog({required this.title, this.body, this.status = Status.draft});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateBlog> schema = $CreateBlogDto;

(only the JSON Schema description) Class @Dto(source: Source.query, keyCase: KeyCase.field, strict: true, messages: {...})

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
@DoxModel(table: 'blogs', softDelete: true)
class Blog extends BlogGenerator {
  @Column()
  String? title;

  @Column(name: 'user_id')
  int? userId;

  @BelongsTo(User)
  User? user;

  @HasMany(Comment)
  List<Comment> comments = <Comment>[];

  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['secret'];
}
Code Does await Blog().find(1) / find('slug', 'a') one row or null await Blog().all() every row that matches where await Blog().where('status', 'live').get() rows that match await Blog().where('id', '>', 5).getFirst() first match or null await Blog().findOrFail(1) / firstOrFail() the row, or throws ModelNotFoundException await Blog().count() int await Blog().where('slug', s).hasRows() / hasNoRows() bool await Blog().pluck('title') / valueOf('title') one column of all rows / of the first row await Blog().sum('views'), avg, min, max one value, null when no row await Blog().paginate(currentPage: 1, perPage: 20) Pagination<Blog>, rows in data await Blog().simplePaginate(currentPage: 1, perPage: 20) a page without the total count await Blog().cursorPaginate(perPage: 20, cursor: c) a page after a cursor, nextCursor await Blog().create(<String, dynamic>{'title': 'a'}) insert and return the model await Blog().firstOrCreate({...}, {...}), firstOrNew, updateOrCreate find, or create blog.title = 'b'; await blog.save() insert or update await blog.delete() soft delete when softDelete: true. Returns the deleted rows as an int. await blog.increment('views') / decrement change a number in one query await Blog().forceCreate({...}) create with every key, ignore fillable await Model.unguarded(() async { ... }) turn off the fillable check inside the callback await blog.sync('tags', <int>[1, 2]) many to many: make the links exactly these ids await blog.attach('tags', 3) / await blog.detach('tags', 3) add / remove links await blog.forceDelete() / await blog.restore() real delete / undo soft delete Blog().withTrash() include soft deleted rows Blog().onlyTrashed() only soft deleted rows await blog.touch() set updated_at to now, touchQuietly() with no events blog.replicate() a new unsaved copy of the model Blog().preload('comments').get() load a relation, one query Blog().whereHas('comments').get() / whereDoesntHave / has('comments', '>=', 3) filter by a relation await blog.$getRelation('user') load a relation on one model blog.related<Comment>('comments')?.where(...).get() relation query blog.toJson() / blog.toMap() map, hidden left out of toJson() Blog().query() a new, empty query

Relations: @HasOne(T), @HasMany(T), @BelongsTo(T), @ManyToMany(T). Polymorphic: @MorphMany(T, 'name'), @MorphOne(T, 'name'), @MorphTo(). Options: foreignKey, localKey, onQuery, eager.

Events: override onCreating(), onCreated(), onSaving(), onUpdated(), onDeleting(), ... or Model.observe<Blog>(BlogObserver()). throw CancelModelEvent('why') in a "before" event stops it. saveQuietly() skips events.

See Model, Events, HasMany, Query by relations.

docs.title: Query builder
docs.text:
List<Map<String, dynamic>> rows = await QueryBuilder.table('blogs')
    .select(<String>['id', 'title'])
    .where('status', 'live')
    .orWhere('views', '>', 100)
    .whereIn('id', <int>[1, 2, 3])
    .whereNull('deleted_at')
    .join('users', 'users.id', 'blogs.user_id')
    .orderBy('id', 'desc')
    .limit(10)
    .offset(20)
    .get();

@DoxEnv()
abstract class AppEnv {

class ChatNamespace extends NamespaceHandler {
  @override
  String get path => '/chat';

  @override
  void onConnection(Socket socket) {
    socket.join('lobby');
    socket.on('chat', onChat);
  }

  void onChat(SocketEvent event) {
    event.socket.to('lobby').emit('chat', event.data);
    event.ack('ok');
  }
}

Log users in at connect time with SocketAuth(findUser).handle in middleware. The user is in socket.user.

Turn it on with a SocketIoProvider (extend it in lib/). With many isolates, clients use transports: ['websocket']. Broadcasts reach every isolate with no Redis; many servers need the Redis adapter.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Every dox command, with its options and the files it writes.

The CLI lives in the dox-cli repo. The paths below are in that repo. The commands come from lib/src/command_registry.dart. The file templates are Dart strings inside lib/src/tools/. The path of each template is given below.

How to install the CLI is on the Dox CLI page.

Rules that apply to every command:

  • dox with no command prints Could not find a command. Run `dox help` for more information. and exits with code 1.
  • An unknown command prints Could not find a command named "<name>". Run `dox help` for more information., and a hint about the dox: commands: key. It exits with code 1.
  • A command that is not built in can come from a package or from the app. See Package commands.
  • Too few or too many arguments prints Invalid number of arguments for command "<name>". with the expected count.
  • A name you pass is turned into snake_case for the file and PascalCase for the class. BlogPost and blog_post give the same result.
  • Many make:* commands also answer to a create:* name, like create:model. dox help <command> shows the aliases.
  • A make:* command does not overwrite. When the file exists it prints <name> already exists and stops.

docs.title: dox create
docs.text:
dox create <project_name> [--version <version>]

Makes a new project from the dox-sample repo.

Option Meaning --version <v> (or --v) A release tag of dox-sample to clone. Without it, the newest dox-sample release with the same major version as the CLI is used.

What it does:

  1. Turns the name into snake_case. Stops with Folder name "<name>" already exist when the folder is there.
  2. Picks the release (see --version above) from the release list of dartondox/dox-sample.
  3. Runs git clone --depth 1 --branch v<version> https://github.com/dartondox/dox-sample.git <name>.
  4. Deletes the .git folder.
  5. Replaces dox_sample with your project name in every text file, except files under bin/dox.
  6. Copies .env.example to .env and writes a new random APP_KEY to it, like dox key:generate. It skips this step when .env is already there.
  7. Prints the next steps: cd <name>, dart pub get and dox serve.

Needs curl and git on the PATH. When it can not find a release (no network), it prints Could not find a template release for Dox <version>. Check your network, or pass --version.

The new project already has bin/server.dart, bin/migrate.dart, bin/seed.dart, bin/queue.dart and bin/schedule.dart. So the migration, seed, queue and schedule commands below work in it right away.

Source: lib/src/tools/create_project.dart.

docs.title: dox add
docs.text:
dox add <package> [--dev] [options]

Adds a Dox package and sets it up. orm is short for dox_orm. It runs dart pub add, then dart pub get, then the <package>:install command of the package with the options, like dox add orm --driver=postgres. A package with no <package>:install command is only added. See Add a package.

Source: lib/src/tools/add_package.dart.

docs.title: dox serve
docs.text:
dox serve [--ignore-build-runner]
dox s
dox server

Starts the dev server.

dox serve --port=... does not set the port. Dox ignores it and prints a warning. Set APP_PORT in .env, or run APP_PORT=9000 dox serve.

Option Meaning --ignore-build-runner Do not start dart run build_runner watch.

What it does:

  1. Starts dart run build_runner watch (unless the option is set).
  2. Starts dart run bin/server.dart and prints its output.
  3. Watches the project folder. When a .dart file changes it prints [Dox] File changed: <file>. It waits until no file changed for 500 ms, then kills the server and starts it again.

Source: lib/src/tools/server_serve.dart.

docs.title: dox build
docs.text:
dox build

AOT compiles the app for production into build/bundle. Use this in production, not dart run.

What it does:

  1. When pubspec.yaml contains build_runner: runs dart run build_runner build. Stops with exit code 1 when it fails.
  2. Runs dart build cli --target bin/server.dart --output build.
  3. When bin/queue.dart or bin/schedule.dart exists: builds it the same way, to build/bundle/bin/queue and build/bundle/bin/schedule.
  4. Deletes the old build/bundle/db, then copies db/ to build/bundle/db. It leaves out SQLite files (*.sqlite, *.sqlite3, *.db, and their -wal, -shm, -journal and .lock files), so your local data does not go to production.
  5. Copies .env.example to build/bundle/.env.example.
  6. Prints [Dox] Built build/bundle. Run it with: cd build/bundle && ./bin/server.

Output:

Path What build/bundle/bin/server the native binary, no Dart SDK needed build/bundle/bin/queue the queue worker, when bin/queue.dart exists build/bundle/bin/schedule the scheduler, when bin/schedule.dart exists build/bundle/lib/ native libraries from build hooks (SQLite, dox_http_native, ...) build/bundle/db/ your migrations and seeders. SQLite files are not copied. build/bundle/.env.example copy it to .env or set real env vars

dart compile exe can not build packages with build hooks, so the CLI uses dart build cli.

Source: lib/src/tools/server_serve.dart (buildServer).

docs.title: dox build_runner:build and dox build_runner:watch
docs.text:
dox build_runner:build
dox build_runner:watch

Run dart run build_runner build once, or dart run build_runner watch. No options. build_runner:build prints only the first line of each output block of build_runner. Run dart run build_runner build yourself to see all of it. The CLI does not pass --delete-conflicting-outputs (build_runner removed that flag).

docs.title: dox key:generate
docs.text:
dox key:generate [--show] [--force]

Makes a 32 character key (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, from Random.secure()) and writes it to APP_KEY in .env. Prints <key> : Key have been updated successfully in .env!.

Option Meaning --show Print a new key and write nothing. --force Skip the question below.

When APP_ENV=production, a new key logs every user out. In a terminal the command asks first. Without a terminal it prints a warning and runs. If you answer no, it prints Stopped. APP_KEY was not changed. and exits with code 1.

What it does with .env:

  • Reads .env in the current folder. The file must exist, else the command fails with a file error.
  • Replaces the value of APP_KEY. Every other line stays as it is, in the same order. This keeps comments, blank lines, quotes and values with more than one = (like DATABASE_URL=postgres://u:p@h/db?a=b).
  • Adds APP_KEY=<key> as the first line when there is no APP_KEY.

Source: lib/src/tools/generate_key.dart.

docs.title: dox env:generate
docs.text:
dox env:generate

Writes lib/config/env.dart, the typed env class, from .env.example.

  • Stops with .env.example is missing. (exit code 1) when there is no example file.
  • Stops with lib/config/env.dart is already there. Delete it to make it again. (exit code 1) when the file exists.
  • Prints Run `dart run build_runner build` to make env.g.dart. when done.

Rules for each key: a whole number (like 3000 or -1) gives int get x => <value>;, true/false give bool get x => <value>;, an empty value gives String? get x;, any other value gives String get x; (required, no default). # comment lines above a key become its doc comment. A key that does not map back from camelCase gets @EnvKey('KEY').

Source: lib/src/tools/env_tools.dart (EnvScaffold).

docs.title: dox env:check
docs.text:
dox env:check

Loads AppEnv from lib/config/env.dart with the real environment and .env. Prints The env is valid. or an EnvException with every missing or bad key (exit code 1).

It writes a small script to .dart_tool/dox/env_check.dart and runs it with dart run. It needs lib/config/env.dart and a name: in pubspec.yaml. Without lib/config/env.dart it prints lib/config/env.dart is missing. Run `dox env:generate` first. (exit code 1).

Source: lib/src/tools/env_tools.dart (envCheck).

docs.title: dox openapi:generate
docs.text:
dox openapi:generate [dir]

Runs dart run bin/openapi.dart [dir]. That file writes openapi.json and openapi.yaml into dir (default storage/openapi). A new project has no bin/openapi.dart. You add it yourself, see OpenAPI. When the file is not there, the command prints bin/openapi.dart is missing. and the code to put in it (exit code 1).

Source: lib/src/tools/openapi_generate.dart.

docs.title: dox update
docs.text:
dox update

Installs the newest CLI with the same major version as the one you have. It reads the version list from pub.dev (retracted versions are skipped), then runs dart pub global activate dox <version>. Needs curl on the PATH.

Source: lib/src/tools/update_dox.dart.

docs.title: dox version
docs.text:
dox version
dox v
dox -v
dox --version

Prints Dox version: <version>. Aliases: --version, -version, v, -v, --v.

docs.title: dox help
docs.text:
dox help [command]
dox --help
dox -h

Aliases: --help, -h. Without a command: lists every command by category. With a command: prints its usage, description, category, aliases and argument count.

docs.title: dox make:controller
docs.text:
dox make:controller <name> [-r|--resource] [--api] [--model=<model>]

Alias: create:controller. Some other make:* commands have a create:* alias too. The Command list table at the end shows which.

Option Meaning -r or --resource A resource controller with index, create, store, show, edit, update, destroy. --api A resource controller without create and edit, the two form pages. Route.resource makes no route for them. --model=<model> or --model <model> A resource controller that uses the model. It imports package:<app>/app/models/<model>/<model>.model.dart. index returns all rows, and store creates a row from req.body. show, edit, update and destroy take the model as a parameter, so route model binding loads it by the {id}.

--api and --model work together. Each one makes a resource controller, also without -r. With --model, the CLI prints a warning when the model file does not exist yet. Any other option prints Unknown option <x> for make:controller. (exit code 1), and no file is made.

A trailing Controller in the name is removed: UserController and User give the same file.

Form Writes Template plain lib/app/http/controllers/<name>.controller.dart _getSample in lib/src/tools/create_controller.dart -r, --api, --model lib/app/http/controllers/<name>.controller.dart _getResourceSample in the same file

The class has @Inject(), so the container makes it. A comment shows the route to add, like Route.get('path', (BlogController c) => c.index);. A resource controller gets Route.resource('path', BlogController);. After the file is made, the CLI tells you to run dart run build_runner build. That adds the controller to lib/generated/container.g.dart.

docs.title: dox make:middleware
docs.text:
dox make:middleware <name>

Writes lib/app/http/middleware/<name>.middleware.dart: a class <Name>Middleware implements IDoxMiddleware with a handle(IDoxRequest req) that returns req. A trailing Middleware in the name is removed.

Template: _getSample in lib/src/tools/create_middleware.dart.

docs.title: dox make:dto
docs.text:
dox make:dto <name>

Writes lib/app/dtos/<name>/<name>.dto.dart: a @Dto() class with one name field and part '<name>.dto.g.dart';. The class name has no Dto at the end: dox make:dto CreateBlog gives the class CreateBlog in lib/app/dtos/create_blog/create_blog.dto.dart. A trailing Dto in the name is removed. Prints Run `dox build_runner:build` to make <name>/<name>.dto.g.dart.

Template: _getSample in lib/src/tools/create_dto.dart.

docs.title: dox make:serializer
docs.text:
dox make:serializer <name>

Writes lib/app/serializers/<name>.serializer.dart: a class <Name>Serializer extends Serializer<<Name>>. It imports the model with package:<app>/app/models/<name>/<name>.model.dart. A trailing Serializer in the name is removed.

Template: _getSample in lib/src/tools/create_serializer.dart.

docs.title: dox make:provider
docs.text:
dox make:provider <name>

Writes lib/providers/<name>_provider.dart: a class <Name>Provider extends DoxProvider with an empty setup() and an optional shutdown(). A trailing Provider in the name is removed: dox make:provider Cache gives CacheProvider in lib/providers/cache_provider.dart. Prints Run `dox build_runner:build` to add it to the container. Dox finds the provider after that. See Providers.

Template: createProvider in lib/src/tools/make_files.dart.

docs.title: dox make:command
docs.text:
dox make:command <name>

Writes lib/app/commands/<name>_command.dart: a class <Name>Command extends Command. Its name is app:<name>, and _ in the name becomes -. So dox make:command send_report makes the command app:send-report. A trailing Command in the name is removed.

It also does two more things:

  • It adds the class to the commands list in lib/app/commands/commands.dart. It makes that file when it is missing.
  • It adds commands: package:<app>/app/commands/commands.dart under dox: in pubspec.yaml, when that key is not set.

Then it prints Run `dart pub get`, then `dox app:send-report`.

It makes all the changes or none. When pubspec.yaml or commands.dart is not in the shape it expects, it prints what to add by hand, exits with code 1 and writes nothing. When dox: commands: already points to another library, it does the same.

See Package commands.

Template: createCommand in lib/src/tools/make_files.dart.

docs.title: dox make:mail
docs.text:
dox make:mail <name> [--no-view]
Form Writes plain lib/app/mail/<name>_mail.dart and the view resources/views/emails/<name>.dox.html --no-view lib/app/mail/<name>_mail.dart only, with a plain text body

The class is <Name>Mail extends Mailable. It takes the recipient Address in its constructor. A comment shows how to send it and how to queue it. A trailing Mail in the name is removed. With the view, the mail has view set to emails/<name> and a data map with name. With --no-view, it has a text getter. It makes both files or none.

After it writes the files, it prints a hint for each package that pubspec.yaml does not have yet: dox_mailer, and dox_view when there is a view. With a view, it also prints that the default view settings work (resources/views), and that you only add a ViewProvider with a ViewConfig to change them.

See Mail.

Template: createMail in lib/src/tools/make_files.dart.

docs.title: dox make:view
docs.text:
dox make:view <name>

Writes resources/views/<name>.dox.html with a small sample: <h1>Hello, {{ name }}</h1>. A name with / makes a folder: dox make:view emails/welcome writes resources/views/emails/welcome.dox.html. Each part of the name becomes snake_case: Pages/About gives resources/views/pages/about.dox.html.

See Views.

Template: createView in lib/src/tools/make_files.dart.

docs.title: dox make:test
docs.text:
dox make:test <name> [--unit]
Form Writes plain test/<name>_test.dart that starts the app with DoxTestClient and checks GET /ping for status 200. Change the path to match your route. --unit test/<name>_test.dart with a plain package:test test. It does not start the app.

A trailing Test in the name is removed.

See Testing.

Template: createTest in lib/src/tools/make_files.dart.

docs.title: dox make:model
docs.text:
dox make:model <name> [-m] [-c] [-r] [-f] [-s] [-a] [--api]
dox create:model <name> [-m] [-c] [-r] [-f] [-s] [-a] [--api]

Writes lib/app/models/<name>/<name>.model.dart: a @DoxModel(table: '<plural snake name>') class with part '<name>.model.g.dart';. BlogPost gives blog_posts. The class has an empty fillable list. Add your columns to it.

Option Meaning -m or --migration Also make a create_<table>_table migration. -c or --controller Also make a plain controller, <name>.controller.dart. -r or --resource Also make a resource controller that uses the model. --api Also make a resource controller without create and edit, that uses the model. -f or --factory Also make a factory, db/factories/<name>.factory.dart. -s or --seed Also make a seeder, db/seeders/<name>.seeder.dart. -a or --all Also make the migration, the factory, the seeder and a resource controller.

You can join short options: -mcr is the same as -m -c -r. With -c and -r together, the controller is a resource controller.

Each extra file is the same as the one from the single command:

Command Same file as dox make:model Post -m dox make:migration create_posts_table dox make:model Post -c dox make:controller Post dox make:model Post -r dox make:controller Post -r --model=Post dox make:model Post --api dox make:controller Post --api --model=Post dox make:model Post -f dox make:factory Post dox make:model Post -s dox make:seeder Post

When the model file exists, the command prints <Name> model already exists and makes no other file. When one of the other files exists, that file is skipped, the same as with its own command. Any other option prints Unknown option <x> for make:model. (exit code 1), and no file is made.

Template: _getSample in lib/src/tools/create_model.dart.

docs.title: dox make:migration
docs.text:
dox make:migration <name> [--sql]
dox create:migration <name> [--sql]
Option Meaning --sql Make a .sql file with -- up and -- down sections instead of a Dart class.

Writes db/migration/<yyyy>_<mm>_<dd>_<hhmmss>_<name>.dart (or .sql). Characters that are not letters, digits or _ are removed from the name. A second argument other than --sql is ignored.

Migrations run sorted by file name. So the new file always sorts after every file already in db/migration. When the current time is not later than the newest file (for example, two migrations in the same second), it uses the newest time plus 1 second.

For a Dart migration it also:

  • writes db/migration/migrations.dart, the registry of every Dart migration in the folder, sorted by name. A file with no class that extends Migration is skipped with a warning;
  • writes bin/migrate.dart when it is missing, and prints bin/migrate.dart created.

The Dart template depends on the name:

Name up() down() create_<table>_table schema.create('<table>', ...) with id() and timestamps() schema.dropIfExists('<table>') <x>_to_<table>_table (also from, in, on) schema.table('<table>', ...) schema.table('<table>', ...) anything else a comment a comment

Templates: dartMigrationSource, migrateEntrySource and _sampleSql in lib/src/tools/create_migration.dart.

docs.title: dox route:list
docs.text:
dox route:list [--json]

Prints every route of the app: method, path, name, handler and middleware. Run it in the app folder.

METHOD  PATH           NAME  HANDLER             MIDDLEWARE
GET     /api/ping            ApiController.pong  LogMiddleware
GET     /ping                WebController.pong  LogMiddleware
GET     /docs                serve
GET     /openapi.json        serve
GET     /openapi.yaml        serve

5 routes
Option Meaning --json Print the same data as one JSON list. 
dox route:list --json

[{"method":"GET","path":"/api/ping","name":null,"handler":"ApiController.pong","middleware":["LogMiddleware"]}]

Each item has method, path, name, handler and middleware. The example shows the first route only.

How to read the table:

  • A controller route shows Controller.method. A function shows its name, or Closure when it has none.
  • Fallback routes have the method FALLBACK. Handlers added with Route.mount have the method MOUNT.
  • A Route.websocket route shows WebSocket as its handler.
  • A route with a domain shows the domain in front of the path.

It does not start the server. It writes a small script to .dart_tool/dox/route_list.dart and runs it. The script loads the routes of your routers with Dox().loadRoutes().

Providers do not run. A route that a provider adds in setup() is not in the list. The Socket.IO mount is one example.

Your dox_core must have Dox().loadRoutes().

Errors go to stderr, so --json output stays clean for scripts. Without a Dox app in the folder, or with an unknown option, the command exits with code 1.

Source: lib/src/tools/route_list.dart.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
All migration:* commands work the same way:

  1. When bin/migrate.dart exists: write the registry again, then run dart run bin/migrate.dart <command> [args]. Your app code runs, so Dart migrations work.
  2. When there is no bin/migrate.dart but db/migration has Dart files: write bin/migrate.dart (the same text as make:migration writes, and print bin/migrate.dart created.), then go on like step 1. This happens after a package command like dox queue:table wrote the first Dart migration.
  3. Else: run the .sql migrations with Migrator() from dox_migration in the CLI process.

The database comes from DATABASE_URL when it is set. Else it comes from DB_CONNECTION, DB_HOST, DB_PORT, DB_USERNAME, DB_PASSWORD and DB_DATABASE (or DB_NAME). See Environment variables. A failed run prints the error and sets exit code 1.

Command Aliases What it does dox migration:run dox migrate Run the migrations that did not run yet. dox migration:rollback [--step=<count>] [--batch=<number>] [--force] dox migrate:rollback Undo the last batch, the last <count> migrations, or only batch <number>. --step 2 and --batch 3 work too. Give --step or --batch, not both. Any other option prints Invalid option <x>, use --step=<count>, --batch=<number> or --force (exit code 1). dox migration:reset dox migrate:reset Undo every migration. dox migration:refresh dox migrate:refresh Undo every migration, then run them all again. dox migration:fresh dox migrate:fresh Drop every table, then run all migrations. dox migration:status dox migrate:status Print which migrations ran, and their batch.

--seed after migration:run, migration:refresh or migration:fresh runs dox db:seed when the migrations end well.

--force after migration:rollback, migration:reset, migration:refresh or migration:fresh skips the question they ask when APP_ENV=production and stdin is a terminal. Without a terminal they print a warning and run.

bin/migrate.dart takes the same commands: dart run bin/migrate.dart <run|rollback [--step=n|--batch=n]|reset|refresh|fresh|status>. With no command it runs run.

docs.title: Factories and seeders
docs.text:
Command Aliases What it does dox make:factory <model> dox create:factory Make db/factories/<model>.factory.dart. It imports the model with the package name of pubspec.yaml. dox make:seeder <name> dox create:seeder Make db/seeders/<name>.seeder.dart. It writes db/seeders/seeders.dart again, and makes bin/seed.dart when it is missing. dox db:seed [--class=<name>] Write db/seeders/seeders.dart again, then run dart run bin/seed.dart [--class=<name>]. Default seeder: DatabaseSeeder. --class <name> (with a space) works too. When bin/seed.dart is missing, it prints bin/seed.dart is missing. (exit code 1).

docs.title: Queue
docs.text:
These commands run the app script bin/queue.dart with dart run. A new project already has it. It uses the dox_queue package. Input, output and errors go straight to your terminal. Ctrl+C (SIGINT) and SIGTERM are sent on to the script, so a worker can finish its job and stop. The exit code of the script is the exit code of dox. When bin/queue.dart is missing, the command prints how to set it up and exits with code 1.

Command Runs What it does dox make:job <name> Make lib/app/jobs/<name>.job.dart with a @Job() class that extends DoxJob. A trailing Job in the name is removed. Make bin/queue.dart when it is missing. Print a hint to add dox_queue to pubspec.yaml when it is not there, and to run dox build_runner:build (it makes lib/generated/jobs.g.dart). dox queue:work [flags] bin/queue.dart work [flags] Run the worker. dox queue:failed bin/queue.dart failed List the failed jobs. dox queue:retry <id\|all> bin/queue.dart retry <id\|all> Put one failed job, or all of them, back on the queue. dox queue:forget <id> bin/queue.dart forget <id> Delete one failed job. dox queue:flush bin/queue.dart flush Delete all failed jobs. dox queue:clear [queue] bin/queue.dart clear [queue] Delete the jobs of a queue. The default queue is default. dox queue:restart bin/queue.dart restart Make the running workers stop after their current jobs. The workers must share the cache store. dox queue:prune-failed [--hours=N] bin/queue.dart prune-failed [--hours=N] Delete failed jobs older than N hours. The default is 24. dox queue:table A package command of dox_queue_database. Make db/migration/<time>_create_queue_tables.dart, which calls QueueTables.up, QueueTables.upBatches and the matching down methods. When a create_queue_tables migration is already there, it prints so and exits with code 1. dox auth:tokens-table A package command of dox_auth. Make a migration for the auth_access_tokens table. When a create_access_tokens_table migration is already there, it prints so and exits with code 1.

Flags of queue:work, passed on as they are:

Flag Default Meaning --queue=a,b default The queues to read, the first one first. --concurrency=N 1 How many jobs run at the same time in this process. --once off Run one job, then stop. --tries=N 1 How many times a job may run before it is marked as failed. A job can set its own tries. --timeout=S 60 Seconds a job may run. --sleep=S 3 Seconds to wait when the queues are empty. --stop-when-empty off Stop when the queues are empty. --timeout-grace=S none After a timeout, wait up to S seconds for the old run to end before the next try.

An unknown flag or command prints the usage and exits with code 64.

Flags of auth:tokens-table. They set the same options of AccessTokenTables.up:

Flag Meaning --uuid The users have uuid ids. Set uuidIds: true on AccessTokenAuthDriver too. --string-ids The users have text ids. Set stringIds: true on AccessTokenAuthDriver too. Do not use it with --uuid. --users-table=<table> Add a foreign key from tokenable_id to this table, with cascade delete. --users-key=<column> The column of --users-table for the foreign key. Default: id. It does nothing without --users-table.

The bin/queue.dart of a new project (<app> is the name in pubspec.yaml). The jobs come from queueConfig in lib/config/queue.dart:

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_queue/dox_queue.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/app.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  exitCode = await QueueWorker(app: appConfig).run(args);
}

Templates: createJob and queueEntrySource in lib/src/tools/create_job.dart.

docs.title: Schedule
docs.text:
These commands run the app script bin/schedule.dart with dart run. A new project already has it. They pass the signals, the terminal and the exit code the same way as the queue commands. When bin/schedule.dart is missing, the command prints how to set it up and exits with code 1.

Command Runs What it does dox schedule:work bin/schedule.dart work Run the scheduler and keep it running. dox schedule:run bin/schedule.dart run Run the tasks that are due now, once. dox schedule:list bin/schedule.dart list List the scheduled tasks. dox schedule:test <name> bin/schedule.dart test <name> Run one task now. dox schedule:clear-cache bin/schedule.dart clear-cache Remove the withoutOverlapping() locks that a crash left behind. Do not run it while a task really runs.

You add tasks in lib/config/schedule.dart. These are the two files of a new project:

lib/config/schedule.dart
import 'package:dox_scheduler/dox_scheduler.dart';

ScheduleConfig scheduleConfig = const ScheduleConfig();

void schedule(Schedule s) {
  // s.call('cleanup', cleanup).dailyAt('02:00');
}
bin/schedule.dart
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_scheduler/dox_scheduler.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/app.dart';
import 'package:<app>/config/schedule.dart';

Future<void> main(List<String> args) async {
  exitCode = await SchedulerRunner(
    schedule: schedule,
    app: appConfig,
    config: scheduleConfig,
  ).run(args);
}

See Scheduler for the task methods. See Queue for jobs.
