A middleware needs to be on the route. AfterResponse lets any code (a controller, a service, a package) add work that runs after the answer of the current request is sent. The code does not need the request.

It is off by default. Turn it on once, in the setup() of a provider. setup() runs in every isolate.

lib/providers/app_provider.dart
@override
void setup() {
  AfterResponse.enable();
}

Then add work anywhere in the request:

AfterResponse.run(() => mailer.sendWelcome(user));
  • The work runs after the answer is sent, one after the other, in the order it was added. The next one starts only when the one before it ends. So work that never ends blocks the rest of the work of that request.
  • Outside a request, or when it is off, the work runs soon, after the code that runs now.
  • An error in the work goes to ExceptionHandler.report. It never reaches the client and never stops the server.
  • The work is not saved anywhere. When the server stops, work that did not run yet is lost. Use a queue for work that must run. To run a queue job this way, see dispatchAfterResponse() in Queue.

docs.title: Request id
docs.text:
RequestId gives each request an id. It is sent back in the X-Request-Id header, and you can read it as req.requestId.

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    const RequestId(),
    LogMiddleware(enabled: true),
  ],
  // ...
);
  • When the client (or a proxy) sends a safe X-Request-Id (1 to 128 characters of A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ -), Dox keeps it. Else it makes a new one of 32 hex characters.
  • RequestId(trustClient: false) always makes a new one.
  • LogMiddleware adds http.request_id to each log line. Put RequestId before it.
  • The default ExceptionHandler.report prints the id with the error. In your own report, read ExceptionHandler.requestId.

docs.title: ETag and 304 Not Modified
docs.text:
ETag adds an ETag header to GET and HEAD answers. When the client sends the same ETag back in If-None-Match, Dox answers 304 Not Modified with no body.

Route.get('/posts', <dynamic>[const ETag(), (PostController c) => c.index]);
  • It works on 200 answers with a body in memory: a String, a Map, a List or a model. Files and streams are not touched.
  • An answer that already has an ETag header or Cache-Control: no-store is not touched.
  • The ETag is weak (W/"..."), made from a fast 64-bit hash of the body. It is not a secure hash.
  • The controller still runs. A 304 saves bandwidth, not server time.

docs.title: Request timeout
docs.text:
RequestTimeout answers 503 Service Unavailable when the middleware after it and the controller take too long.

Route.get('/report', (ReportController c) => c.show)
    .timeout(Duration(seconds: 30));

// the same as
Route.get('/report', <dynamic>[
  RequestTimeout(Duration(seconds: 30)),
  (ReportController c) => c.show,
]);

The answer is the normal error JSON:

{"code": "request_timeout", "message": "The request took too long"}
  • For every route, add RequestTimeout(...) to globalMiddleware.
  • Dart can not stop a running Future. The controller keeps running in the background. Its late result is dropped, so nothing is sent twice.
  • It is 503, not 504. 504 Gateway Timeout is what a proxy sends when the app is slow. 503 says the app itself gave up.

docs.title: Server timing
docs.text:
ServerTiming adds a Server-Timing header to the answer. The browser dev tools show it in the Network tab, under Timing.

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    if (Env.get<String>('APP_ENV') == 'development') const ServerTiming(),
  ],
  // ...
);

It always sends two times, in milliseconds:

  • handler: the time in the controller.
  • total: the time of the middleware after ServerTiming and the controller.

Add your own times to the current request from any code. You do not pass the request:

ServerTiming.add('db', Duration(milliseconds: 4));

String html = await ServerTiming.measure('render', () => view.render());

The header looks like this:

Server-Timing: db;dur=4.10;desc="3 calls", handler;dur=12.34, total;dur=13.02
  • add with the same name again adds the times together. With more than one call, the text shows the count, like "3 calls". Pass description: to set your own text.
  • measure runs the function and adds the time it took, also when it throws.
  • Without the middleware, or outside a request, add and measure do nothing. The cost is one small lookup.
  • A name may only have letters, digits and !#$%&'*+-.^_`|~. Other characters become _. An empty name is ignored.
  • One answer keeps at most 32 names, plus handler and total.
  • handler and total are kept for the built-in times. If your code adds a time named total or handler, it is sent as app_total or app_handler. It does not change the built-in times. If you also add a time named app_total, the two are added together.
  • If the answer already has a Server-Timing header (set with res.header), the times are added after it, like cdn;dur=1, handler;dur=12.34, total;dur=13.02.

To add the time of every database query, listen to the queries once, for example in setup() of a provider. The listener runs inside the request that made the query, so add finds that request:

lib/providers/query_timing_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart'; // SqlQueryBuilder and QueryEvent

void onQuery(QueryEvent event) {
  ServerTiming.add('db', event.time);
}

/// Dox finds every DoxProvider class,
/// see lib/generated/container.g.dart.
class QueryTimingProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    SqlQueryBuilder().listen(onQuery);
  }
}

Each listen call adds the listener again. If setup() runs a second time (for example in tests), the time of each query is counted twice. Call SqlQueryBuilder().removeListener(onQuery) first, or when you are done.

The header then shows the total query time and the count, like db;dur=4.10;desc="3 calls". See Listen to queries.

Development or trusted clients only

The header tells every client how long your code takes. An attacker can use that, for example to guess if an email has an account. ServerTiming is off unless you add it. Turn it on in development, or only for clients you trust.

docs.title: Many middleware on one route
docs.text:
Put them in the list before the controller. They run from left to right. You can mix class and function middleware, with or without next.

Route.get('/ping', <dynamic>[
  LoggerMiddleware(),
  apiKeyMiddleware,
  (WebController c) => c.pong, // the controller is always last
]);

docs.title: Middleware for a group of routes
docs.text:
Route.middleware(<dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware()], () {
  Route.get('/me', (AuthController c) => c.me);
  Route.post('/logout', (AuthController c) => c.logout);
});

docs.title: Middleware for a router or for all routes
docs.text:
For one router, set its middleware list:

lib/routes/api.dart
class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[LoggerMiddleware()];

  @override
  void register() {
    // every route here runs LoggerMiddleware
  }
}

For all routes, set globalMiddleware in the app config:

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    LogMiddleware(enabled: env.appEnv != 'production'),
  ],
  // ...
);

A provider can add global middleware with Dox().addGlobalMiddleware(...). They run before the app's globalMiddleware. A second add of the same middleware is skipped.

The list is cleared at each start, before the providers run. Add package middleware from a provider's setup(), which runs on every start. Anything added before the app starts is cleared. Use a top-level function or a const instance. The providers do not run for dox route:list, so it does not show this middleware.

class AuditProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  Future<void> setup() async {
    Dox().addGlobalMiddleware(AuditMiddleware());
  }
}

The order is: package middleware from providers, then the app's global middleware, then router middleware, then group middleware, then route middleware.

flowchart LR
    Q["Request"] --> G["Global<br>globalMiddleware"]
    G --> R["Router<br>middleware getter"]
    R --> P["Group<br>Route.middleware"]
    P --> T["Route<br>list before the controller"]
    T --> C["Controller"]
    C --> S["Response"]
    G & R & P & T -.->|"returns a value or throws"| S

Built-in middleware

  • LogMiddleware from dox_core logs one line per request through Logger.
    • It follows LoggerConfig: enabled, level and prettyPrint.
    • If the logger is off, LogMiddleware(enabled: true) does not turn logs on.
    • enabled: false turns only the request logs off. Leave it unset to follow the logger.
    • With prettyPrint it prints colored text.
    • Without it, it prints one JSON line with status, message, network.client.ip, http.method, http.url, http.request_id and payload.
    • The filter can change status, message and the other fields. It can not change timestamp or logger: Logger sets them. A logger key is ignored, also when the logger name is empty.
    • Headers are logged only with withHeader: true.
    • Body fields and headers whose name has a word like password, secret, token, authorization, cookie or api_key in it (upper or lower case) are logged as [REDACTED]. Change the list with redact:.
    • The new project turns it off when APP_ENV is production.
  • AuthMiddleware from dox_auth checks the JWT token. AuthMiddleware(optional: true) lets guests through too. GuestMiddleware lets only guests through, for login pages. See Authentication.
  • RateLimit from dox_core answers 429 when a client sends too many requests. See Rate limiting.
  • SecurityHeaders from dox_core adds safe headers like X-Frame-Options to every answer. See Security headers.
  • SessionMiddleware from dox_core gives each request a session. See Session.
  • CsrfMiddleware from dox_core stops cross site request forgery. See CSRF protection.
  • RequestId, ETag, RequestTimeout and ServerTiming from dox_core. See above.
  • ValidateSignature from dox_core checks signed urls. See Signed URLs.

docs.title: Request
docs.text: This page shows how to read input, files, headers and cookies from a request.

docs.title: Typed input (recommended)
docs.text:
Ask for a DTO in your controller. Dox reads the body (or the query for GET, HEAD and DELETE), checks it, and gives you a typed object.

Route.put('/users/{id}', (UserController c) => c.update);

@Inject()
class UserController {
  Future<User?> update( // (1)!
    int id, // (2)!
    UpdateUser input, // (3)!
  ) async {
    User? user = await User().find(id);
    user?.name = input.name;
    await user?.save();
    return user;
  }
}
  1. The return value is the response. Dox waits for a Future. A String is sent as text. A Map or a model is sent as JSON.
  2. A path param. It is {id} from the route. /users/abc answers 404, because abc is not an int.
  3. A DTO. Dox reads the body, checks it, and builds the object before this method runs.

Bad input gets 422 before your method runs. See Validation.

docs.title: Raw input
docs.text:
Add a DoxRequest parameter to read the raw values. These values are not checked.

@Inject()
class ApiController {
  String sayHello(DoxRequest req) {
    String? name = req.input('name');
    return 'Hello $name';
  }
}
Code Gives req.input('name') one value from the query string or the body. The body wins when both have the key. req.input('user.name', 'guest') a value inside a map or list, with a dot key. The second value is the default, used when the key is not there or is null. req.all() all values from the query string and the body, as a Map req.only(<String>['name', 'email']) only these keys req.except(<String>['password']) all values, without these keys req.has('name') true when the key is there as it is and not empty. It does not read dot keys. req.filled('name') true when the key is there and not empty. A text of only spaces, an empty list and an empty map count as empty. req.exists('name') true when the key is there, with any value (also '' or null) req.missing('name') true when the key is not there req.boolean('remember') true for true, 1, on and yes. Else false. req.integer('page', 1) the value as an int. The default is used when the key is not there or is not a number. req.body the body only (JSON, form data) req.query the query string only req.add('key', value), req.merge({...}) add values, for example in a middleware

A dot key reads inside the input. req.input('items.0.id') gives the id of the first item. A key that is in the input as it is wins. So a body key 'a.b' is read before the b key inside a. Dot keys also work in filled, exists, missing, boolean, integer, file and hasFile. has does not read dot keys: req.has('user.name') is false for {"user": {"name": "Ann"}}. Use filled for that.

The flags onlyPresent and hasKeyOnly make only leave out missing keys and has only check the key. See Core flags.

Form and query keys with brackets give lists and maps:

Input req.input(...) gives tags[]=a&tags[]=b req.input('tags') is ['a', 'b'] address[city]=Yangon req.input('address') is {'city': 'Yangon'} items[0][name]=x req.input('items') is [{'name': 'x'}] name=a&name=b (no brackets) req.input('name') is 'b', the last value

docs.title: Route params
docs.text: Ask for a path param as a typed parameter, like int id in the example above. The text values are also in req.param, like req.param['id']. They are URL-decoded: /users/a%20b gives 'a b'. See Controller: parameters.

docs.title: Form data (File)
docs.text:
An uploaded file is a RequestFile. The request must be multipart/form-data. Put the file in a DTO, so Dox checks its type and size:

lib/app/dtos/upload_image/upload_image.dto.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'upload_image.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class UploadImage {
  @Image()
  @MaxSize('5MB')
  final RequestFile image;

  const UploadImage({required this.image});

  static const DtoSchema<UploadImage> schema = $UploadImageDto;
}
lib/app/http/controllers/api.controller.dart
@Inject()
class ApiController {
  Future<Map<String, String>> uploadImage(UploadImage input) async {
    String uploadedPath = await input.image.store('images');
    return <String, String>{'filename': uploadedPath};
  }
}

store() comes from the dox_storage package. Add it and import package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart.

Without a DTO, req.file('image') gives the RequestFile, or null when the field is not a file. req.hasFile('image') is true when the field holds a file or a list of files. For a field with many files, use req.input('images'). The file is not checked.

docs.title: RequestFile
docs.text:
RequestFile file = req.input('video');

file.filename;        // name from the client
file.filetype;        // content type, like video/mp4
file.extension;       // mp4
file.length;          // size in bytes
await file.size;      // size in KB
file.stream();        // read it in chunks
await file.store('videos');              // save to storage (needs dox_storage). returns the path
await file.moveTo('/data/videos/1.mp4'); // move it. returns the new File
await file.bytes;     // the whole file in memory. avoid for big files

Save the file before you return

A file up to 1 MB stays in memory. A bigger file is written to a temp file while it arrives. The temp file is deleted when the response is sent. So call store, moveTo or stream before your controller returns.

docs.title: Size limits
docs.text:
A body that is too big gets 413 Payload Too Large. Dox checks Content-Length first. It also counts the bytes while it reads the body.

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig(
  maxBodySize: 10 * 1024 * 1024,        // JSON and urlencoded, default 10 MB
  maxMultipartSize: 100 * 1024 * 1024,  // form-data uploads, default 100 MB
);

Set the same limit in your proxy, like client_max_body_size in nginx.

docs.title: Headers
docs.text:
String? token = req.header('X-Token');
Map<String, dynamic> all = req.headers; // a repeated header is joined with ', '

req.userAgent();  // User-Agent header
req.host();       // Host header
req.origin();     // Origin header, or null
req.referer();    // Referer header, or null
req.isJson();     // true for a JSON body
req.isFormData(); // true for multipart/form-data
req.locale;       // first language of Accept-Language, like 'th', or null
req.bearerToken(); // the token of 'Authorization: Bearer <token>', or null

docs.title: Path and URL
docs.text:
req.path();                   // '/admin/users/5'
req.fullUrl();                // 'https://example.com/admin/users/5?tab=info'
req.pathIs('admin/*');        // true. `*` matches any text
req.routeIs('admin.users.*'); // true when the route name matches

pathIs cleans the path like the router does. A / at the start or the end does not matter, and // counts as one /. So 'admin/*' and '/admin/*' are the same, and /admin/ and /admin// match 'admin', like they reach the /admin route. routeIs is false for a route with no name. Give a route a name with .name('admin.users.show').

docs.title: Cookies
docs.text:
String? token = req.cookie('token');                 // decrypted value
String? raw = req.cookie('theme', decrypt: false);   // value as sent

See Response to set a cookie.

docs.title: Client IP and scheme
docs.text:
req.ip();       // client IP
req.scheme();   // http or https
req.isSecure(); // true for https

Behind a proxy, req.ip() shows the proxy, not the client. Set trustedProxies in AppConfig to fix it. See Deployment.

docs.title: Response
docs.text: This page shows what a controller can return, and how to set the status, headers and cookies.

docs.title: Return a value
docs.text:
Return the value from your controller. Dox turns it into the response.

You return The client gets a String the text a Map or a List JSON a model, a list of models, a serializer JSON (from toJson()) a DateTime the ISO 8601 text an IHttpException, like NotFoundHttpException() its status code and JSON: {"code": ..., "message": ...}, or a Map message as it is a File (from dart:io) the file, streamed a Stream<List<int>> the bytes, streamed StreamFile, DownloadableFile (also from Storage() of dox_storage) the file, streamed response(...) full control: status, headers, cookies 
// JSON
Map<String, String> hello(DoxRequest req) {
  return <String, String>{'message': 'hello world!'};
}

// a model
Future<Blog?> show(int id) async {
  return Blog().find(id);
}

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Throw or return an exception to answer with an error.

Exception Status BadRequestException() 400 NotFoundHttpException() 404 PayloadTooLargeException() 413 UnsupportedMediaTypeException() 415 TokenMismatchException() 419 ValidationException() 422 TooManyRequestsException() 429 InternalErrorException() 500

Each one takes message:, errorCode: and code::

throw NotFoundHttpException(message: 'Blog not found');

The client gets 404 with {"code":"not_found","message":"Blog not found"}. code is the errorCode. A Map message is sent as it is.

For another status, extend IHttpException:

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ForbiddenException extends IHttpException {
  ForbiddenException({String message = 'Forbidden'}) {
    super.code = HttpStatus.forbidden;
    super.errorCode = 'forbidden';
    super.message = message;
  }
}

Any other error gets 500. It is also passed to the exception handler.

docs.title: Files and big responses
docs.text:
Return a File or a Stream<List<int>>. Dox sends it in chunks. It does not load it all into memory.

  • A File sets Content-Type (from the file name), Content-Length and Accept-Ranges.
  • It answers Range: bytes=... with 206 Partial Content. Video players can seek, and downloads can resume.
  • Storage().stream() and Storage().download() on the local disk also stream the file.
import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_storage/dox_storage.dart';

// a file from disk
Route.get('/video', (DoxRequest req) => File('storage/video.mp4'));

// a download from Storage
Future<DownloadableFile> download(DoxRequest req) async {
  // sends Content-Disposition, so the browser saves the file
  return Storage().download('report.pdf');
}

// a stream from Storage
Future<StreamFile> show(DoxRequest req) async {
  return Storage().stream('photo.jpg');
}

See File Storage.

docs.title: The response() helper
docs.text:
Use response(content) when you need to set the status, headers or cookies. All methods return the response, so you can chain them.

import 'dart:io';

import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

DoxResponse store(DoxRequest req) {
  return response(<String, String>{'status': 'created'})
      .statusCode(201)
      .header('X-Request-Id', 'abc')
      .contentType(ContentType.json);
}
Method Does statusCode(201) sets the status code. Default 200. header('X-Key', 'value') sets one header. A value a middleware put on the response stays, and this one is added. header('X-Key', 'value', replace: true) replaces it. withHeaders({...}) adds these headers. A key replaces the header with the same name, in any case. Other headers stay. contentType(ContentType.html) sets Content-Type (ContentType is from dart:io) cache(Duration(minutes: 5)) sets Cache-Control: max-age=300 cookie(DoxCookie(...)) sets a cookie content(value) changes the body stream(byteStream) sends a Stream<List<int>> as the body

docs.title: Redirect
docs.text:
// 302 to a path
return redirect('/login');

// another status
return redirect('/posts', status: 301);

// back to the page the request came from (Referer), or '/'
return back(req);

See Session for flash messages and errors with a redirect.

The flags htmlStrings (a string is sent as text/html) and replaceHeaders (header() replaces) change this page. See Core flags.

docs.title: Cookie
docs.text:
// set a cookie
DoxCookie cookie = DoxCookie('theme', 'dark');
return response('ok').cookie(cookie);

// set a cookie with options
DoxCookie token = DoxCookie(
  'token',
  'value',
  maxAge: Duration(days: 7), // sent as Max-Age in seconds. default 1 hour
  httpOnly: true, // default true: page scripts can not read it
  secure: true,   // default: Secure only when the request came over https
  path: '/',
  sameSite: SameSite.lax, // from dart:io. default: none sent
);
return response('ok').cookie(token);

// delete a cookie
return response('ok').cookie(DoxCookie('token', ''), setExpire: true);

To read a cookie, see Request: cookies.

The flag cookieDefaults sends Path=/ and SameSite=Lax when you set no path or sameSite. See Core flags.

Encrypt and decrypt

By default, Dox encrypts the cookie value with APP_KEY, and decrypts it when you read it. To turn this off, use DoxCookie(key, value, encrypt: false) to set it, and req.cookie(key, decrypt: false) to read it.

docs.title: Change every response
docs.text:
To change every response in one place (for example, to add a header), set a responseHandler in AppConfig.

lib/app/http/handler.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ResponseHandler extends ResponseHandlerInterface {
  @override
  DoxResponse handle(DoxResponse res) {
    return res.header('X-Powered-By', 'Dox');
  }
}
lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  responseHandler: ResponseHandler(),
  // ...
);

docs.title: Routing
docs.text:
A route connects a URL and an HTTP method to the code that answers it.

This is the path of one request through the router:

flowchart LR
    Q["Request<br>GET /blogs/42"] --> B["Router<br>method, host, path"]
    B -->|no match| N["404"]
    B -->|match| P["Params as text<br>req.param"]
    P --> M["Middleware"]
    M -->|returns a value| S["Response"]
    M -->|returns the request| T["Typed params, DTO<br>int id"]
    T --> C["Controller"]
    C --> S

docs.title: Where routes live
docs.text:
Routes are in the lib/routes folder. Each file has one Router class. The prefix of the router is added in front of all its routes.

lib/routes/api.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong'); // GET /api/ping
  }
}

Dox finds every Router class by itself. It is in lib/generated/container.g.dart after dart run build_runner build. To pick the order of routers, list them in routers: of AppConfig. See Dependency injection: routers and providers.

The leading / in a path is optional. 'ping' and '/ping' are the same route.

To see every route of your app, run dox route:list. It does not start the server. See dox route:list.

docs.title: Route methods
docs.text:
Route.get('/blogs', (BlogController c) => c.index);
Route.post('/blogs', (BlogController c) => c.store);
Route.put('/blogs/{id}', (BlogController c) => c.update);
Route.patch('/blogs/{id}', (BlogController c) => c.update);
Route.delete('/blogs/{id}', (BlogController c) => c.destroy);

Info

There are also Route.options, Route.copy, Route.view, Route.link, Route.unlink, Route.purge, Route.lock, Route.unlock and Route.propfind. These are HTTP methods. Route.view is the WebDAV VIEW method. It does not render a template. To show a template, use a GET route: Route.get('welcome', (DoxRequest req) => view(req, 'welcome')) with view() of dox_view.

Route.health('/health') adds a health check route. It answers 200 with {"status": "ok"}. Route.websocket('echo', (WebSocket socket, DoxRequest req) {...}) adds a raw WebSocket route. By default any website can open it from a browser, with the cookies of the user. To check the Origin, pass allowedOrigins: ['https://app.example.com'], or set AppConfig(webSocketAllowedOrigins: [...]) for every WebSocket route. Then only pages of the same host and the listed sites can open it. Other origins get 403. [] means the same host only. When a WebSocket route has no check, Dox prints one warning to stderr at start. A message over maxMessageSize bytes (default 16 MB) closes the socket with code 1009. Example: Route.websocket('chat', handler, maxMessageSize: 64 * 1024).

A HEAD request runs the GET route of the same path. The answer has the status and headers of GET, with no body.

docs.title: More than one method
docs.text:
Route.match adds the same handler for a list of methods. Route.any adds it for GET, POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE.

Route.match(<String>['GET', 'POST'], '/contact', (ContactController c) => c.handle);
Route.any('/webhook', (WebhookController c) => c.handle);
  • HEAD comes with GET, so do not list it. An unknown method throws an ArgumentError at start.
  • Route.any does not add OPTIONS. So Dox still answers the CORS preflight request for the path.
  • .where(...) and .timeout(...) after Route.match or Route.any work on every route it added. .name(...) names the last one.

docs.title: Redirect routes
docs.text:
Route.redirect sends a path to another URL. The status is 302 by default.

Route.redirect('/home', '/');
Route.redirect('/old-blog', '/blog', status: 301);
Route.permanentRedirect('/old-pricing', '/pricing'); // 301

The redirect works for the same methods as Route.any.

  • The target is sent as it is. A param like {id} in the target is not filled in: Route.redirect('/u/{id}', '/users/{id}') sends the client to /users/{id}.
  • The query string of the request is dropped. /home?page=2 goes to /, not /?page=2.
  • For these cases, use a normal route and return redirect(...) with the URL you build.

docs.title: The handler
docs.text:
The second argument is the code that answers the request. It can be:

// a function
Route.get('/ping', (DoxRequest req) => 'pong');

// a controller method. The controller comes from the container.
Route.get('/ping', (WebController c) => c.pong);

@Inject()
class WebController {
  String pong(DoxRequest req) {
    return 'pong';
  }
}

// a list: middleware first, the controller last
Route.get('/ping', <dynamic>[
  LoggerMiddleware(),
  (WebController c) => c.pong,
]);

In a list, the last item is the controller. The items before it are middleware. (WebController c) => c.pong picks the method. Dox calls it once per isolate, at start. See Dependency injection.

See Controller for the parameters a handler can ask for.

docs.title: Route params
docs.text:
Put a param in {}. Ask for it as a typed parameter in the controller.

Route.get('/blogs/{id}', (BlogController c) => c.show);

@Inject()
class BlogController {
  Future<Blog?> show(int id) async {
    return Blog().find(id);
  }
}

/blogs/abc answers 404, because abc is not an int. See Controller: parameters for all the rules.

docs.title: Optional param
docs.text:
{name?} can be missing. Use a nullable type.

Route.get('/posts/{page?}', (int? page) {
  return 'page ${page ?? 1}'; // GET /posts and GET /posts/2 both match
});

docs.title: Catch-all param
docs.text:
{name*} matches the rest of the path, with slashes.

Route.get('/docs/{page*}', (String page) {
  return page; // GET /docs/a/b/c gives 'a/b/c'
});

docs.title: Param rules
docs.text:
.where(param, regex) lets a route match only when the param text matches the regex. When it does not match, the router tries the next route. When no route matches, the client gets 404.

Route.get('/users/{id}', (UserController c) => c.show).where('id', '[0-9]+');
Route.get('/users/{name}', (UserController c) => c.byName); // gets the rest

Route.get('/files/{type}', handler).where('type', 'png|jpg');
Route.get('/docs/{page}', handler).where('page', '.*'); // matches slashes too
  • The regex must match the whole param text. You do not need ^ or $. A leading ^ and a trailing $ are dropped.
  • Use (?:...) for a group, not (...). A regex with a (...) group throws an ArgumentError at start.
  • A param name that the path does not have throws an ArgumentError at start.
  • Call .where more than once for more params.
  • Routes without .where match the same as before. The check costs nothing for them.
  • The regex checks the param text two times: as it is in the URL, and again after % codes are decoded. Both checks must pass. A % code for a letter, a digit or -._~ is decoded before the router sees the path, so /users/%31 is /users/1 and matches [0-9]+. Other % codes stay in the URL text and must pass the second check. So /files/x%2Fy does not match [^/]+, because %2F is /. The controller gets the decoded value. In the second check, . also matches a new line (%0A), so .* still matches it.

docs.title: Group routes
docs.text:
// by prefix
Route.group('/blogs', () { // (1)!
  Route.get('/', (BlogController c) => c.index); // GET /blogs
  Route.get('/{id}', (BlogController c) => c.show); // (2)!
});

// by domain
Route.domain('dartondox.com', () { // (3)!
  Route.get('/ping', (WebController c) => c.pong);
});

// by middleware
Route.middleware(<dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()], () { // (4)!
  Route.get('/me', (AuthController c) => c.me);
  Route.post('/logout', (AuthController c) => c.logout);
});
  1. /blogs goes in front of every path in the callback. Dox puts one / between the parts. 'blogs' and '/blogs/' work the same.
  2. Makes GET /blogs/{id}.
  3. These routes match only when the Host header is dartondox.com. Other hosts get 404.
  4. AuthMiddleware runs before me and logout. It runs after the global and router middleware.

Groups can be nested. Route.group('blogs', ...) with Route.get('all', ...) makes /blogs/all.

A group can also add a prefix to the route names inside it, with name:.

To turn CORS on or off for some routes, see CORS.

docs.title: Resource routes
docs.text:
One line makes the usual CRUD routes for a controller.

Route.resource('blogs', BlogController);

BlogController is a class from the container. A controller object works too: Route.resource('blogs', BlogController()).

Method Path Controller method Route name GET /blogs index blogs.index GET /blogs/create create blogs.create POST /blogs store blogs.store GET /blogs/{id} show blogs.show GET /blogs/{id}/edit edit blogs.edit PUT, PATCH /blogs/{id} update blogs.update DELETE /blogs/{id} destroy blogs.destroy

The name comes from the path: / becomes ., and {params} are left out. So Route.resource('users/{user}/posts', ...) gives users.posts.index. Pass name: to pick another one: Route.resource('blogs', BlogController, name: 'posts').

The param of one item is {id}. Pass parameter: to name it:

Route.resource('photos', PhotoController, parameter: 'photo');
// GET /photos/{photo}, PUT /photos/{photo}, ...

Then Route.bind('photo', ...) and model binding work on these routes.

A method that the controller does not have is skipped. No route is made for it. Any other error from the controller is not hidden. It stops the app at start, so you see it. See Resource controller to make one with the CLI.

docs.title: Forms with PUT, PATCH and DELETE
docs.text:
An HTML form can only send GET or POST. To reach a PUT, PATCH or DELETE route, add MethodOverride to the global middleware.

AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[const MethodOverride()],
);

Then send the form as POST with a _method field.

<form method="POST" action="/blogs/5">
  <input type="hidden" name="_method" value="DELETE">
</form>
  • Only a POST request changes, and only to PUT, PATCH or DELETE. Other values are ignored.
  • req.method gives the new method.
  • CsrfMiddleware still checks the request, so send the _token field too.
  • It works only in globalMiddleware, not on a router or a route. It is off by default.

A client that can not send PUT, like an old proxy or JS client, can send the X-HTTP-Method-Override header instead. Turn it on with header: true. It is off by default.

AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[const MethodOverride(header: true)],
);

The header has the same rules as _method. When both are there, the header wins.

docs.title: Named routes
docs.text:
Give a route a name with .name(). Then build its URL from the name, so a path lives in one place.

Route.get('/users/{id}', (UserController c) => c.show).name('users.show');

route('users.show', params: <String, Object>{'id': 5});
// /users/5

route('users.show', params: <String, Object>{'id': 5}, query: <String, Object>{'tab': 'posts'});
// /users/5?tab=posts

route() gives the path. Route.url() does the same. Param values are URL encoded. A missing {name?} param is left out.

A param that is not in the path goes to the query string. A value that is null is left out. When params and query have the same key, query wins.

route('users.show', params: <String, Object>{'id': 5, 'tab': 'posts'});
// /users/5?tab=posts

route('users.show', params: <String, Object>{'id': 5, 'tab': 'a'}, query: <String, Object>{'tab': 'b'});
// /users/5?tab=b

docs.title: Full URL
docs.text:
Pass absolute: true to get the full URL, with APP_URL in front. Pass baseUrl: to use another base. baseUrl: works only with absolute: true.

route('users.show', params: <String, Object>{'id': 5}, absolute: true);
// https://example.com/users/5   (APP_URL=https://example.com)

route('users.show', params: <String, Object>{'id': 5}, absolute: true, baseUrl: 'https://admin.example.com');
// https://admin.example.com/users/5

With absolute: true and no APP_URL and no baseUrl:, route() throws an ArgumentError.

A group can put a prefix in front of the names inside it:

Route.group('admin', () {
  Route.get('users', (UserController c) => c.index).name('users'); // admin.users
}, name: 'admin.');

Dox stops with a clear error when:

  • two routes have the same name (at start),
  • route() gets a name that no route has,
  • a {param} of the path has no value.

docs.title: Signed routes
docs.text:
A signed URL is a named route with a signature in its query, so nobody can change it. Use it for links in emails, like "unsubscribe". Protect the route with ValidateSignature, and make the URL with Route.signedUrl:

Route.get('/unsubscribe/{user}', <dynamic>[
  const ValidateSignature(),
  (UserController c) => c.unsubscribe,
]).name('unsubscribe');

Route.signedUrl('unsubscribe',
    params: <String, Object>{'user': 5}, expires: Duration(days: 7));
// https://example.com/unsubscribe/5?expires=...&signature=...

A changed or expired URL gets 403. See Signed URLs.

docs.title: Route model binding
docs.text:
A binder turns a route param into a value before the controller runs, for example a model from the database. Add it with Route.bind, before the routes that use it.

Route.bind<User>('user', (String id) => User().find(id));

Route.get('/users/{user}', (DoxRequest req, User user) {
  return user;
});

Every route with a {user} param now runs the binder first. The binder gets the raw text from the URL. It returns the value, or null when there is none. null answers 404, the same way as a thrown NotFoundHttpException.

There are two ways to read the value:

  • Ask for a parameter of the bound type, like User user. Dox matches it by type, so it can be at any place in the parameter list.
  • Read it from the request: req.bound<User>('user'). This also works in a controller that only takes DoxRequest.

Other path params still work next to it:

Route.get('/users/{user}/posts/{page}', (User user, int page) {
  return user.posts(page);
});

The binder runs after the middleware, so an auth middleware can stop the request before any database call.

A @DoxModel class does not need Route.bind. Dox makes a binder for it in lib/generated/container.g.dart. See Dependency injection: route model binding. Route.bind wins when both exist.

docs.title: Serve static files
docs.text:
Route.staticFiles(prefix, folder) serves the files of a folder, like CSS, JavaScript and images.

Route.staticFiles('/', 'public');
Route.staticFiles('build', 'public/build', maxAge: Duration(days: 365));
  • Only GET and HEAD requests read files, and only when no route matches. A route always wins.
  • .., dot files (like .env or .git) and folders are never sent. They get 404.
  • The one dot folder that is sent is .well-known at the top of the folder (public/.well-known/...). It holds ACME (Let's Encrypt) challenges, security.txt and apple-app-site-association. Dot files inside it still get 404.
  • A file gets a weak ETag (from its size and change time) and Last-Modified. The browser gets 304 with no body when it already has the file. If-None-Match wins over If-Modified-Since. Range requests work. With If-Range, the Range is used only when it is the file's Last-Modified date. Else the whole file is sent.
  • maxAge sends Cache-Control: public, max-age=.... Give a long maxAge to build files with a hash in the name (like Vite's).
  • No middleware runs for a file. The global CORS config still applies.
  • Like other routes, the prefix follows Route.group, the router prefix and Route.domain.
  • The folder path is relative to the folder the app starts in. Symlinks in the folder are followed.

Warning

Never save user uploads in this folder. An uploaded html or svg file would run its script on your site. Use dox_storage for uploads. It sends such files as downloads.

Behind a proxy, the proxy can serve the folder instead. Then the files never reach Dox.

docs.title: Fallback route
docs.text:
Route.fallback answers a GET or HEAD request that matches no route and no static file. Use it for a custom 404 page, or to send index.html of a single page app.

lib/routes/web.dart
class WebRouter extends Router {
  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/', (WebController c) => c.home);

    Route.fallback((DoxRequest req) {
      return response(<String, String>{'message': 'Page not found'}).statusCode(404);
    });
  }
}
  • Other methods still get the normal 404 or 405.
  • A GET to a path that only has a POST route gets the fallback, if a fallback covers that path. If none does, the client gets 405.
  • Add the fallback before startServer(), like other routes. A fallback added later only works in the isolate that added it. The other isolates do not get it.
  • The fallback runs its middleware like any route. Add it in a Router, so the global middleware (like security headers) runs too.
  • It follows Route.group, the router prefix and Route.domain. In a group, it only answers paths under the group prefix. A prefix can have params, like {tenant}, and req.param gives them. When two fallbacks match, the one with the longest prefix wins.
  • The handler decides the status. Return a 404 status for a "not found" page, else the client gets 200.

Note

The built-in 404 and 405 answers do not run the global middleware. Running it there could change answers for apps today. For example, CsrfMiddleware would answer 419 to a POST to an unknown path, and SessionMiddleware would start a session for every bad link. Use Route.fallback in a router when your 404 page needs the global middleware.

docs.title: Serve storage files
docs.text:
Storage.route(path) from the dox_storage package serves the files of a storage disk at GET <path>/{key*}. By default only signed URLs work. Other requests get 403. See File Storage.

Storage.route('files');
Storage.route('public', disk: 'local', signed: false);

An html, svg, xml or javascript file is sent as a download (Content-Disposition: attachment) with Content-Security-Policy: sandbox. So a script in an uploaded file does not run on your site. Every file response also has X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, so the browser does not guess another type.

For user uploads, download: true sends every file as a download, also images and PDFs:

Storage.route('uploads', download: true);

docs.title: Request body for the docs
docs.text:
post, put and patch take a body: schema. It shows in the OpenAPI docs. It does not check the request. To check input, use a DTO.

Route.post('/posts', (PostController c) => c.store, body: v.object(<String, Schema<Object?>>{
  'title': v.string().min(3),
}));

docs.title: Mount a raw handler
docs.text:
Route.mount(prefix, handler) sends every request under a path prefix straight to a raw HttpRequest handler. It runs before routing and before the body is read. The handler writes and closes the response itself. Socket.IO uses it for /socket.io/.

Route.mount('/socket.io/', io.handle);
Route.mount('/admin', admin.handle, middleware: true);

How the prefix matches:

  • It matches whole path parts. /admin matches /admin, /admin/ and /admin/users. It never matches /administrator or /admin-login.
  • A trailing / does not change the match. /socket.io/ also matches /socket.io.
  • The query string is not part of the match.
  • When two prefixes match, the longest one wins. // counts as one /, so /admin//secure/x goes to a mount at /admin/secure.
  • The match uses the raw path. %2F stays encoded, so /admin/secure%2Fx goes to a mount at /admin. To protect a nested path, set middleware: true on the outer mount too.

Warning

By default a mount skips all middleware, also the global middleware (security headers, CSRF, rate limit). Set middleware: true to run AppConfig.globalMiddleware before the handler. The global CORS config never applies to a mount. The handler must send its own CORS headers.

With middleware: true:

  • A middleware that gives a response (like 403) stops the request. The handler does not run.
  • The body is not read for the middleware, so the handler can still read it. A CSRF token must come in a header.
  • The handler sends the answer itself. So the part of a next middleware that runs after the handler cannot change the answer.
  • A terminate step runs once the answer is sent, like on other routes.
  • RequestTimeout does not run for a mount. The handler already owns the answer.
  • Cookies that a middleware adds after the handler (the session cookie, XSRF-TOKEN) are not sent. Get the CSRF token from a normal route.
  • An error in the handler gives 500, like without middleware.

docs.title: Serializer
docs.text:
A serializer sets the JSON shape of a response: which keys the client gets, their names and their values.

It works with any Dart type: a model, a plain class, or a map.

Tip

You do not always need a serializer. A controller can return a model, a Map or a List as it is. See Response. To only hide some model fields, use hidden.

docs.title: Create a serializer
docs.text:
dox make:serializer Blog

This makes lib/app/serializers/blog.serializer.dart. The file is for a model with the same name. Change the type to use it for something else.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
Extend Serializer<T> and write convert. convert gets one value of type T and gives back one JSON object.

lib/app/serializers/blog.serializer.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

import 'package:my_app/app/models/blog/blog.model.dart';

class BlogSerializer extends Serializer<Blog> {
  BlogSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(Blog m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'uid': m.id,
      'title_en': m.title,
    };
  }
}

Return the serializer from a controller. Dox sends its toJson().

lib/app/http/controllers/blog.controller.dart
class BlogController {
  Future<BlogSerializer> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    List<Blog> blogs = await Blog().all();
    return BlogSerializer(blogs); // a list
  }

  Future<BlogSerializer> show(DoxRequest req, String id) async {
    Blog? blog = await Blog().find(id);
    return BlogSerializer(blog); // one model
  }
}

The response of show:

{
  "uid": 1,
  "title_en": "This is title"
}

What you give, and what the client gets:

You give The client gets one value of type T one JSON object a List<T> a JSON list ([] when the list is empty) null (for example, find found nothing) null any other type null

The list type must be List<T>

A List<dynamic> is not a List<T>, so the response is null. This happens with a list from jsonDecode. Call .cast<T>() first. See JSON from another API.

docs.title: Change values
docs.text:
convert is plain Dart. You can format dates, join fields and add new keys.

lib/app/serializers/user.serializer.dart
class UserSerializer extends Serializer<User> {
  UserSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(User m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'id': m.id,
      'name': '${m.firstName} ${m.lastName}',
      'is_active': m.status == 'active',
      'joined_at': m.createdAt?.toIso8601String(),
    };
  }
}

docs.title: A serializer inside a serializer
docs.text:
Use one serializer for a relation inside another. Load the relation first, for example with preload.

lib/app/serializers/comment.serializer.dart
class CommentSerializer extends Serializer<Comment> {
  CommentSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(Comment m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'id': m.id,
      'content': m.content,
      'user': UserSerializer(m.user).toJson(), // null when there is no user
    };
  }
}

Future<CommentSerializer> index(DoxRequest req) async {
  List<Comment> comments = await Comment().preload('user').all();
  return CommentSerializer(comments);
}

docs.title: With pagination
docs.text:
page.data is a List<User>. Put the serializer output in place of data.

Future<Map<String, dynamic>> index(ListUsers query) async {
  Pagination<User> page = await User()
      .orderBy('id', 'desc')
      .paginate(currentPage: query.page, perPage: query.perPage);
  return <String, dynamic>{
    ...page.toJson(),
    'data': UserSerializer(page.data).toJson(),
  };
}

See Pagination for the full example.

docs.title: Examples without models
docs.text: T can be any type. You do not need the ORM.

docs.title: A plain Dart class
Rows from the query builder
docs.text:
QueryBuilder.table(...) gives rows as maps, not models. Use Serializer<Map<String, dynamic>> to pick and rename the keys.

lib/app/serializers/sales_report.serializer.dart
class SalesReportSerializer extends Serializer<Map<String, dynamic>> {
  SalesReportSerializer(super.data);

  @override
  Map<String, dynamic> convert(Map<String, dynamic> m) {
    return <String, dynamic>{
      'product': m['name'],
      'sold': m['total'],
    };
  }
}

Future<SalesReportSerializer> report(DoxRequest req) async {
  List<Map<String, dynamic>> rows = await QueryBuilder.table('orders')
      .selectRaw('name, count(*) as total')
      .groupBy('name')
      .get();
  return SalesReportSerializer(rows);
}

docs.title: JSON from another API
docs.text:
jsonDecode gives a List<dynamic>. Cast it to the type of the serializer first.

Future<SalesReportSerializer> remote(DoxRequest req) async {
  String body = await fetchReport(); // your HTTP call
  List<dynamic> rows = jsonDecode(body);
  return SalesReportSerializer(rows.cast<Map<String, dynamic>>());
}

docs.title: See also
docs.text: • CLI: dox make:serializer

docs.title: Session
docs.text:
A session keeps data for one browser between requests.

Use it for web pages: the logged in user, a cart, a "Saved" message after a form post.

An API with tokens does not need a session.

docs.title: Turn it on
docs.text:
Add SessionMiddleware to globalMiddleware, or to the routers or routes that need it. Add CsrfMiddleware after it. See CSRF protection.

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  globalMiddleware: <dynamic>[
    const SessionMiddleware(),
    const CsrfMiddleware(except: <String>['/api/*']),
  ],
  // ...
);

Now every request has req.session. Using req.session on a route without the middleware throws an error.

docs.title: Use the session
docs.text:
// store a value
req.session.put('cart', <int>[1, 2]);

// read a value, with a default
List<dynamic> cart = req.session.get('cart', <int>[]);

// is it there (and not null)?
bool hasCart = req.session.has('cart');

// read and remove
dynamic removed = req.session.pull('cart');

// remove one value, or all of them
req.session.forget('cart');
req.session.flush();

// all values, as a copy
Map<String, dynamic> all = req.session.all();

Values must be JSON types: Map, List, String, num, bool or null.

docs.title: Flash data
docs.text:
Flash data lives for this request and the next one. Use it for a message after a redirect.

Route.post('/posts', (DoxRequest req) async {
  // ... save the post
  req.session.flash('message', 'The post is saved');
  return redirect('/posts');
});

Route.get('/posts', (DoxRequest req) {
  String? message = req.session.get('message'); // 'The post is saved'
  // ...
});

"The next request" means the next request that uses the session. A request that never reads the session (like an image) does not remove it.

To keep flash data for one more request, call req.session.reflash(), or req.session.keep(['message']) for some keys only.

docs.title: Redirect back with errors
docs.text:
back(req) redirects to the page the request came from (the Referer header), or to / when there is none. A Referer of another host is not used, so it also goes to /. redirect('/path') redirects to any path.

When a form post fails validation, Dox does this for you on a route with a session:

  1. It flashes the errors as errors, like {'email': 'The email is not a valid email'}.
  2. It flashes the old input. Password fields (password, password_confirmation, current_password) and files are never kept.
  3. It redirects back with 302.

The next page reads them:

Route.get('/register', (DoxRequest req) {
  Map<String, dynamic> errors = req.session.errors; // empty when there are none
  String? email = req.session.old('email');
  // ...
});

A request that wants JSON still gets the normal 422 JSON answer. A request wants JSON when it has an Accept header with json, a JSON body, or X-Requested-With: XMLHttpRequest. An Inertia request (it has the X-Inertia header) is redirected like a form post.

You can do the same by hand:

req.session.flashErrors(<String, String>{'email': 'The email is taken'}, input: req.all());
return back(req);

docs.title: After login and logout
docs.text:
// after login: a new session id and a new CSRF token, the data stays
req.session.regenerate();

// on logout: remove all data and get a new session id
req.session.invalidate();

Always call regenerate() after login. Then an id that someone saw before the login is of no use.

regenerate(keepToken: true) gives a new id but keeps the CSRF token, so forms open in other tabs keep working. Do not use it at login. A token from before the login would stay valid after the login.

With the default cookie session driver, all session data sits in the cookie. So an old copy of the cookie still works after logout. If logout must really end old cookies, use the cache session driver, like SessionConfig(driver: 'cache', store: 'redis').

dox_auth does this for you. See Session login.

docs.title: Config
docs.text:
Set session in the app config. All options have a default.

lib/config/app.dart
AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  session: const SessionConfig(
    driver: 'cache',
    store: 'redis',
    lifetime: Duration(hours: 2),
  ),
  // ...
);
Option Default What it does driver cookie cookie or cache. See below. store null The cache store for the cache driver, like redis, memory or file. null uses the default store of AppConfig.cache. cookie dox_session The name of the session cookie. lifetime 2 hours The session ends after this long with no use. The cookie driver keeps the save time in the encrypted cookie and checks it, so a copied old cookie stops working too. path / Path of the cookie. domain null Domain of the cookie. null means only the host that set it. httpOnly true Page scripts can not read the cookie. secure null null sets Secure when the request came over https. sameSite SameSite.lax SameSite of the cookie (from dart:io).

You can also give a config to one middleware: SessionMiddleware(SessionConfig(...)).

docs.title: The cookie driver
docs.text:
All session data is in the cookie, encrypted with AES-GCM and your APP_KEY. The browser can not read or change it. There is nothing to store on the server.

A cookie can hold about 4 KB. A session that is too big gives an error. Keep the data small (an id, not a whole object), or use the cache driver.

docs.title: The cache driver
docs.text: The cookie only has a random session id (encrypted too). The data lives in a cache store. Use redis when you run more than one isolate or more than one server: then all of them see the same sessions. A memory store is good for tests. It is not shared between isolates. With no Redis, a database store shares the sessions too: SessionConfig(driver: 'cache', store: 'database').

docs.title: When the session is read and saved
docs.text:
• The cookie driver reads the session on first use. A request that never uses req.session does not decrypt anything.
  • The cache driver reads the store before the controller, but only when the request has a session cookie. A new visitor costs nothing.
  • The session is saved only when it changed. Only then is the cookie sent. A session that is used but not changed is saved again after half of its lifetime, so it does not end while the user is active.

docs.title: Read the session from a package
docs.text:
Other packages (like an Inertia adapter) can read the same data:

if (req.hasSession) {
  Map<String, dynamic> errors = req.session.errors;
  dynamic message = req.session.get('message');
}

docs.title: Load a session with no request
docs.text:
Code that has no request, like a Socket.IO login, can load the session from the cookie value:

Session session = await SessionMiddleware().fromCookie(value);
dynamic userId = session.get('auth_web');
  • Give the value as the browser sent it (still encrypted). Do not decrypt it first.
  • The checks are the same as for a request. A changed cookie, a cookie of another name, a cookie made with another APP_KEY, an expired session or an unknown id gives an empty session.
  • Changes to this session are not saved.
  • With the cookie driver, an old copy of the cookie still works after logout, until the session lifetime ends. If a logout must stop old cookies, use the cache driver.
  • SessionMiddleware(config) uses another SessionConfig, like on a route.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
client.withSession() gives a test client that keeps cookies like a browser. It also sends the XSRF-TOKEN cookie back in X-XSRF-TOKEN, so CsrfMiddleware lets its posts in:

DoxTestClient browser = client.withSession();
await browser.get('/cart/add?id=1');
(await browser.get('/cart')).expectJson(isNotEmpty);

See Testing: keep a session.

docs.title: Validation rules
docs.text:
This page lists every annotation you can put on a @Dto field.

See Validation for how DTOs work.

How to read the tables:

  • Code is the error code. Use it in @Dto(messages: ...) and in a MessageResolver.
  • Message is the default English text. {field} is the last key of the path.
  • Every annotation also takes message:. It wins over every other message.
  • All limits include the limit itself, unless the table says "exclusive".
  • On a List<T> field, a value rule checks each item. Only the list rules check the list itself.

docs.title: Type errors
docs.text:
These have no annotation. They come from the field type.

Code When Message required a required field is missing, null, or "" The {field} is required string not a string The {field} must be a string integer not a whole number The {field} must be an integer numeric not a number (double, num) The {field} must be a number boolean not a bool The {field} must be a boolean date not an ISO 8601 date The {field} must be a date in not a name of the enum The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values} array not a list The {field} must be an array object not an object (nested DTO, Map) The {field} must be an object file not a file The {field} must be a file unrecognized_keys unknown key, with @Dto(strict: true) The {field} field is not allowed

docs.title: Text
docs.text:
For String fields (and List<String> items).

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @Length(min: 3, max: 50) length_between The {field} must be between {min} and {max} characters minLength, maxLength @Length(min: 6, max: 6) length The {field} must be exactly {length} characters minLength, maxLength @MinLength(3) min_length The {field} must be at least {min} characters minLength @MaxLength(50) max_length The {field} may not be greater than {max} characters maxLength @Email() email The {field} is not a valid email format: email @Url() url The {field} must be a url format: uri @Uuid() uuid The {field} is invalid uuid format: uuid @Ulid() ulid The {field} must be a valid ULID pattern @Ip() ip The {field} must be an ip address anyOf ipv4 / ipv6 @Regex(r'[a-z]+') regex The {field} format is invalid pattern @In(['a', 'b']) in The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values} enum @NotIn(['root']) not_in The {field} field cannot be {value} not: {enum} @StartsWith('dox') start_with The {field} must start with {prefix} pattern @EndsWith('.dev') end_with The {field} must end with {suffix} pattern @Alpha() alpha The {field} must be an alphabetic pattern @AlphaNumeric() alpha_numeric The {field} must be only alphabetic and number pattern @AlphaDash() alpha_dash The {field} must be only alphabetic, number, dash and underscore pattern

Details:

  • @Length has min: and max:. Both are optional, but you must give one. With only min: it acts like @MinLength, with only max: like @MaxLength.
  • Length counts characters (Unicode code points). é counts as 1.
  • @Url() needs http or https and a host.
  • @Uuid() takes any version. Upper or lower case.
  • @Ulid() takes 26 Crockford base32 characters, upper or lower case. The first one is 0 to 7.
  • @Regex(pattern, {message}) must match the whole value. You do not need ^ and $. The regex is checked when the generator runs. A bad regex stops the build.
  • @Alpha(), @AlphaNumeric() and @AlphaDash() use ASCII letters a-z, A-Z. @AlphaDash() also allows digits 0-9, - and _.
  • @In and @NotIn compare exactly (case matters).

docs.title: More text rules
docs.text:
For String fields.

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @Json() json The {field} is not a valid json contentMediaType: application/json @Digits(6) digits The {field} must be {digits} digits pattern @DigitsBetween(4, 6) digits_between The {field} must be between {min} and {max} digits pattern @DateFormatted('Y-m-d') date_format The {field} must match the format {format} @HexColor(), @HexColor(short: true) hex_color The {field} must be a hex color like #1a2b3c pattern @Password(min: 8, ...) password The {field} must have {rules} minLength
  • @HexColor() takes # and 6 hex digits, in any case. @HexColor(short: true) also takes 3 digits, like #abc.
  • @Digits and @DigitsBetween take only 0-9. No sign, no dot. Use a String field, so leading zeros stay.
  • @DateFormatted uses the PHP date() letters: day d, j, D (Mon), l (Monday), N, w, S (st), z; month m, n, M (Jan), F (January), t; year Y, y, L; time a, A, g, h, G, H, i, s, v, u; time zone e, T, P, p, O, Z, I; full U, c, r. Put \ before a letter to use it as text, like Y-m-d\TH:i. Any other letter stops the build (and throws an ArgumentError in v.string().dateFormat()). Other characters must be there as they are. j, n, g, G, z and U take no leading zero: j/n/Y rejects 01/02/2024. e and T take any name that looks like a time zone. They do not check that it is a real one. The date must exist: 2023-02-29 fails. Names need the case shown (Jan, not jan). A day name must fit the date. The field stays a String. Use a DateTime field for ISO 8601 dates.
  • @Password options: min (default 8), letters, mixedCase (one upper and one lower case letter), numbers, symbols. They are all off by default. Letters, numbers and symbols are Unicode, so é is a letter. {rules} lists the options you set, like at least 8 characters, one number, and one symbol, or at least 8 characters and one number. It does not check leaked passwords.

docs.title: Other fields
docs.text:
These read another key of the same object. The other key is the input key, like account_type, not the Dart name accountType. If you give the Dart name of a field with another key, the build stops. @Confirmed and @Same compare the raw input of both keys. So @Trim does not change the compare.

Annotation Code Message @Confirmed() confirmed The {field} confirmation does not match @Same('email') same The {field} must match {other} @RequiredIf('type', 'company') required_if The {field} is required when {other} is {values} @RequiredWith(['phone']) required_with The {field} is required when {others} is present @RequiredUnless('type', 'guest') required_unless The {field} is required unless {other} is {values} @RequiredWithout(['email']) required_without The {field} is required when {others} is not present @RequiredWithoutAll(['email', 'phone']) required_without_all The {field} is required when none of {others} are present @Different('old_password') different The {field} and {other} must be different @ProhibitedIf('type', 'guest') prohibited_if The {field} is prohibited when {other} is {values} @GreaterThanField('min_price') greater_than The {field} must be greater than {min} @GreaterThanOrEqualField('min_price') min The {field} must be greater than or equal {min} @LessThanField('max_price') less_than The {field} must be less than {max} @LessThanOrEqualField('max_price') max The {field} must be less than or equal {max}
  • @Confirmed() on password needs the key password_confirmation with the same value. The error is on password. Use @Confirmed(other: 'password_again') for another key. The DTO does not need a field for the confirmation key.
  • Text and numbers match by text, both ways: 1234 matches "1234", and "1234" matches 1234.
  • @RequiredIf and @RequiredWith work on a nullable field, a Maybe field or a field with a default. On an always-required field the build stops.
  • @RequiredIf('type', ['company', 'shop']) takes a list: any of the values makes the field required. "true" matches true, "1" matches 1. An enum value matches its name: @RequiredIf('role', Role.admin) matches "admin".
  • @RequiredWith(['phone', 'email']): the field is required when any of the keys is there and not empty.
  • @RequiredUnless('type', 'guest') makes the field required unless type is guest. A missing type counts as null, so the field is required then. It takes a list of values like @RequiredIf.
  • @RequiredWithout(['email']): the field is required when any of the keys is missing or empty. @RequiredWithoutAll(['email', 'phone']): when all of them are missing or empty.
  • @RequiredUnless, @RequiredWithout and @RequiredWithoutAll follow the same rules as @RequiredIf: a nullable, Maybe or default field, and input keys.
  • @Different('old_password') needs a value that is not the same as the other key. It compares the raw input like @Same. A missing other key passes.
  • @ProhibitedIf('type', 'guest') means: when type is guest, the field must be missing or empty. Empty is null, blank text, an empty list or an empty map. 0 and false fail. This is not the same as @Prohibited(), which fails on null and []. It reads type and matches like @RequiredIf.
  • @GreaterThanField, @GreaterThanOrEqualField, @LessThanField and @LessThanOrEqualField compare a value with another field. They are for int, double and num fields. They read the raw input of the other key: a number, or number text from a form. A missing other key (or one that is not a number) fails. {min} and {max} in the message are the other key. They use the codes of @GreaterThan, @Min, @LessThan and @Max.
  • On a List<T> field, @Different checks the whole list, not each item. The field compare rules do not fit a list.
  • Missing means: not there, null, blank text, an empty list or an empty map.
  • They run in step 1, with the other "required" checks. @Confirmed and @Same run in step 2.

docs.title: Present or missing
docs.text:
These check if a key is sent and has a value.

Annotation Code Message @Filled() filled The {field} must have a value @Present() present The {field} must be present @Prohibited() prohibited The {field} is prohibited @Accepted() accepted The {field} must be accepted @Declined() declined The {field} must be declined
  • @Filled(): a missing key passes. A key that is sent must have a value: not null, not blank text, not an empty list.
  • @Present(): the key must be sent. Its value may be null or empty.
  • @Filled() and @Present() are for a nullable, Maybe or default field, like @RequiredIf. They run in step 1.
  • @Prohibited(): the key must be missing, or blank text like "" or " ". Any other sent value fails, also null, [], {}, 0 and false. It reads the raw input, so it runs before the type check, in step 1. It is for a nullable, Maybe or default field.
  • @Accepted() takes true, 1, "1", "true", "yes" and "on". @Declined() takes false, 0, "0", "false", "no" and "off". The text is case sensitive. Use them on a bool field with no default. Then a missing value fails with required. In a form, yes and on turn into true first. In a JSON body a bool field takes only true and false, unless the DTO has @Dto(coerce: true).
@Accepted()
final bool terms;

@Present()
final String? note; // the key must be there, null is fine

docs.title: Skip a field
Change text
docs.text:
These change the value before the rules run. They always run in this order, wherever you put them: @Trim, then @Lowercase or @Uppercase, then the "empty string is missing" check.

Annotation Does @Trim() removes spaces at the start and the end @Lowercase() makes the text lower case @Uppercase() makes the text upper case @AllowEmpty() keeps "" as a value. Without it, "" counts as missing.

They have no error and no JSON Schema output. @Lowercase() and @Uppercase() together stop the build.

docs.title: Bad value to default
docs.text:
Annotation Does @OrDefault() a bad value gives the default of the field (or null, or Maybe.missing()), not an error.
  • It drops type errors and the errors of the normal rules of the field.
  • Errors from async rules (@Unique, @Exists, your AsyncRule) and from validate() are not dropped. They still give 422.
  • The field needs a default, a nullable type or a Maybe type. Else the build stops.

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
For int, double and num fields (and list items).

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @Min(18) min The {field} must be greater than or equal {min} minimum @Max(100) max The {field} must be less than or equal {max} maximum @Range(1, 10) between The {field} must be between {min} and {max} minimum, maximum @Positive() greater_than The {field} must be greater than 0 exclusiveMinimum: 0 @GreaterThan(0.5) greater_than The {field} must be greater than {min} (exclusive) exclusiveMinimum @LessThan(100) less_than The {field} must be less than {max} (exclusive) exclusiveMaximum @In([1, 2, 3]) in The selected {field} is invalid. Valid options are {values} enum @NotIn([0]) not_in The {field} field cannot be {value} not: {enum}

The values are num. @Min(1.5) on an int field stops the build. @Range checks that a number is between two values.

docs.title: Lists
docs.text:
For List<T> fields. These check the list, not the items.

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @MinItems(1) min_items The {field} must have at least {min} items minItems @MaxItems(5) max_items The {field} may not have more than {max} items maxItems @UniqueItems() unique_items The {field} must not have duplicate items uniqueItems: true

@UniqueItems() works for String, numbers, bool, enums and DateTime. On a list of DTOs it stops the build.

docs.title: Dates
docs.text:
For DateTime fields.

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @After('2000-01-01') after The {field} must be a date after {date} format: date-time @Before('now') before The {field} must be a date before {date} format: date-time @AfterOrEqual('today') after_or_equal The {field} must be a date after or equal to {date} format: date-time @BeforeOrEqual('end_date') before_or_equal The {field} must be a date before or equal to {date} format: date-time
  • The value is one of:
    • an ISO 8601 date, like '2000-01-01',
    • a word: 'now' (the time of the request), 'today', 'tomorrow' or 'yesterday'. These are in UTC, and 'today' is the start of the day,
    • the input key of another DateTime field of the same DTO, like 'start_date'.
  • With another field, the check uses its converted value. When that field has no value, the check passes.
  • A text that is not a date, a word or a DateTime field stops the build.
  • @After and @Before are exclusive: @After('2000-01-01') does not accept 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z. @AfterOrEqual and @BeforeOrEqual accept the same time.
  • Words and other fields need one build_runner run.
final DateTime startDate;

@After('start_date')
@BeforeOrEqual('tomorrow')
final DateTime endDate;

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
For RequestFile and List<RequestFile> fields.

Annotation Code Message JSON Schema @MaxSize('2MB') max_size The {field} may not be larger than {max} maxLength (bytes) @Mimes(['pdf', 'png']) mimes The {field} must be a file of type: {types} contentMediaType @Image() image The {field} must be an image contentMediaType: image/* @MinSize('10KB') min_size The {field} must be at least {min} minLength (bytes) @MimeTypes(['image/png', 'image/*']) mime_types The {field} must be a file of type: {types} contentMediaType @Dimensions(minWidth: 100, ratio: 3 / 2) dimensions The {field} has invalid image dimensions contentMediaType: image/*
  • @MaxSize and @MinSize units: B, KB, MB, GB. 1KB = 1024 bytes. A bad size text stops the build.
  • @Mimes takes file extensions. Dox finds the real type from the first bytes of the file. The file name extension must not name another type, or a type a browser runs (like html or svg). So x.html with GIF bytes does not pass. An empty or unknown extension is fine. For zip based types (like docx or xlsx), the file name extension must match too. For types without a byte signature (like txt or csv), it uses the file name extension.
  • @Image() is @Mimes(['jpg', 'jpeg', 'png', 'gif', 'webp', 'bmp']). No svg.
  • @MimeTypes takes MIME types. Dox turns each one into file extensions, then checks the real bytes like @Mimes. It does not trust the content type the client sent. image/* means: jpg, jpeg, png, gif, webp, bmp, tif, tiff, ico, heic, heif, avif and psd. No svg. This is wider than @Image(), and browsers can not show most of the extra types. For images that browsers can show, use @Image() or list the MIME types. Write image/jpeg, not image/jpg. image/jpg is not a real MIME type, so it never matches. An unknown MIME type never matches.
  • @Dimensions checks the width and height in pixels. Limits: width, height (exact), minWidth, maxWidth, minHeight, maxHeight and ratio (width / height, like 3 / 2). Give at least one limit, or the build stops. It reads only the image header of PNG, GIF, WebP and JPEG files, never the whole file. Any other file, or a broken or cut short header, fails. For a JPEG over 1 MB, Dox reads the first 128 KB. A JPEG with more photo metadata than that before its size fails. A ratio passes when it is off by less than one pixel.
  • The JSON Schema of a file is {"type": "string", "format": "binary"}, plus the keys above.

With fluent schemas, the same rules are on v.file(). Sizes there are in bytes, not text:

v.file()
    .maxSize(2 * 1024 * 1024) // 2 MB
    .mimeTypes(<String>['image/jpeg', 'image/png'])
    .dimensions(minWidth: 100, maxWidth: 2000);

The fluent methods are maxSize(bytes), minSize(bytes), mimes(types), mimeTypes(types), dimensions(...), image() and extensions(types).

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
From dox_orm. Async: they run after all other checks passed.

Annotation Code Message @Unique(table, {column, ignoreParam, ignoreColumn, connection}) unique The {field} has already been taken @Exists(table, {column, connection}) exists The selected {field} is invalid
  • @Unique column default: the input key. @Exists column default: id.
  • They read the table, not the model. So soft-deleted rows count too.
  • ignoreParam: 'id' skips the row where ignoreColumn (default id) equals the path param {id}.
  • They add nothing to the JSON Schema.

See Database rules.

In a fluent schema, use v.string().unique('users', column: 'email') and v.int().exists('teams'). See Fluent schemas.

docs.title: Keys and DTO options
docs.text:
Annotation Does @Name('emailAddress') the input key for this field. Default: the field name in snake_case. @Dto() marks the class. @Dto(source: Source.query) where to read: Source.auto (default), Source.query, Source.body. @Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field) keys: KeyCase.snake (default) or KeyCase.field (the Dart name as is). @Dto(strict: true) unknown keys are errors. Default false: they are dropped. @Dto(emptyStringsToNull: true) "" is read as null, not as missing. Default false. @Dto(trim: true) trims every String field and text item, like @Trim() on each. Default false. @Dto(coerce: true) a JSON body may send text for numbers and bools, like a form. Default false. @Dto(messages: {...}) messages by code or key.code. A dotted path like address.city.required or tags.*.required works too. A Laravel rule name works too, like name.min. See Messages. @Dto(attributes: {...}) the names shown for {field}, by key, like {'first_name': 'first name'}. See Names for {field}. @Describe('...') on a field: a short text for the description of the field in the JSON Schema. It does not change the checks.

A /// doc comment on a field becomes its description in the JSON Schema. @Describe wins over the /// comment. Use it when the text is for API users and MCP clients, not for the code. The OpenAPI docs and MCP tools (McpDtoTool) show it.

@Describe('Category ID (see list_categories).') final int categoryId;

docs.title: Types in detail
docs.text:
How each field type reads input. The short table is in Types.

  • JSON is strict. In a JSON body, "18" is not an int. You get the error integer. With @Dto(coerce: true), JSON is read like form text for int, double, num and bool, and a bool also takes 1 and 0.
  • Query and form data are text. Dox turns the text into the field type first. If it can not, you get the type error.
  • int takes 18 or 18.0, never a fraction. "4.5" or 4.5 gives integer.
  • bool in text takes true, 1, yes, on and false, 0, no, off (any case).
  • DateTime takes 2024-01-31 or 2024-01-31T10:00:00Z. A value without a time zone is read as UTC. The result is always UTC (isUtc == true). A number (timestamp) is not allowed.
  • An enum matches the Dart name exactly. "Admin" does not match Role.admin. Custom wire values (like "ADMIN") are not supported.
  • Object? and dynamic take any value. They are not checked.
  • Map<String, dynamic> must be an object. Its values are not checked.
  • In query and form data, one value for a List<T> field gives a list with one item.
  • In bracket keys, list indexes are sorted and packed: items[3] alone gives a list with one item.
  • In query and form data, a list can have at most 1000 items, and keys can nest at most 10 levels. More gives 422 with the key _root.

docs.title: Body types
docs.text: Body Result application/json (or any +json type) read with strict JSON types application/x-www-form-urlencoded, multipart/form-data read as text, then converted any other content type 415 Unsupported Media Type JSON that is not valid 400 Bad Request JSON that is not an object (like [1, 2]) 422 with the key _root

docs.title: The order of checks
docs.text:
1. Read the input and convert types. Change text (@Trim, @Lowercase, @Uppercase). Find missing required fields.
  2. The field rules, top to bottom. The first rule that fails stops the other rules of that field. So there is no @Bail. A fluent schema runs all rules, unless you add .bail(). See Stop at the first error.
  3. The validate() method (nested DTOs first, then the parent).
  4. Async rules (@Unique, @Exists, your AsyncRule), one at a time, in field order.

Each step runs only when the step before it had no errors. So the database is never asked about input that is already wrong.

  • Steps 1 and 2 run per DTO. So one answer can have a type error in address and a rule error in items.1.
  • Inside one step, Dox collects the errors of all fields.
  • A default value is not checked by the field rules. Async rules check the final value.

docs.title: What the generator checks
docs.text:
The build stops with a clear error when:

  • a field is not final, or is not a parameter of the unnamed constructor,
  • a field type is not supported (see Types),
  • a rule does not fit the field type (like @Email() on an int),
  • a Maybe<T> field has no const Maybe.missing() default,
  • @RequiredIf, @RequiredWith, @RequiredUnless, @RequiredWithout, @RequiredWithoutAll, @Filled, @Present, @Prohibited, @ProhibitedIf, @ExcludeIf or @ExcludeUnless is on a field that is always required,
  • @OrDefault() is on a field that is always required (no default, not nullable and not a Maybe),
  • a rule that reads another key (like @RequiredIf, @Same, @Different, @ExcludeIf or @GreaterThanField) names a Dart field (like accountType) instead of its input key (account_type),
  • @After, @Before, @AfterOrEqual or @BeforeOrEqual has a text that is not a date, a word or another DateTime field,
  • @DateFormatted has a letter it does not know,
  • two @Dto classes in the app have the same name,
  • the class is generic, or extends another class (other than Object).

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
This page shows how to check request input with typed DTO classes.

Write a class with @Dto(). Ask for it in your controller. Dox reads the request, checks it, and gives you a typed object. When the input is wrong, Dox answers 422 with the errors. Your controller does not run.

lib/app/dtos/create_user/create_user.dto.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'create_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class CreateUser {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 3, max: 50)
  final String name;

  @Email()
  final String email;

  @MinLength(8)
