  final String password;

  @Min(18)
  final int? age; // nullable, so optional

  const CreateUser({
    required this.name,
    required this.email,
    required this.password,
    this.age,
  });

  static const DtoSchema<CreateUser> schema = $CreateUserDto;
}
lib/app/http/controllers/user.controller.dart
class UserController {
  Future<User> store(CreateUser body) async {
    // body is already checked
    User user = User()
      ..name = body.name
      ..email = body.email
      ..password = await Hash.makeAsync(body.password);
    await user.save();
    return user;
  }
}

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
You do this once per app.

  1. Make a DTO with dox make:dto CreateUser. It writes lib/app/dtos/create_user/create_user.dto.dart.
  2. Run the generator: dox build_runner:build (or dox build_runner:watch). It writes a .dto.g.dart file next to each DTO, and one list of all DTOs in lib/generated/dtos.g.dart.
  3. Give that list to the app:
lib/config/app.dart
import 'package:my_app/generated/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  dtos: dtos, // from lib/generated/dtos.g.dart
  // ...
);

Dox uses no reflection, so it needs this list to find your DTOs. Without it, the server stops at start with a clear error.

docs.title: Use a DTO
docs.text:
Add a parameter with the DTO type. Dox checks the request before your method runs.

Future<User> store(CreateUser body) async { ... }

// with the request and a path param
Future<User> update(DoxRequest req, int id, UpdateUser body) async { ... }

Or check inside the method. req.validate<T>() returns the object, or throws the 422 error.

CreateUser data = await req.validate<CreateUser>();

See Controller: parameters for the full rules.

docs.title: Required and optional
docs.text:
The Dart type decides. You do not write required or nullable.

Field Key missing Value null final String name; error required error required final int? age; null null final Role role; with this.role = Role.user Role.user error required
  • Rules on an optional field run only when it has a value.
  • A default value is used only when the key is missing. The rules do not check it.
  • An empty string counts as missing. So a required String rejects "". Add @AllowEmpty() to keep "".
  • Spaces are kept. So " " passes required, unless the field has @Trim(). To trim every text field of a DTO, use @Dto(trim: true). Then " " counts as missing. It works like @Trim() on each String field and on the text items of its lists and maps. A nested DTO uses its own @Dto(trim:).
  • To read "" as null instead, use @Dto(emptyStringsToNull: true). With @Dto(trim: true) too, blank text like " " is null as well. Then {"bio": ""} clears a Maybe<String?> field. A required field still gets required. A field that is not nullable but has a default gets required too, because null is not a missing key.
  • @OrDefault() turns a bad value into the default, with no error.
    • It works on any field, in a body or a query.
    • Example: @OrDefault() @NotIn(<int>[0]) final int page; with this.page = 1 reads page=abc and page=0 as 1.
    • The field needs a default, a nullable type or a Maybe type. A Maybe field gets Maybe.missing().
    • Errors from async rules (@Unique, @Exists, your AsyncRule) and from validate() are not dropped. They run later, on the built object, and still give 422.
  • Three opt-in flags change how DTOs are checked: get all errors at once, reject [] in a required list, and reject "" in a Maybe field.

docs.title: Missing or null? (for PATCH)
docs.text:
A T? field gives null for both. To know the difference, use Maybe<T>:

@Length(max: 500)
final Maybe<String?> bio; // default: const Maybe.missing()

// in the controller
if (body.bio.isPresent) {
  user.bio = body.bio.value; // can be null: the client cleared it
}

docs.title: Types
Where the data comes from
docs.text:
Request Dox reads GET, HEAD, DELETE the query string POST, PUT, PATCH the body (JSON, form or multipart)

Dox reads one source. It never mixes the query and the body. To choose the source yourself:

@Dto(source: Source.query) // on the DTO
class SearchUsers { ... }

await req.validate<SearchUsers>(source: Source.query); // for one call

Path params are not part of a DTO. Ask for them as controller parameters, like int id.

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
The input key is the field name in snake_case: firstName reads first_name.

final String firstName; // key: first_name

@Name('emailAddress')
final String email; // key: emailAddress
  • @Dto(keyCase: KeyCase.field) uses the field names as they are.
  • Unknown keys are dropped. With @Dto(strict: true), an unknown key is an error.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
Put rules on a field as annotations. They run from top to bottom. The first rule that fails gives the error.

@Trim()
@Lowercase()
@Email()
@MaxLength(255)
final String email;
Kind Annotations Text @Length, @MinLength, @MaxLength, @Email, @Url, @Uuid, @Ulid, @Ip, @Regex, @In, @NotIn, @StartsWith, @EndsWith, @Alpha, @AlphaNumeric, @AlphaDash Change text @Trim, @Lowercase, @Uppercase, @AllowEmpty Numbers @Min, @Max, @Range, @Positive, @GreaterThan, @LessThan, @In, @NotIn Lists @MinItems, @MaxItems, @UniqueItems Dates @After, @Before, @AfterOrEqual, @BeforeOrEqual Other fields @Same, @Confirmed, @Different, @GreaterThanField, @GreaterThanOrEqualField, @LessThanField, @LessThanOrEqualField, @ProhibitedIf Present or missing @RequiredIf, @RequiredUnless, @RequiredWith, @RequiredWithout, @RequiredWithoutAll, @Filled, @Present, @Prohibited, @Accepted, @Declined Skip a field @ExcludeIf, @ExcludeUnless Files @MaxSize, @MinSize, @Mimes, @MimeTypes, @Image, @Dimensions Database @Unique, @Exists

Every rule, with its error code and message, is in Validation rules.

  • A rule on a list checks each item: @Email() on a List<String>. Only the list rules check the list itself.
  • For a few allowed values, use a Dart enum, or @In(<String>['draft', 'published']).

docs.title: Nested objects and lists
docs.text:
A field can be another @Dto class, or a list of them.

@Dto()
class CreateOrder {
  final Address address;

  @MinItems(1)
  final List<OrderItem> items;

  const CreateOrder({required this.address, required this.items});

  static const DtoSchema<CreateOrder> schema = $CreateOrderDto;
}

Address and OrderItem are @Dto classes too. An error in a nested value has a path key, like items.1.quantity.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
A RequestFile field reads a file from multipart/form-data.

@Image()
@MaxSize('2MB')
@Dimensions(minWidth: 100, maxWidth: 2000)
final RequestFile avatar;

@Mimes(<String>['pdf', 'docx'])
final List<RequestFile> documents;

Dox checks the real file type from its first bytes. It does not trust the file name or the client. To save the file, see File upload.

docs.title: Checks across fields: validate()
docs.text:
Add a validate(DtoErrors errors) method to the DTO. Dox calls it after all field rules passed.

void validate(DtoErrors errors) {
  if (password != passwordConfirmation) {
    errors.add('password_confirmation', 'The passwords do not match');
  }
}
  • The key is the input key (snake_case). Use _root for an error about the whole body.
  • errors.has(key) tells you if a key already has an error.
  • The method can be async. Do not throw for bad input. Add an error.

docs.title: Database rules: @Unique and @Exists
docs.text:
These read the database, so they run last. They come from dox_orm. Add import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart'; to the DTO file.

@Unique('users', column: 'email')
final String email;

@Exists('teams') // column defaults to id
final int teamId;

For an update, skip the row you are updating with ignoreParam:

// PUT /users/{id}
@Unique('users', column: 'email', ignoreParam: 'id')
final String email;

All options are in Validation rules: database. The full order of checks is in The order of checks.

docs.title: The error response
docs.text:
When a check fails, Dox answers 422 with one message per field:

{
  "email": "The email is not a valid email",
  "tags.0": "The tags may not be greater than 20 characters",
  "items.1.quantity": "The quantity must be greater than 0"
}

The key is the path to the value, with the input keys. List items use the index.

The flag laravelErrors sends {"message": "...", "errors": {"field": ["..."]}} instead. See Core flags.

For another error shape, read error.issues of the ValidationException in your ExceptionHandler. Each issue has its dottedPath, its rule code (like min_length), its message and its params.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
Change a message in one of these places. The first one wins.

  1. On the rule: @Email(message: 'Please check your email').
  2. On the DTO, by code or by key.code. A full dotted path works too, like 'address.city.required' (it also reaches a nested DTO). A message in the nested DTO itself, like 'city.required', wins over it. Use * for list items, like 'tags.*.required':
@Dto(messages: <String, String>{
  'email.required': 'We need your email',
  'integer': 'The {field} must be a number',
})
  1. For the whole app, with a MessageResolver. Use it for other languages:
class AppMessages extends MessageResolver {
  static const Map<String, Map<String, String>> _texts = <String, Map<String, String>>{
    'th': <String, String>{'required': 'กรุณากรอก {field}'},
  };

  @override
  String resolve(MessageRequest request) {
    String? template = _texts[request.locale]?[request.code]; // locale from Accept-Language
    if (template == null) {
      return super.resolve(request);
    }
    return format(template, request.params);
  }
}

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  validationMessages: AppMessages(),
  // ...
);

Placeholders: {field} (the last key), {value}, and rule values like {min} and {max}.

docs.title: Names for {field}
docs.text:
By default {field} is the key, like The first_name is required. To show another name, give attribute names. A key with no name still shows the key.

On the DTO:

@Dto(attributes: <String, String>{'first_name': 'first name'})
class CreateUser { ... }
// The first name is required

For the whole app (and for fluent schemas), in the MessageResolver:

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  validationMessages: MessageResolver(
    attributes: <String, String>{'first_name': 'first name'},
  ),
  // ...
);
  • A name is looked up by the dotted path (address.city), then with * for list items (items.*.qty), then by the field name (city).
  • The names of the DTO win over the names of the MessageResolver. A nested DTO uses its own names first, then the names of the outer DTO.
  • MessageResolver.setAttributes(...) adds names to a resolver. A custom resolver can override attributeName(path).
  • {other} and {others} (the other keys of rules like @RequiredIf and @Same) show their names too.
  • The error path and the key in the error response do not change. Only the text does.
  • @Dto(attributes:) needs one build_runner run.

docs.title: Laravel rule names in message keys
docs.text:
Some Dox codes have another name in Laravel. With the opt-in flag laravelMessageKeys, a message key can use the Laravel name too. So 'name.min' gives the message for the min_length error of name. Without the flag, only the Dox codes match.

Validator.flags = const ValidationFlags(laravelMessageKeys: true);

Set it in a provider's setup(), like the other flags. The error code in the response does not change: it is still min_length.

At each step of the lookup, the Dox code is tried first, then the Laravel name. So 'name.min_length' wins over 'name.min'. A key with a path still wins over a key with only a code: 'name.min' wins over 'min_length'.

Dox code Laravel name min_length min max_length max length size length_between between start_with starts_with end_with ends_with alpha_numeric alpha_num greater_than gt less_than lt min_items min max_items max unique_items distinct min_size min max_size max mime_types mimetypes datetime date

This works in @Dto(messages:) and in a MessageResolver. A code with the same name in both (like email or required) needs nothing. With the flag on, a message key min or max with no path fits text, list and file errors too, not only numbers.

docs.title: Custom rules
docs.text:
Extend Rule<T>. T is the field type (or the item type, for a list).

class Slug extends Rule<String> {
  const Slug({super.message});

  @override
  String get name {
    return 'slug'; // the error code
  }

  @override
  String get defaultMessage {
    return 'The {field} must be a slug';
  }

  @override
  bool check(String value, RuleContext context) {
    return _pattern.hasMatch(value);
  }

  static final RegExp _pattern = RegExp(r'^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$');
}

// use it
@Slug()
final String slug;
  • A rule with values: add final fields and override params. They become placeholders.
  • context.lookup('other.key') reads another input value.
  • context.sibling('key') reads the raw input of a field next to this one, in the same object. For example, context.sibling('password_confirmation') in a rule on password. It gives undefined when the field is missing.
  • A rule that needs the database: extend AsyncRule<T> and write checkAsync.

docs.title: Dynamic input
docs.text:
When the shape is known only at runtime (like form fields from the database), use a fluent schema:

Map<String, dynamic> data = await req.validateSchema(v.object(fields));

See Fluent schemas. Use a DTO for everything else.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
A DTO is a normal Dart class. Make one directly to skip the checks:

CreateUser input = const CreateUser(
  name: 'Ann',
  email: 'ann@dox.dev',
  password: 'secret123',
);

To test the checks, use safeValidateMap. It never throws:

ParseResult<CreateUser> result = await CreateUser.schema.safeValidateMap(<String, dynamic>{
  'name': 'A',
  'email': 'not-an-email',
  'password': 'secret123',
});

expect(result.success, isFalse);
expect(result.errors['email'], 'The email is not a valid email');
  • validateMap does the same, but returns the object or throws.
  • source: Source.query reads the map like a query string. params: {'id': '5'} gives path params.
  • @Unique and @Exists need a test database.

docs.title: Views
docs.text:
Views are HTML templates.

Dox fills them with your data and sends them as the response.

The dox_view package has a template engine like Edge.js. Templates are .dox.html files in resources/views.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
dox add view

It adds the package, the provider, the resources/views folder and a sample view. It never overwrites a file, so it is safe to run twice.

docs.title: Set it up by hand
docs.text:
dart pub add dox_view

Add the provider in lib/, so every isolate sets up the engine:

lib/providers/view_provider.dart
import 'package:dox_view/dox_view.dart';

class AppViewProvider extends ViewProvider {
  AppViewProvider() : super(const ViewConfig());
}

To make a view file, run dox make:view emails/welcome. It writes resources/views/emails/welcome.dox.html. See dox make:view.

docs.title: Render a view
docs.text:
view() renders a template and sends it as HTML. Leave out the .dox.html extension.

DoxResponse show(DoxRequest req) {
  return view(req, 'users/show', <String, dynamic>{
    'user': user,
    'posts': posts,
  });
}

This renders resources/views/users/show.dox.html:

<h1>{{ user.name }}</h1>

View.render() gives the HTML as a string, for example for an email:

String html = View.render('emails/welcome', <String, dynamic>{'name': 'Ann'});

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
{{ }} prints a value. It escapes HTML, so a user can not add a <script> tag to your page.

<p>Hello {{ user.name }}</p>

{{{ }}} prints a value with no escape. Use it only for HTML you trust.

<article>{{{ post.html }}}</article>

null prints nothing. true prints true, false prints false, and 10.0 prints 10.0. A variable that does not exist prints nothing. The bladeOutput and strictVariables options change this. See Strict options.

A comment is not in the output:

{{-- only you see this --}}

To print {{ or a tag as text, put @ before it: @{{ name }} prints {{ name }}, and @@if prints @if.

docs.title: Stay safe
docs.text:
{{ }} escapes HTML. It does not make every place in a page safe.

  • Always quote attributes. Write href="{{ url }}", not href={{ url }}. Without quotes, a space in the value starts a new attribute, like onclick=....
  • Check URLs from users. href="{{ url }}" does not block a javascript: URL. A click on javascript:alert(1) runs the code. Allow only http:// and https:// URLs (or your own paths) before you print them.
  • <script> and <style> are not safe for {{ }}. Inside them, {{ }} only escapes HTML. It does not make a value safe for JavaScript or CSS. Do not print user data there with {{ }}. In a <script>, use @json. See JSON for JavaScript. Or put the value in a quoted data- attribute, and read it in your script.
<a href="{{ profile.website }}">Website</a>  {{-- only after you check it is http or https --}}

<div id="app" data-user-name="{{ user.name }}"></div>
<script>
  const name = document.getElementById('app').dataset.userName;
</script>

docs.title: Expressions
docs.text:
Inside {{ }} and tags, you can use:

What Example Values 'text', "text", 42, 1.5, true, false, null Lists and maps [1, 2], { name: 'Ann', 'full name': 'Ann Lee' } Fields user.name, user?.name, items[0], map['key'] Math +, -, *, /, %, ~/ Compare ==, !=, <, <=, >, >= (=== and !== work too) Logic &&, \|\|, !, a ?? b, a ? b : c Functions route('users.show', { id: 5 }), name.toUpperCase()

+ joins text: {{ 'Hi ' + name }}.

Fields work on maps, and on objects with a toJson() method, like Dox models.

Lists, maps and text have length, isEmpty and isNotEmpty. Lists also have first, last, contains(), join() and indexOf(). Text has toUpperCase(), toLowerCase(), trim(), contains(), startsWith(), endsWith(), split(), replaceAll(), substring() and indexOf(). Numbers have toStringAsFixed(), round(), floor(), ceil() and abs().

In @if and ?:, these values are false: null, false, 0, '', an empty list and an empty map. With the stringZeroIsFalse option, the text '0' is false too. See Strict options.

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text:
@if(user.isAdmin)
  <a href="/admin">Admin</a>
@elseif(user.isEditor)
  <a href="/posts">Posts</a>
@else
  <p>Welcome</p>
@end

@unless(x) is @if(!x).

A tag alone on its line leaves no empty line in the output.

A tag can not come right after a letter or a digit, so me@mail.com stays text. Put a space before the tag, or use {{ on ? 'active' : '' }}.

docs.title: Loops
docs.text:
<ul>
  @each(user in users)
    <li>{{ user.name }}</li>
  @else
    <li>No users yet</li>
  @end
</ul>

The @else part shows when the list is empty.

Get the index too, or the key of a map:

@each((user, index) in users)
  {{ index + 1 }}. {{ user.name }}
@end

@each((value, key) in settings)
  {{ key }}: {{ value }}
@end

$loop tells you where the loop is:

@each(tag in tags)
  {{ tag }}{{ $loop.last ? '' : ', ' }}
@end
Field What it is $loop.index the round, from 0 $loop.iteration the round, from 1 $loop.first true in the first round $loop.last true in the last round $loop.count the number of items. $loop.length is the same. $loop.remaining the rounds left after this one $loop.even true when iteration is even: the 2nd, 4th, ... round $loop.odd true when iteration is odd: the 1st, 3rd, ... round $loop.depth 1 for a loop, 2 for a loop inside a loop $loop.parent the $loop of the loop around this one. null when there is none. 
@each(row in rows)
  @each(cell in row)
    <td class="{{ $loop.parent.odd ? 'light' : 'dark' }}">{{ cell }}</td>
  @end
@end

A loop in an @include counts the loop around the @include as its parent. A loop in a component starts at depth 1.

docs.title: Variables
docs.text:
@let makes a variable. @assign changes it.

@let(total = 0)
@each(item in cart)
  @assign(total = total + item.price)
@end
Total: {{ total }}

docs.title: Partials
docs.text:
@include puts another template in this one. It sees the same variables.

@include('partials/nav')

A map as the second argument gives more variables to the template:

@include('partials/card', { title: 'Profile', user: post.author })
  • The template sees the variables of the page and the map. On the same name, the map wins.
  • The map is only for this include. The page does not see it after the include.
  • A second argument that is not a map throws a ViewException.

@includeIf and @includeWhen include the template only when the condition is true. The two tags do the same. The condition is the first argument, the template name is the second, and the map is the third:

@includeIf(user, 'partials/account')
@includeWhen(user.isAdmin, 'partials/admin', { level: 2 })

docs.title: More tags
docs.text:
Close a block tag with @end. @else works in all of them, but not in @once and @verbatim.

Put @auth, @guest, @production, @once and @verbatim alone on their line. In the middle of text, like @once upon a time, they stay text.

With a space before the (, a tag can also be plain text. These rules decide:

  • In the middle of a line, it is a tag only when its args are one valid expression (one or two for @section and @yield). So text like see @class (see docs) stays text.
  • Alone on its line, it is a tag even when its args are not valid, unless a rule below says it stays text. Then the args give an error, like @class (see docs).
  • A tag with a body, like @isset, @empty, @env, @section and @push, also needs its own @end after it, on any line. The @end of a block around it does not count. So @empty (none) stays text, also alone on its line.
  • @extends, @section, @yield, @stack, @push, @prepend, @method and @error also need text in quotes as the first argument, on any line. So git @push (force) and an @error (see log) stay text, but @yield ('title') is a tag. If such a tag stays text, its @end gives the error "@end has no matching tag before it".
  • @json and @includeWhen are never tags with a space, on any line. So the @json (format) stays text.

With no space, like @empty(items) or @json(user), a tag is always a tag.

Tag What it does @isset(user.phone) ... @end shows when the value is not null. A field of null is not an error here. @empty(items) ... @end shows when the value is false: null, false, 0, '', an empty list or map. With stringZeroIsFalse, '0' too. @auth ... @end shows when the user is logged in (req.auth) @guest ... @end shows when the user is not logged in @env('local') ... @end shows when APP_ENV is this value. A list works too: @env(['local', 'staging']). Case does not matter. @production ... @end shows when APP_ENV is production @once ... @end shows only the first time in one render, for example a <script> in a component @verbatim ... @end prints the text as it is: no {{ }} and no tags run inside it @extends('layouts/app') the layout of the page. See Layouts with sections. @section('name') ... @end fills a section. Short form: @section('title', 'Home'). @yield('name') prints a section. @yield('title', 'My app') has a default. @stack('scripts') prints every push of the stack. See Stacks. @push('scripts') ... @end adds to the end of a stack @prepend('scripts') ... @end adds to the start of a stack @csrf the hidden _token field. See Forms. @method('PUT') the hidden _method field @error('email') ... @end shows when the field has a validation error. See Forms. @json(value) the value as JSON. See JSON for JavaScript. @includeWhen(condition, 'name') includes a template when the condition is true. See Partials. @datetime(...) a tag of your app. See Your own tags. 
@auth
  <a href="/logout">Log out</a>
@else
  <a href="/login">Log in</a>
@end

@auth and @guest use the req.auth that view() gets. In View.render there is no request, so @guest shows.

@verbatim ends at the first @end, so the text inside can not have @end. Use it for code of a JavaScript framework that also uses {{ }}:

@verbatim
  <div id="app">{{ message }}</div>
@end

These tags print an HTML attribute:

<a @class(['link', { active: isActive, muted: !isActive }])>Home</a>
<input type="checkbox" name="news" @checked(user.news)>
<option value="en" @selected(lang == 'en')>English</option>
<button @disabled(saving)>Save</button>
  • @class takes text, a map of class name to a condition, or a list of these. It prints class="..." with the names whose condition is true. The names are escaped.
  • @checked, @selected and @disabled print the attribute name when the value is true.

A tag can not come right after a letter or a digit. Write on @else off, not on@else off.

When resources/views/components/ has a template with the same name, like class.dox.html, the component wins.

docs.title: Layouts and components
docs.text:
A component is a template with its own props and slots. Use one for the page layout.

resources/views/layouts/main.dox.html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <title>{{ title ?? 'My app' }}</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <header>{{ $slots.header }}</header>
    <main>{{ $slots.main }}</main>
  </body>
</html>
resources/views/home.dox.html
@component('layouts/main', { title: 'Home' })
  @slot('header')
    <h1>Welcome</h1>
  @end

  <p>Hello {{ user.name }}</p>
@end
  • The second argument is the props. In the component they are variables (title), and also $props.title.
  • @slot('name') ... @end fills a named slot. Everything else goes into $slots.main.
  • A slot is HTML, so {{ }} does not escape it again.
  • $slot is the same as $slots.main. Both are always there. They are empty when the component has no body.
  • A component only sees its props, $props, $slots, $slot, $attributes, the globals and the request helpers of view() (see Forms). It does not see the variables of the page.

@!component(...) is a component with no body and no @end.

docs.title: Components as tags
docs.text:
A template in resources/views/components/ is also a tag with its name. A . in the tag is a folder.

resources/views/components/button.dox.html
<button class="btn btn-{{ type ?? 'primary' }}">{{ $slots.main }}</button>

@button({ type: 'danger' })
  Delete
@end

@!form.input({ name: 'email' })   {{-- components/form/input.dox.html --}}

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
$attributes has the props as HTML attributes. {{ $attributes }} prints them, like id="save" title="Save". The values are escaped.

$attributes.merge({ ... }) adds default attributes. A prop wins over a default, but class is joined:

<button {{ $attributes.merge({ class: 'btn', type: 'button' }) }}>{{ $slot }}</button>

@button({ class: 'btn-big', type: 'submit' })
  Save
@end

This prints <button class="btn btn-big" type="submit">.

Only text, numbers and true are attributes. true prints the name alone, like hidden. A number prints like {{ }}: 1.0 is title="1.0", or title="1" with bladeOutput. null, false, lists, maps and objects are left out. You can still read any prop, like $attributes.type.

$attributes keeps any attribute name, like onclick. So do not pass a map from the user as the props of a component.

docs.title: Layouts with sections
docs.text:
A page can also name its layout with @extends. The page fills sections. The layout prints them with @yield.

resources/views/layouts/app.dox.html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
  <head>
    <title>@yield('title', 'My app')</title>
  </head>
  <body>
    <main>@yield('content')</main>
  </body>
</html>
resources/views/home.dox.html
@extends('layouts/app')

@section('title', 'Home')

@section('content')
  <p>Hello {{ user.name }}</p>
@end
  • @extends must be the first thing in the template. A template can have only one.
  • @section('name') ... @end fills a section. The short form @section('title', 'Home') takes a value. The value is escaped, like {{ }}.
  • @yield('name') prints a section. With a second argument, like @yield('title', 'My app'), it prints that value when the page has no such section. The value is escaped too.
  • In a page with @extends, only the sections reach the layout. Text outside a section is not printed. @let and @push outside a section still work.
  • A section sees the variables of the page. The layout sees them too.
  • A layout can extend another layout. When a page and its layout fill the same section, the page wins.
  • The names of sections and stacks must be plain text in quotes, like 'title'.
  • The first @section with a name wins. So a @section inside @each keeps only the first round.
  • A @yield('s') that comes before the @section('s') in the same file prints nothing.
  • An @include or a component with its own @extends prints its layout in place. It shares the section names with the page.
  • A tag right after a letter or a digit, like L@yield('s'), stays text.

Use @extends for the page layout. Use a component when you need props or more than one copy on a page.

docs.title: Stacks
docs.text:
A stack collects HTML from many templates and prints it in one place. Use it for scripts and styles.

<head>
  @stack('styles')
</head>
<body>
  @yield('content')
  @stack('scripts')
</body>

@push('scripts')
  <script src="/js/chart.js"></script>
@end
  • @push('name') ... @end adds to the end of the stack. @prepend('name') ... @end adds to the start.
  • A push works from the page, its layout, an @include and a component.
  • @stack can come before the @push in the page. It still prints every push.
  • The pushes are printed in the order they run. A page with @extends runs before its layout.
  • Put @once inside @push in a component, so the script is added one time only.

@extends, @section, @yield, @stack, @push, @prepend, @method, @error, @json and @includeWhen need ( ). With no ( ), like @section in a sentence, they stay text. For a space before the (, see the rule in More tags.

docs.title: Forms
docs.text:
With SessionMiddleware, view() adds these to every template:

Name What it is csrfField() the hidden _token field for CsrfMiddleware. @csrf prints the same. csrfToken() the CSRF token errors the flashed validation errors, like errors.email old('email') the input of the request before session('key') a value from the session

If your app has a global named errors, the global shows when the request has no validation errors. When there are validation errors, they win over the global.

<form method="POST" action="/register">
  {{ csrfField() }}
  <input name="email" value="{{ old('email') }}">
  @error('email')
    <p class="error">{{ message }}</p>
  @end
  <button>Register</button>
</form>

@error('field') ... @end shows its body when errors has a message for the field. Inside the body, message is that message.

  • When the value in errors is a list, message is its first item.
  • With no error for the field, the body is not printed. An @else part is printed instead, when there is one.
  • With no session, and in View.render, there are no errors, so the body is not printed. It does not throw.
  • A name with dots, like @error('user.email'), reads the key 'user.email' of errors first. That is how the validator names a nested field. When there is no such key, it reads email inside user.
  • The name can be a variable, like @error(name) in an input component.
  • message is only there inside the body. After @end, a message variable of your page has its own value again.

@csrf prints the same hidden field as csrfField(). Put it alone on its line. With no session, @csrf throws a ViewException.

A browser form can only send GET and POST. For a PUT, PATCH or DELETE route, send a POST and add @method. It prints the hidden _method field that the MethodOverride middleware reads:

<form method="POST" action="/posts/{{ post.id }}">
  @csrf
  @method('PUT')
  <input name="title" value="{{ post.title }}">
  <button>Save</button>
</form>

This prints <input type="hidden" name="_token" value="..."> and <input type="hidden" name="_method" value="PUT">.

Every template from view() also has request.path, request.method and request.query.

Components and layouts see all of these too, so a layout can use request.path and a form component can use csrfField().

docs.title: Globals
docs.text:
Globals are variables and functions that every template can use. route() is there by default.

const ViewConfig(globals: <String, Object?>{'appName': 'My app'});

View.global('year', DateTime.now().year);
View.global('money', (num cents) => (cents / 100).toStringAsFixed(2));

<footer>{{ appName }} {{ year }}</footer>
<a href="{{ route('users.show', { id: user.id }) }}">Profile</a>
<p>{{ money(order.total) }}</p>

You can add globals before or after View.configure(). The engine keeps them. When a name is in both, the value in ViewConfig.globals wins.

Each isolate has its own engine. So add globals in your provider, after super.setup(). Then every isolate gets them:

lib/providers/view_provider.dart
class AppViewProvider extends ViewProvider {
  AppViewProvider() : super(const ViewConfig());

  @override
  void setup() {
    super.setup();
    View.global('year', DateTime.now().year);
  }
}

A value of type SafeString is printed with no escape:

View.global('logo', const SafeString('<img src="/logo.svg" alt="Logo">'));

docs.title: JSON for JavaScript
docs.text:
@json(value) prints a value as JSON. Use it to give data to JavaScript:

<script>
  const user = @json(user);
</script>

<div data-tags='@json(tags)'></div>
  • Maps, lists, text, numbers, true, false and null work. An object with a toJson() method works too, like a Dox model.
  • <, >, &, ' and the line separators U+2028 and U+2029 are written as \uXXXX. So a value can not close the <script> block or the attribute.
  • The output is safe in two places: inside a <script> block, and inside an attribute in single quotes. Do not put it in an attribute in double quotes: JSON has " in it, and that ends the attribute.
  • A value that can not be JSON, like a DateTime or an object with no toJson(), throws a ViewException.

json(value) is the same as a function. {{ json(value) }} prints the same text, and does not escape it again. Use it where you need an expression:

@!chart({ points: json(points) })

In Dart, SafeString.json(value) gives the same text.

docs.title: Your own tags
docs.text:
A directive is a tag that your app adds. Write a class with a render method. It gets the values between ( and ), and gives the text to print.

class DateTimeDirective implements ViewDirective {
  @override
  Object? render(List<Object?> args, Scope scope) {
    Object? value = args[0];
    DateTime time = value is DateTime ? value : DateTime.parse('$value');
    return '${time.day}/${time.month}/${time.year}';
  }
}

View.directive('datetime', DateTimeDirective());

<time>@datetime(post.createdAt)</time>
  • The text is escaped, like {{ }}. Give a SafeString to print HTML as it is. null prints nothing.
  • scope.lookup('name') reads a variable of the template.
  • A directive has no body and no @end.
  • The tag needs ( ). With no ( ), like @datetime in a sentence, it stays text.
  • The name can have letters, digits and _. The name of a built-in tag, like if, section or json, throws a ViewException.
  • When resources/views/components/ has a template with the same name, the component wins.
  • You can also give them in the config: ViewConfig(directives: <String, ViewDirective>{'datetime': DateTimeDirective()}).

Each isolate has its own engine. So add directives in your provider, after super.setup(), like globals.

docs.title: Config
docs.text:
Option Default What it does path resources/views the folder of the templates extension .dox.html the file extension cache on, but off when APP_ENV is development or local keep parsed templates in memory globals {} variables for every template directives {} your own tags, by name strictVariables false a variable that does not exist throws a ViewException. See Strict options. stringZeroIsFalse false the text '0' is false in a condition bladeOutput false print true as 1, false as nothing and 10.0 as 10 bladeWarnings true warn about Blade names that are not Dox tags. See Coming from Blade.

With the cache off, a changed template shows on the next request, with no restart.

docs.title: Strict options
docs.text:
These three options are off by default. Turn each one on in ViewConfig:

const ViewConfig(
  strictVariables: true,
  stringZeroIsFalse: true,
  bladeOutput: true,
);

strictVariables: a variable that does not exist throws a ViewException. The message has the name of the variable, the template and the line. So a typo like {{ titel }} shows as an error, not as an empty spot on the page. When it is off, a variable that does not exist prints nothing.

A variable that is there with the value null is fine. These ways to read a variable that may not exist never throw:

Code What it gives when user does not exist @isset(user) ... @end the body is not printed @empty(user) ... @end the body is printed {{ user ?? 'Guest' }} Guest {{ user?.name }} nothing

The rule covers the variable on the left of ?? and ?.. In {{ a ?? b ?? 'x' }}, both a and b can be missing. {{ user.name ?? 'Guest' }} still throws when user does not exist: write {{ user?.name ?? 'Guest' }}.

stringZeroIsFalse: the text '0' is false in @if, @unless, @empty, ?:, &&, ||, !, @class, @checked, @selected, @disabled, @includeIf and @includeWhen. Other text, like '0.0' or '00', is still true. When it is off, '0' is true, like any text that is not empty.

bladeOutput: {{ }} and {{{ }}} print true as 1, false as nothing, and a number with no fraction, like 10.0, as 10. The values of @yield, @section and @method, and the numbers in $attributes, are printed the same way. Joining text with + does not change: {{ 'a' + true }} is still atrue. When it is off, true prints true, false prints false, and 10.0 prints 10.0.

docs.title: Coming from Blade
docs.text:
Some Blade names are not Dox tags. Dox prints them as plain text. To help you find them, Dox writes a warning to stderr when it reads a template that has one:

dox_view: warning: posts/index:12 "@foreach" is not a Dox tag. Use "@each(item in items) ... @end".
Blade Dox {!! html !!} {{{ html }}} @foreach, @forelse, @for @each(item in items) ... @else ... @end @endif, @endforeach, @endsection and the other @end... names, @stop @end @switch @if ... @elseif ... @else ... @end @php, @endphp @let(name = value) @show @end, then @yield('name') @parent not there. Use @stack and @push to add content.
  • The output of the template does not change. The warning is only a hint.
  • Each warning is written one time.
  • @end... names warn anywhere in a line. The other names warn only with the ( right after the name, like @foreach(...), or alone on their line. So a sentence like the @foreach loop does not warn.
  • Text in a {{-- --}} comment, in @verbatim, and a name with @@ before it, do not warn. A name in an HTML comment, like <!-- @endif -->, does warn.
  • ViewConfig(bladeWarnings: false) turns the warnings off.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
A syntax error, or an error in an expression, throws a ViewException. The message has the template name and the line:

ViewException: expected ")" but found the end (in "users/show", line 12)

docs.title: Prettier
docs.text:
Prettier formats .html files, and it does not know the @ tags. Add this line to .prettierignore:

*.dox.html

docs.title: Build a blog API
docs.text:
This tutorial takes you from an empty folder to a small blog API that runs as one native binary.

Every step has the full code and a curl command to check it.

The finished project is on GitHub: examples/blog-api. CI builds it and runs its tests on every push, so the code on these pages keeps working.

docs.title: What you will build
docs.text:
A JSON API for blog posts.

Method Path Who What it does GET /api/posts anyone list all posts GET /api/posts/{id} anyone one post, or 404 POST /api/posts logged in user make a post (201, or 422 on bad input) PUT /api/posts/{id} logged in user change a post POST /api/auth/register anyone make an account, get a token POST /api/auth/login anyone log in, get a token GET /api/auth/user logged in user the user of the token

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Dart 3.13 or newer: dart --version.
  • curl, to call the API.
  • About 15 minutes.

You do not need Docker or a database server. The app uses SQLite, which is one file in your project.

docs.title: The steps
docs.text:
1. Create the project
  2. Model and migration
  3. Routes and controller
  4. Validation
  5. Login with dox_auth
  6. Test
  7. Build and deploy

docs.title: The finished project
docs.text:
Files that you make or change in this tutorial are marked with *. The template has more files (queue, scheduler, storage). This tree shows the ones that matter here.

blog/
├── bin/
│   ├── migrate.dart              runs the dox migration:* commands
│   ├── server.dart               runs the migrations, starts the server
│   └── queue.dart, schedule.dart, seed.dart
├── db/migration/
│   ├── ..._create_posts_table.dart   *
│   ├── ..._create_users_table.dart
│   └── migrations.dart           the list of migrations (Dox writes it)
├── lib/
│   ├── app/http/controllers/
│   │   ├── auth.controller.dart  *
│   │   └── post.controller.dart  *
│   ├── app/dtos/
│   │   ├── login_user/login_user.dto.dart   *
│   │   ├── register_user/register_user.dto.dart *
│   │   └── save_post/save_post.dto.dart    *
│   ├── app/models/
│   │   ├── post/post.model.dart  *
│   │   └── user/user.model.dart
│   ├── config/
│   │   ├── app.dart              * adds the DTO list
│   │   ├── database.dart
│   │   └── env.dart              the .env keys, typed
│   ├── routes/api.dart           *
│   ├── providers/
│   │   ├── auth_provider.dart    *
│   │   └── orm_provider.dart
│   └── generated/
│       ├── container.g.dart      * generated
│       └── dtos.g.dart           * generated
├── test/http_test.dart           *
├── .env                          made by dox create
├── Dockerfile
└── pubspec.yaml                  * adds dox_auth

Start with step 1: create the project.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the project
docs.text: This step makes a new Dox project, points it at SQLite, starts the dev server and calls the first route.

docs.title: 1. Install the CLI and make the project
docs.text:
dart pub global activate dox
dox create blog
cd blog
dart pub get

dox create downloads the dox-sample template from GitHub and names the package blog. So every import in this tutorial starts with package:blog/.

docs.title: 2. Use SQLite
docs.text:
dox create already made .env with a new random APP_KEY. The template already uses SQLite:

.env
APP_PORT=3000
APP_KEY=<your new random key>

DB_CONNECTION=sqlite
DB_NAME=db/dox.sqlite

Dox makes the file db/dox.sqlite at the first start. SQLite does not read the other DB_* lines. The app reads these keys through the typed class in lib/config/env.dart. See Environment variables.

The folder must exist

Dox makes the database file when it is missing, but not its folder. If you set DB_NAME=storage/blog.sqlite, run mkdir storage first.

docs.title: 3. Start the server
docs.text:
dox s

dox s runs the code generator and the server. It restarts the server when you save a .dart file. The first start is slower, because it compiles the SQLite library. At the first start it also runs the migrations of the template. The last line is a JSON log line with this message:

Server started at http://[::]:3000 with 8 isolate (native)

Open it at http://localhost:3000. The number of isolates is the number of CPU cores.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
In a second terminal:

curl -i http://localhost:3000/api/ping

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
...

pong

The route is in lib/routes/api.dart. The ApiRouter has the prefix api, so /ping is served at /api/ping.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Step 2: Model and migration

docs.title: Step 2: Model and migration
docs.text: This step makes the posts table with a Dart migration and a Post model for it.

docs.title: 1. Make the model and the migration
docs.text:
Stop dox s first with Ctrl+C. dox s restarts the server when a new file appears, and the server runs new migrations at start. So it would run the new migration before you add the columns.

dox make:model Post -m

This makes two files and updates one:

File What it is lib/app/models/post/post.model.dart the model (new) db/migration/<date>_create_posts_table.dart the migration (new) db/migration/migrations.dart the list of all Dart migrations. Dox writes it. Do not edit it.

The template already has bin/migrate.dart. The dox migration:* commands run it.

docs.title: 2. Add the columns to the migration
docs.text:
Open the new file in db/migration. Add title and body:

db/migration/2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table.dart
// ignore_for_file: file_names
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';

class CreatePostsTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('posts', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('title');
      table.text('body');
      table.timestamps();
    });
  }

  @override
  Future<void> down(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.dropIfExists('posts');
  }
}
  • table.id() makes an auto increment primary key on every database.
  • table.timestamps() makes created_at and updated_at. The model fills them.

docs.title: 3. Add the fields to the model
4. Run the migrations on server start
docs.text:
Nothing to change here. The template's bin/server.dart already runs the migrations before the server starts:

bin/server.dart
import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

void main() async {
  Dox().initialize(appConfig);

  await Migrator(
    migrations: migrations,
    config: databaseConfig.getConnectionConfig(),
  ).migrate();

  await Dox().startServer();
}

This also works in the native binary of step 7.

docs.title: 5. Run the migration and the generator
docs.text:
dox migration:run

Migrating: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table

The migration ran too early?

If dox s was still running, the posts table may already exist without title and body. Run dox migration:rollback, then dox migration:run again.

The model needs its generated file post.model.g.dart. dox s makes it while it runs. If dox s is not running, run the generator once:

dart run build_runner build

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
dox migration:status

Migration                                 Batch  Status
2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table   1      Ran
2026_10_25_000000000_create_queue_tables  1      Ran
2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table      2      Ran

The first two come with the template. The server ran them at the first start in step 1.

Now start the server again with dox s.

docs.title: Next
docs.text: Step 3: Routes and controller

docs.title: Step 3: Routes and controller
docs.text: This step adds a resource controller and the routes to list, create and show posts.

docs.title: 1. Make the controller
docs.text:
dox make:controller Post -r

-r makes a resource controller with the seven CRUD methods. Replace the file with this. It keeps only index, store and show:

lib/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart
import 'package:blog/app/models/post/post.model.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

@Inject()
class PostController {
  /// GET /api/posts
  Future<List<Post>> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    return Post().all();
  }

  /// POST /api/posts
  Future<DoxResponse> store(DoxRequest req) async {
    Post post = Post()
      ..title = req.input('title')
      ..body = req.input('body');
    await post.save();
    return response(post).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// GET /api/posts/{id}
  Future<Post> show(int id) async {
    Post? post = await Post().find(id);
    if (post == null) {
      throw NotFoundHttpException();
    }
    return post;
  }
}

How it works:

  • @Inject() puts the controller in the container. Dox makes it for you. dox s runs build_runner, which adds it to lib/generated/container.g.dart. A new project already has container: registerContainer in lib/config/app.dart, so you change nothing there.
  • A controller returns a model or a list of models. Dox sends it as JSON.
  • response(post).statusCode(201) sets the status code.
  • show(int id) gets the {id} from the URL. /api/posts/abc answers 404, because abc is not an int.
  • req.input('title') reads the body as it is. It is not checked yet. Step 4 fixes that.

docs.text: Step 4: Validation

docs.title: Step 4: Validation
docs.text:
This step checks the input of create and update with a @Dto class.

Bad input gets a 422 answer, and the controller does not run.

docs.title: 1. Make the DTO
docs.text:
dox make:dto SavePost

One class is enough for create and update, because both need the same fields. Replace the file with this:

lib/app/dtos/save_post/save_post.dto.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'save_post.dto.g.dart';

/// Typed, checked input. Run `dox build_runner:build` after a change.
@Dto()
class SavePost {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 3, max: 100)
  final String title;

  @Trim()
  @MinLength(10)
  final String body;

  const SavePost({required this.title, required this.body});

  static const DtoSchema<SavePost> schema = $SavePostDto;
}
  • A field that is not nullable and has no default is required.
  • The rules run from top to bottom. @Trim() removes spaces first. An empty string then counts as missing.
  • See Validation for all rules.

docs.title: 2. Give the DTO list to the app
docs.text:
The generator writes a list of all DTOs to lib/generated/dtos.g.dart. Dox needs this list, because it does not use reflection. Add two lines to lib/config/app.dart:

lib/config/app.dart
import 'package:blog/generated/dtos.g.dart';

AppConfig appConfig = AppConfig(
  /// DTOs (generated list in lib/generated/dtos.g.dart)
  dtos: dtos,

  // ... the rest stays the same
);

docs.title: 3. Use the DTO in the controller
docs.text:
Ask for SavePost as a parameter. Dox checks the body and gives you a typed object. This also adds update, so PUT /api/posts/{id} works:

lib/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart
import 'package:blog/app/dtos/save_post/save_post.dto.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/models/post/post.model.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

@Inject()
class PostController {
  /// GET /api/posts
  Future<List<Post>> index(DoxRequest req) async {
    return Post().all();
  }

  /// POST /api/posts
  Future<DoxResponse> store(SavePost body) async {
    Post post = Post()
      ..title = body.title
      ..body = body.body;
    await post.save();
    return response(post).statusCode(201);
  }

  /// GET /api/posts/{id}
  Future<Post> show(int id) async {
    return _find(id);
  }

  /// PUT /api/posts/{id}
  Future<Post> update(int id, SavePost body) async {
    Post post = await _find(id);
    post
      ..title = body.title
      ..body = body.body;
    await post.save();
    return post;
  }

  Future<Post> _find(int id) async {
    Post? post = await Post().find(id);
    if (post == null) {
      throw NotFoundHttpException();
    }
    return post;
  }
}

Route.resource in lib/routes/api.dart sees the new update method and adds PUT and PATCH /api/posts/{id}. You change nothing there.

docs.title: 4. Run the generator
docs.text:
dox s runs it for you. Without dox s:

dart run build_runner build

It writes lib/app/dtos/save_post/save_post.dto.g.dart and lib/generated/dtos.g.dart.

content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"title":"The title is required","body":"The body is required"}

HTTP/1.1 201 Created

{"id":1,"title":"Hello Dox (edited)","body":"My first post, edited.","created_at":"2026-10-22T13:58:14.062215Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T13:59:13.539886Z"}

docs.title: Step 5: Login with dox_auth
docs.text: This step adds register and login with a JWT token, and only lets a logged in user create or change posts.

docs.title: 1. Add the package
docs.text: dart pub add dox_auth

docs.title: 2. Make the users table
docs.text:
The template already has a User model in lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart:

lib/app/models/user/user.model.dart
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart';

part 'user.model.g.dart';

@DoxModel(table: 'users', softDelete: true)
class User extends UserGenerator {
  @override
  List<String> get hidden => <String>['password'];

  @Column()
  String? name;

  @Column()
  String? email;

  @Column()
  String? password;
}

password is in hidden, so it is never in the JSON. This matters: the token holds the user as JSON, and anyone can read a JWT.

The users table already exists. The template has its migration, and the server ran it at the first start in step 1:

db/migration/2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table.dart
class CreateUsersTable extends Migration {
  @override
  Future<void> up(Schema schema) async {
    await schema.create('users', (Table table) {
      table.id();
      table.string('name');
      table.string('email').unique();
      table.string('password');
      table.softDeletes();
      table.timestamps();
    });
  }
  // ...
}

table.softDeletes() makes the deleted_at column that softDelete: true needs. email is unique, so a second register with the same email fails.

docs.title: 3. Make the DTOs
docs.text:
dox make:dto RegisterUser
dox make:dto LoginUser
lib/app/dtos/register_user/register_user.dto.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';
import 'package:dox_orm/dox_orm.dart' hide Schema;

part 'register_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class RegisterUser {
  @Trim()
  @Length(min: 2, max: 50)
  final String name;

  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  @Unique('users', column: 'email')
  final String email;

  @MinLength(8)
  final String password;

  const RegisterUser({
    required this.name,
    required this.email,
    required this.password,
  });

  static const DtoSchema<RegisterUser> schema = $RegisterUserDto;
}

@Unique comes from dox_orm. It reads the database, so it runs after the other rules. dox_orm also has a class named Schema, so the import hides it.

lib/app/dtos/login_user/login_user.dto.dart
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

part 'login_user.dto.g.dart';

@Dto()
class LoginUser {
  @Trim()
  @Lowercase()
  @Email()
  final String email;

  final String password;

  const LoginUser({required this.email, required this.password});

  static const DtoSchema<LoginUser> schema = $LoginUserDto;
}

docs.title: 4. Set up the auth provider
docs.text:
A provider runs once in every isolate at start. This one tells dox_auth which model to use and how to sign tokens:

lib/providers/auth_provider.dart
import 'package:blog/app/models/user/user.model.dart';
import 'package:blog/config/env.dart';
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

/// Auth provider
/// --------------------------
/// Sets up JWT login with the User model.
/// Tokens are signed with APP_KEY and last 7 days.
class AppAuthProvider extends DoxProvider {
  @override
  void setup() {
    Auth.initialize(
      AuthConfig(
        defaultGuard: 'api',
        guards: <String, AuthGuard>{
          'api': AuthGuard(
            driver: JwtAuthDriver(
              secret: SecretKey(env.appKey),
              expiresIn: const Duration(days: 7),
            ),
            provider: AuthProvider(model: () => User()),
          ),
        },
      ),
    );
  }
}

Dox finds the provider by itself. Run dart run build_runner build and it is in lib/generated/container.g.dart. You do not add it to a list.

docs.title: 5. Write the auth controller
6. Protect the write routes
docs.text:
Replace Route.resource with single routes. The routes inside Route.middleware need a valid token:

lib/routes/api.dart
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/api.controller.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/auth.controller.dart';
import 'package:blog/app/http/controllers/post.controller.dart';
import 'package:dox_auth/dox_auth.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/dox_core.dart';

class ApiRouter extends Router {
  @override
  String get prefix => 'api';

  @override
  List<dynamic> get middleware => <dynamic>[];

  @override
  void register() {
    Route.get('/ping', (ApiController c) => c.pong);

    // Anyone can read posts.
    Route.get('/posts', (PostController c) => c.index);
    Route.get('/posts/{id}', (PostController c) => c.show);

    // Register and log in.
    Route.post('/auth/register', (AuthController c) => c.register);
    Route.post('/auth/login', (AuthController c) => c.login);

    // Only a logged in user can write posts.
    Route.middleware(<dynamic>[AuthMiddleware()], () {
      Route.get('/auth/user', (AuthController c) => c.user);
      Route.post('/posts', (PostController c) => c.store);
      Route.put('/posts/{id}', (PostController c) => c.update);
    });
  }
}

AuthMiddleware reads the Authorization: Bearer <token> header and loads the user. When the token is missing or wrong, it answers 401 Authentication failed. On a public route, AuthMiddleware(optional: true) loads the user when there is a good token, and lets guests through.

docs.title: 7. Run the generator
docs.text:
dart run build_runner build

dox s runs it for you. There is no new migration in this step, because the users table already exists.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
Register:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/register \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","password":"secret123"}'

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8
...

{"token":"eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIs...","user":{"id":1,"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","created_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z"}}

The same email again gives 422:

{"email":"The email has already been taken"}

A wrong password gives 401:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ann@example.com","password":"wrong"}'

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
...

{"code":"unauthorized","message":"Wrong email or password"}

Log in and keep the token in a shell variable:

TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/auth/login \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"ann@example.com","password":"secret123"}' \
  | sed -E 's/.*"token":"([^"]+)".*/\1/')
echo $TOKEN

A post without a token is refused:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Third post","body":"Written with a token."}'

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
...

{"code":"unauthorized","message":"Authentication failed"}

With the token it works:

curl -i -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/posts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"title":"Third post","body":"Written with a token."}'

HTTP/1.1 201 Created
...

{"id":3,"title":"Third post","body":"Written with a token.","created_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:08.094211Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:08.094211Z"}

Who am I:

curl http://localhost:3000/api/auth/user -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

{"id":1,"name":"Ann","email":"ann@example.com","created_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z","updated_at":"2026-10-22T14:01:07.827769Z"}

No password in the answer, because it is in hidden.

docs.text: Step 6: Test

docs.title: Step 6: Test
docs.text: This step writes one HTTP test for the list route and runs it.

docs.title: 1. Write the test
docs.text:
The template has test/http_test.dart. Replace it with this:

test/http_test.dart
import 'package:blog/config/app.dart';
import 'package:blog/config/database.dart';
import 'package:dox_core/testing.dart';
import 'package:dox_migration/dox_migration.dart';
import 'package:test/test.dart';

import '../db/migration/migrations.dart';

void main() {
  late DoxTestClient client;

  setUpAll(() async {
    await Migrator(
      migrations: migrations,
      config: databaseConfig.getConnectionConfig(),
    ).migrate();
    client = await DoxTestClient.start(appConfig);
  });

  tearDownAll(() async {
    await client.close();
  });

  test('GET /api/posts gives a list', () async {
    TestResponse res = await client.get('/api/posts');
    res.expectStatus(200).expectJson(isA<List<dynamic>>());
  });
}
  • DoxTestClient.start runs the app inside the test, on a free port. It does not clash with dox s.
  • It runs the migrations first, so the test also works on an empty database.
  • package:test is already in dev_dependencies of the template.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
dart test test/http_test.dart

00:01 +1: All tests passed!

Use another database for tests

The test uses the .env file, so it reads and writes db/dox.sqlite. To keep test data out of it, make a .env.testing file with DB_NAME=test.sqlite. dart test reads it on top of .env.

docs.text: Step 7: Build and deploy

docs.title: Step 7: Build and deploy
docs.text:
This step compiles the app to one native binary, runs it, and shows the Dockerfile of the project.

Never run production with dox s or dart run

They use the JIT compiler. It needs about 25 times more memory and starts slower. Build a native (AOT) binary for production.

docs.title: 1. Build the binary
docs.text:
dox build

Built with build_runner/aot in 1s; wrote 0 outputs.
Running build hooks...Running link hooks...
Generated: /.../blog/build/bundle/bin/server
[Dox] Built build/bundle. Run it with: cd build/bundle && ./bin/server

dox build runs the code generator, then dart build cli. The result is in build/bundle:

Path What it is bin/server the binary, about 10 MB. It needs no Dart SDK. bin/queue the queue worker. Run it as its own process. bin/schedule the scheduler. Run it as its own process. lib/ native libraries from build hooks, like libsqlite3. Keep it next to bin/. db/ your migrations. Your local SQLite file is not copied. .env.example a copy of the example env file.

docs.title: 2. Run the binary
docs.text:
The binary reads .env from the folder you start it in. Copy yours there. The db folder for the SQLite file is already in build/bundle.

cd build/bundle
cp ../../.env .env
./bin/server

Migrating: 2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table
Migrated: 2023_07_16_131937700_create_users_table
Migrating: 2026_10_25_000000000_create_queue_tables
Migrated: 2026_10_25_000000000_create_queue_tables
Migrating: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
Migrated: 2026_10_22_205345_create_posts_table
... "message":"Server started at http://[::]:3000 with 8 isolate (native)" ...

The migrations run again, because db/dox.sqlite is a new file in build/bundle. The migration list is compiled into the binary, so no source code is needed. On a server you can skip .env and set real environment variables. They win over .env.

docs.title: Check it
docs.text:
In a second terminal:

curl http://localhost:3000/api/ping
curl http://localhost:3000/api/posts

pong
[]

The list is empty, because this is a new database file. Stop the server with Ctrl+C.

docs.title: 3. Docker
docs.text:
The project has a Dockerfile. It builds the same bundle and copies it to an empty (scratch) image:

Dockerfile
FROM dart:stable AS build

# Resolve dependencies first, so this layer is cached.
WORKDIR /app
COPY pubspec.* ./
RUN dart pub get

COPY . .
RUN dart pub get --offline

# The dox CLI. `dox build` runs build_runner, then AOT-compiles
# bin/server.dart, bin/queue.dart and bin/schedule.dart with
# `dart build cli`. It puts all of them in build/bundle/bin, the native
# libraries in build/bundle/lib and the migrations in build/bundle/db.
# The queue worker and the scheduler run as their own processes:
# `/app/bin/queue work` and `/app/bin/schedule work`.
ARG DOX_VERSION=^3.2.0
RUN dart pub global activate dox "$DOX_VERSION"
RUN /root/.pub-cache/bin/dox build

# Lay out the final file tree:
# /app/bin/server, /app/bin/queue, /app/bin/schedule, /app/lib (native
# libraries), /app/db/migration, /app/storage and a writable /tmp
# (uploads bigger than 1 MB are streamed to a temp file).
RUN mkdir -p /out/app/storage /out/tmp \
  && chmod 1777 /out/tmp \
  && cp -r build/bundle/. /out/app/ \
  # the native HTTP server (Rust) needs libgcc_s, which /runtime/ does not have
  && LIBGCC=$(find / -name libgcc_s.so.1 -path '*lib*' | head -n 1) \
  && mkdir -p /out$(dirname $LIBGCC) && cp $LIBGCC /out$LIBGCC

# Minimal serving image: the AOT runtime files from the dart image
# (`/runtime/`) plus our bundle. No Dart SDK, no source code.
FROM scratch
COPY --from=build /runtime/ /
COPY --from=build /out/ /
WORKDIR /app

# Config comes from env variables. The image has no .env file,
# so secrets stay out of it.
EXPOSE 3000
CMD ["/app/bin/server"]

Build and run it. The image has no .env file, so pass the config as environment variables. APP_KEY must be exactly 32 characters. The app does not start with a shorter or longer key.

docker build -t blog .
docker run -p 3000:3000 \
  -e APP_KEY=$(openssl rand -hex 16) \
  -e DB_CONNECTION=sqlite \
  -e DB_NAME=storage/blog.sqlite \
  blog

SQLite in Docker

The database file lives inside the container. It is lost when the container is removed. Mount a volume for it: -v blog-data:/app/storage. For a busy app, use Postgres or MySQL. See Database.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Deployment: HTTPS with a proxy, systemd, many machines.
  • Model: relationships and events.
  • Serializer: change the JSON shape of a response.
  • Authentication: all options of dox_auth.
  • OpenAPI: API docs from your routes and DTOs.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: What changed in each package, newest first. This page is made from the CHANGELOG.md files in the repo when the docs are built.

• New: package:dox_annotation/install.dart with Installer, the steps of a <package>:install command that dox add runs. writeFile (only when the file is not there), makeFolder, addEnv (to .env and .env.example, only when the key is missing), addEnvGetter (to AppEnv in lib/config/env.dart), addDependency (dart pub add, also dev), buildRunner, note (add your own summary line) and printSummary. lines is read only. Every step is safe to run twice. It is not in the dox_annotation.dart barrel.
  • New: DoxProvider.boot(). It runs once in every isolate after setup() of every provider is done. Optional, the default does nothing. dox_queue starts its in-process worker there, so the other providers (eg. the mail jobs) are ready first.
  • New: package:dox_annotation/provider.dart with DoxProvider. It moved here from dox_core, so a package below dox_core can have a provider. It is not in the dox_annotation.dart barrel.
  • New: package:dox_annotation/command.dart with Command and MigrationFile. They moved here from dox_core, so a package below dox_core can add dox commands.
  • New: GlobalMiddleware, a small shared list that packages use to add global middleware at startup. A package that does not depend on dox_core can use it. GlobalMiddleware.clear() is for tests.
• Version bump only, to match the other packages.
• Version bump only, to match the other packages.
• Version bump only, to match the other packages.

• New: id() on IAuth, so req.auth?.id() works. It gives the primary key of the logged-in user from the id() of the auth class (like Auth().id() of dox_auth), or null. It is an extension (IAuthHelpers), so a class that implements IAuth does not need to change. For a guest, req.auth is null.

• Removed: ICacheDriver and IStorageDriver. Nothing used them. For a cache driver, use CacheDriver from dox_cache.
  • Tests for IHttpException.toResponse().
• Version bump only, to match the other packages.
• The first stable release.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.5
docs.text:
• New timestamps option on @DoxModel. timestamps: false turns off created_at and updated_at, like $timestamps = false in Laravel. createdAt: null or updatedAt: null turns off one of them.
  • New primaryKeyType option on @DoxModel. Use primaryKeyType: String for a UUID key. The default is int.
  • Fix: IHttpException.toResponse() now returns {"code": errorCode, "message": message} for a text message, so the client gets the errorCode. A Map message is returned as it is.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.2
docs.text:
• Needs Dart 3.13 or newer.
  • All dependencies updated to their latest versions.
  • OpenAPI annotations, all optional: @Summary, @Description, @Tags, @Request, @Body, @Query, @Response, @ApiDeprecated, @ApiIgnore, @DoxController. Lower case names work too (@summary(...)), except @Response.
  • The DTO annotations (@Dto, @Length, @Email, ...) live in dox_validation. dox_core exports them.
  • IDoxRequest has no validate() and no processInputMapper() any more. Use a DTO.
  • Breaking (small): these names are exported by dox_core too. If a file also imports a package with a Request or Response class (like package:http) without a prefix, add a prefix to that import.
  • New @DoxEnv() and @EnvKey('X') for the typed env class.

docs.title: 3.0.0-alpha.1
docs.text:
• Version 3 of Dox. All Dox packages now share one version.
  • Needs Dart 3.6 or newer.
  • See the release notes for all main changes.

• New: the job builder moved here from dox_queue. It writes lib/generated/jobs.g.dart with every @Job() class, the same file as before. It runs only in an app that has dox_queue in dependencies or dev_dependencies. (When the build can not read the app's pubspec.yaml, it runs when the app can import dox_queue.) If your build.yaml names the builder dox_queue:jobs, change it to dox_builder:jobs.
  • Breaking: this dox_builder needs dox_queue 3.2 or newer. With dox_queue 3.1, both packages have a builder for jobs.g.dart, and build_runner stops at start with "outputs collide". Run dart pub upgrade to move both together. An app that must stay on dox_queue 3.1 turns off the new builder, and the dox_queue 3.1 builder keeps making the file: 
    # build.yaml of the app
targets:
  $default:
    builders:
      dox_builder:jobs:
        enabled: false
  • New: when the app can import dox_mailer, jobs.g.dart also lists the mail jobs of Mail.queue() (SendQueuedMail and SendEncryptedQueuedMail). So the worker can read them before Mail.configure() runs. The saved job names do not change. A dox_mailer without these classes (3.1) gets no mail lines.
  • Finds DoxProvider classes from dox_annotation. Release it together with dox_annotation and dox_core. An app must upgrade dox_builder together with dox_core, or its providers are not found.
  • New: the OpenAPI schema of a model reads visibleFields, like hidden: with a list, only its keys are in the schema. Needs the next dox_orm for toJson() to match.
  • New: onTrashed() counts as a model hook, so a model with only that hook gets hasModelHooks. Needs the next dox_orm.
  • New: models get $copyColumnsFrom(). It copies every column field from another model of the same class. refresh() in the next dox_orm uses it, so it works for columns with a cast or a beforeGet. Nothing else calls it, so reads and saves do no extra work.
  • New: models read @HasManyThrough and @HasOneThrough. Needs the next dox_orm.
  • New: DTOs read @Dto(trim: true), @Dto(coerce: true) and @Dto(attributes: {...}). Needs the next dox_validation.
  • New: @After and @Before take 'today', 'tomorrow', 'yesterday' and the input key of another DateTime field. New @AfterOrEqual and @BeforeOrEqual. A text that is not a date, a word or a DateTime field stops the build. The words and fields work with any dox_validation. @AfterOrEqual and @BeforeOrEqual need the next dox_validation.
  • New: DTOs read @RequiredUnless, @RequiredWithout, @RequiredWithoutAll, @Filled, @Present, @Prohibited, @ProhibitedIf, @ExcludeIf and @ExcludeUnless. Each one on an always-required field stops the build, like @RequiredIf. Needs the next dox_validation.
  • New: the rules @Different and the field compare rules check the whole field on a List field, not each item. Rules that name another key stop the build when they name a Dart field name in place of the input key.
  • A DTO that uses none of these gets the same code as before.
  • OpenAPI: a controller method that calls req.authorize(...) gets a 401 and a 403 answer in the docs. A @Response with the same status wins.
  • OpenAPI: a controller method that calls req.validateSchema(...), or req.validate<T>() with no request class found, gets a 422 answer. A @Response(422, ...) wins. Needs the next dox_core.
  • OpenAPI: a controller method that calls Gate.authorize(...) gets a 403 answer in the docs. A @Response(403, ...) wins.
  • DTOs: a DTO with no @RequiredIf or @RequiredWith field (and no nested DTO with one) now writes usesRequiredWhen => false. Then the check does not keep each converted value, which saves work. Needs the next dox_validation.
  • New: DTO code reads the DTO flags of ValidationFlags at run time: dtoAllErrors, dtoRejectEmptyList and dtoMaybeRejectsEmpty. All are off by default, so the checks work as before. The builder writes this code only when the app's dox_validation has DtoState.allErrors. With an older dox_validation it writes the old code, so it still compiles.
  • New: a model @BelongsTo field passes its name as relation: to belongsTo(), for the dox_orm flag belongsToKeyFromRelation. The builder writes it only when the app's dox_orm has the relation: parameter. With an older dox_orm the code does not change.
  • Fix: @OrDefault() on a Maybe<T> field no longer stops the build. A bad value gives Maybe.missing().
  • Fix: a nested DTO deeper in lists and maps, like List<List<A>> or Map<String, List<A>>, now runs its validate() and its async rules. Before, only one level (List<A>, Map<String, A>) was found. So after build_runner, an app may now get errors from these deeper DTOs that were skipped before.
• Version bump only, to match the other packages.
• DTOs: @Describe('...') on a field sets description in its JSON Schema (the generated toJsonSchema() and the OpenAPI docs). It wins over the /// doc comment. Needs dox_validation 3.1.2.

• DTOs: @Dto(emptyStringsToNull: true) makes the generated code read "" as null (needs the next dox_validation).
  • DTOs: @OrDefault() makes a bad value of that field give its default (or null) instead of an error. A field with @OrDefault() and no default that is not nullable stops the build.

• Fix: the JSON Schema pattern of @AlphaDash now allows digits, like the check does (needs dox_validation 3.1.0). The OpenAPI output of a DTO with @AlphaDash changes.
  • Fix: in generated DTO code, @RequiredIf and @RequiredWith now run after all fields are converted. Before, a rule on a field read the raw value of a field that comes after it, like ' PRO ', not 'pro' after @Trim and @Lowercase. Run build_runner to get the new code.
  • Fix: reload() and preload now set a nullable @HasOne, @BelongsTo, @MorphOne or @MorphTo field to null when the related row is gone. Before, the field kept its old value. Run build_runner to get the new code.
  • Fix: reload() and preload now set a @HasMany, @ManyToMany or @MorphMany field to an empty list when there are no related rows. Before, the field kept its old list. Run build_runner to get the new code.
  • Behavior change: a nullable list relation, like List<Tag>? tags, is now [] (not null) after a preload with no rows.
  • DTOs: @RequiredIf('type', 'company') and @RequiredWith(['phone']) from dox_validation. The field is required only when the condition is true. Use them on a nullable field, a Maybe field or a field with a default. On an always-required field the build stops with a clear error.
  • DTOs: the build stops when @RequiredIf, @RequiredWith, @Same or @Confirmed(other:) names a Dart field (like accountType) instead of its input key (account_type). The check would never match. It also stops for a @DateFormatted format with a letter it does not know.
  • DTOs: in a @Dto(strict: true) class, the key that @Confirmed reads (like password_confirmation) is not an unknown key.
  • New: DTO file rules @MinSize('10KB'), @MimeTypes(['image/png', 'image/*']) and @Dimensions(minWidth:, maxWidth:, minHeight:, maxHeight:, width:, height:, ratio:). They need dox_validation 3.1.0 or newer. A bad size or a @Dimensions() with no limit stops the build.
  • New: @ManyToMany(withPivot: [...], withTimestamps: true) is passed to the ORM, so the relation reads the extra pivot columns. Needs dox_orm 3.1.0 or newer.
  • New: the model builder makes the code for @MorphMany, @MorphOne and @MorphTo (polymorphic relations). A @MorphTo field has no model: its type is the field type, like Model<dynamic>, and its morph name is the field name in snake_case. The OpenAPI model schema has these relation keys too. Needs dox_orm 3.1.0 or newer.

• Breaking: column and JSON keys can change. Please read this before you update.
  • Digits are no longer split off. Before, address2 gave the key address_2. Now it gives address2.
  • A name you give is used exactly as written. Before, @Column(name: 'userID') gave user_i_d. Now it gives userID. The same is true for @Computed(name:), and for primaryKey, createdAt and updatedAt in @DoxModel.
  • DTO input keys change the same way: a field line2 now reads the key line2, not line_2.
  • What to do: run build_runner and look for changed keys in the generated files. Then rename the column in a migration. Or keep the old key with @Column(name: 'address_2') (or @Name('line_2') on a DTO field).
  • Fix: types from an import with a prefix (import 'other.dart' as o;) keep the prefix in the generated code, like o.Role, List<o.Role>, EnumCast(o.Role.values) and o.$InnerDto. Before, the code did not compile. This works in models, DTOs, env classes and scopes.
  • Fix: @Column(cast: ...) now works for a model in a part file. The cast is read from the AST of the field.
  • Fix: table names, column keys and relation keys are escaped in the generated code (\, ' and $).
  • Fix: a private class (like _AdminRouter or @Inject() class _Cache) is no longer put in container.g.dart, where it did not compile. The build shows a warning with the class and file.
  • Fix: container errors now show the file and line of the problem.
  • New: a constructor parameter of an abstract type gets the one container class that implements it. When two or more classes implement it, the build stops and names them.
  • Fix: the OpenAPI builder reads the files in path order, so openapi.g.dart does not change between builds.
  • Fix: the OpenAPI builder finds routes with a prefixed dox_core import, like dox.Route.get(...). Only the Route class of dox_core counts.
  • Fix: the OpenAPI builder stops with a clear error when two controllers, two @Security classes or two schema classes have the same name in two files. Before, one silently replaced the other. Dox finds them by name at runtime, so a new name would not match. Rename one of them.
  • Fix: OpenAPI annotations count only when they come from a Dox package (package:dox_...). An app class with the same name, like Summary, is no longer read as one.
  • Faster builds: the container, DTO list and OpenAPI builders skip .g.dart files. They also look at the text of a file first, and only resolve it when it can hold what they look for.

  • Change: the model, DTO and env builder runs on lib/ only by default. Before, it also ran on test/, bin/ and tool/. A package with models or DTOs in test/ adds this to its build.yaml:

    targets:
  $default:
    builders:
      dox_builder:
        generate_for: ["lib/**", "test/**"]
• Version bump only, to match the other packages.
• The first stable release.

docs.text: • lib/generated/dtos.g.dart is now written for every app, also with no @Dto. The list is empty then. So the app can always have dtos: dtos in AppConfig. An app here is a package that imports AppConfig (from dox_core). Other packages with no DTO still get no file. The empty list is final, not const, so dtos: dtos does not trigger the avoid_redundant_argument_values lint.
